definition_zh: 蜜蜂；蜂类（含不酿蜜的种类）；为作物传粉的蜂群；忙碌勤快的人；邻里一起干活或娱乐的聚会；拼写比赛；蜂产品（作定语）；热闹的集体活动
definition_en: a four-winged insect that lives in a colony, gathers nectar and pollen and makes honey; also used of hard-working people, communal work parties and spelling contests
core_image: 一朵花的开口处，一只蜜蜂把后腿的花粉筐装得鼓鼓的，转身朝蜂巢的六角门洞飞去
scene: 果园里，蜜蜂落在苹果花上，把后腿的花粉筐装得鼓鼓的。A bee gathers pollen from the apple blossom and carries it back to the hive.
sceneCN: 这里 bee 指「采集花蜜与花粉的蜂类昆虫」（第 1 个义项：四翅、营群体生活的蜜蜂）；句意为一只蜜蜂从苹果花上采集花粉，带回蜂巢。可辨识物件：苹果花、后腿花粉筐、蜂巢入口、成群飞回的同类。

pos.zh: 蜜蜂；蜂类；忙碌的人；（美）拼字比赛；邻里互助聚会

collocations.zh: 蜂王；也指团体中的女核心人物

senses.title: A four-winged colony insect
senses.titleCN: 蜜蜂：四翅、营群体生活的蜂类
senses.definition: a four-winged insect that lives in a colony, gathers nectar and pollen and makes honey
senses.definitionCN: 四翅、成群生活、采集花蜜与花粉并酿蜜的昆虫
senses.example: A bee gathers pollen from the apple blossom and carries it back to the hive.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蜜蜂从苹果花上采集花粉，带回蜂巢。
senses.why: The everyday sense names the insect itself; the older Germanic word simply meant the buzzing creature, and honey-making is its best-known habit.
senses.whyCN: 日常义就是这种昆虫本身；日耳曼语旧词只表示「嗡嗡叫的小东西」，酿蜜是它最出名的习性。

senses.title: Any member of the bee superfamily
senses.titleCN: 蜂总科的任一成员，包括不酿蜜的种类
senses.definition: any insect of the bee superfamily, including solitary species that do not make honey
senses.definitionCN: 蜂总科的任何昆虫，包括不酿蜜的独居种类
senses.example: Mining bees nest in bare soil and never build a honeycomb.
senses.exampleCN: 地蜂在裸露的土壤里筑巢，从不建蜜脾。
senses.why: Taxonomy widened the label: the family covers solitary as well as colonial species, so honey is not part of the definition.
senses.whyCN: 分类学把称呼放宽了：这一科既有独居种也有群居种，酿蜜并不构成定义的一部分。

senses.title: The insects that pollinate a crop
senses.titleCN: 为一地作物传粉的蜂群
senses.definition: bees treated collectively as the pollinators that a crop or a wild plant depends on
senses.definitionCN: 把蜂视为一个整体，指作物或野生植物所依赖的传粉者
senses.example: Without native bees, the almond orchards set far less fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 没有本地蜂群，杏园结出的果实会少得多。
senses.why: When farmers say the bees, they mean the pollinating work force rather than one insect, so the word shifts from a creature to a service.
senses.whyCN: 农人说的「蜂」指整支传粉劳力，而非某一只昆虫，词义便从个体转向一项服务。

senses.title: A busy, industrious person
senses.definition: a person who is always working, used with a hint of affectionate teasing
senses.definitionCN: 总在干活的人，带一点亲昵的打趣
senses.example: My neighbour is a busy bee, pruning hedges before breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 我那位邻居是个闲不住的忙人，早饭前就在修剪树篱。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the insect's tireless foraging and applies it to human energy, always with the fixed word busy.
senses.whyCN: 比喻借用蜜蜂不知疲倦的采集，转到人的精力上，且总与「busy」连用。

senses.title: A communal working party
senses.titleCN: 邻里一起干活的聚会（剥玉米会、缝被会）
senses.definition: a gathering of neighbours who work together on one task, such as husking corn or sewing a quilt
senses.definitionCN: 邻里聚在一起完成同一件活的场合，如剥玉米或缝被子
senses.example: The quilting bee finished three covers in a single afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 这场缝被聚会一个下午就做好了三床被面。
senses.why: Frontier life turned a solitary chore into a social event, and the insect's colony became the model for people working side by side.
senses.whyCN: 拓荒生活把独做的杂活变成社交场合，蜜蜂的群体便成了并排干活的样板。

senses.title: A spelling competition
senses.definition: a contest in which competitors take turns spelling words aloud until only one remains
senses.definitionCN: 参赛者轮流口头拼写单词、直到只剩一人的比赛
senses.example: She won the county spelling bee by spelling a hard word calmly.
senses.exampleCN: 她沉着地拼出一个难词，赢下了县里的拼写比赛。
senses.why: The contest borrowed the gathering sense of bee, a meeting for a shared activity, and kept only the insect name as a fossil.
senses.whyCN: 比赛借用了 bee 的「聚会」义，即为一件事聚在一起，只把昆虫名当作凝固的残迹留下。

senses.title: Hive products sold as food
senses.titleCN: 蜂产品（作定语，如蜂花粉）
senses.definition: honey and other hive products, sold under labels such as bee pollen or bee honey
senses.definitionCN: 蜂蜜及其他蜂巢产品，常以蜂花粉、蜂蜜之类的名称出售
senses.example: The farm sells bee pollen beside jars of honey.
senses.exampleCN: 农场在蜂蜜罐旁出售蜂花粉。
senses.why: Here bee works as a noun modifier naming the source of the product rather than the animal.
senses.whyCN: 此处 bee 作名词修饰语，指产品的来源，而非动物本身。

senses.title: A loud communal gathering
senses.titleCN: 热闹的集体活动（旧时乡村用法）
senses.definition: any lively gathering organized around a shared task or amusement, especially in older rural usage
senses.definitionCN: 围绕同一件事或娱乐而形成的热闹聚会，尤见于旧时乡村
senses.example: The barn raising turned into a bee that lasted until dark.
senses.exampleCN: 那场建仓互助会最后变成热闹的蜂会，一直闹到天黑。
senses.why: The older rural sense generalizes the work party into any crowded, buzzing occasion, and the noise of the hive supplies the image.
senses.whyCN: 旧时乡村义把互助干活扩展为任何拥挤喧闹的场合，蜂巢的嗡鸣提供了意象。

intro.en: Bee descends from Old English bēo, a Germanic word for the honeybee whose plural was bēon. Latin apis, the other great source of bee vocabulary, is not related to it.
intro.cn: bee 来自古英语 bēo，是日耳曼语中指蜜蜂的词，复数作 bēon。拉丁 apis 是另一条蜂类词汇的来源，与它并非同源。

items.en: Old English bēo named the honeybee, with the plural bēon; the modern plural bees was reshaped on the model of ordinary nouns.
items.cn: 古英语 bēo 指蜜蜂，复数作 bēon；现代复数 bees 是按普通名词的样式重塑的。

items.en: Old High German bīa, Old Norse bȳ and Gothic bī- point to a reconstructed Germanic form *bijō, which is a reconstruction rather than an attested word.
items.cn: 古高地德语 bīa、古北欧语 bȳ 与哥特语 bī- 指向重构的日耳曼语形式 *bijō，这是重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: A link between the word and a root meaning 'to buzz or tremble' has been suggested because of the insect's hum; the suggestion is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 有人因这种昆虫的嗡鸣，把该词与意为「嗡嗡作响、颤动」的词根联系起来；这只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Latin apis 'bee' survives in English only inside borrowed technical words such as apiary and apiculture, so it never replaced the everyday noun.
items.cn: 拉丁 apis「蜜蜂」只保留在 apiary、apiculture 这类借入的技术词里，从未取代日常名词。

items.en: From the eighteenth century, American rural usage called a communal work party a bee, and the same pattern later produced the spelling bee.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，美国乡村用法把邻里互助干活称作 bee，同一模式后来又造出拼写比赛一词。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the deeper origin and the exact first citation are not settled, so any pre-Latin form offered here is a reconstruction and competing hypotheses are left side by side.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：更深的来源与确切最早书证均无定论，此处给出的拉丁语之前形式属重构形式，并列假说一并保留、不作定论。

note.en: Group one gathers words that are close in sound or spelling but come from other roots; group two gathers the insects most often compared with bees.
note.cn: 第一组收同音或形近但来源不同的词；第二组收最常与蜜蜂相比的昆虫。

entries.definition: The verb be is a grammatical word with no connection to the insect; the shared sound is accident, not kinship.
entries.definitionCN: 动词 be 是语法词，与这种昆虫无关；同音只是巧合，并非同源。

entries.definition: Been is the past participle of be, close in sound but built from a completely different grammatical stock.
entries.definitionCN: been 是 be 的过去分词，读音相近，却来自完全不同的语法系统。

entries.definition: Bean names a seed of the legume family; the identical sound hides an unrelated history.
entries.definitionCN: bean 指豆科植物的种子；完全相同的读音掩盖着互不相干的历史。

entries.definition: A beetle is a different order of insect with hardened wing covers; the spelling overlap is misleading.
entries.definitionCN: 甲虫属于另一个目，翅鞘坚硬；拼写上的重合具有误导性。

entries.definition: A wasp has a slender waist and a stinger and is not a bee, though both belong to the same broad order.
entries.definitionCN: 黄蜂腰细、有蜇针，不是蜜蜂，尽管两者同属一个较大的目。

entries.definition: Honeybee names the species kept for honey, the closest everyday relative of bee.
entries.definitionCN: honeybee 指为取蜜而饲养的种类，是 bee 在日常用语中最贴近的同族词。

entries.definition: A bumblebee is a big, densely hairy bee that nests in small colonies underground.
entries.definitionCN: 熊蜂是体型大、绒毛密的蜂，在地下筑小群体巢。

entries.definition: A hornet is a large social wasp whose sting is feared; it is a wasp, not a bee.
entries.definitionCN: 胡蜂是体大的社会性黄蜂，蜇人厉害；它属黄蜂，不是蜜蜂。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Germanic root gives the everyday noun, the compounds and the collective plural bees.
normal.cn: 日耳曼词根给出日常名词、复合词与集合复数 bees。

normal.en: The family runs bee, beehive, beekeeper, beeswax, honeybee, bumblebee and beeline.
normal.cn: 词族包括 bee、beehive、beekeeper、beeswax、honeybee、bumblebee 与 beeline。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: queen bee, worker bee, spelling bee, bee pollen.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：蜂王、工蜂、拼写比赛、蜂花粉。

normal.en: Busy as a bee is the standard simile for tireless work.
normal.cn: 忙得像蜜蜂是形容不知疲倦的固定比喻。

normal.en: A colony has three castes: queen, workers and drones.
normal.cn: 蜂群有三个等级：蜂王、工蜂与雄蜂。

abstract.en: Picture a city built entirely of hexagonal rooms, each holding one sleeping larva.
abstract.cn: 想象一座全由六角房间构成的城，每间里睡着一只幼虫。

abstract.en: Picture pollen as yellow luggage strapped to a traveller's legs.
abstract.cn: 想象花粉是绑在旅人腿上的黄色行李。

abstract.en: Picture a hall of voices taking turns, each voice spelling one word.
abstract.cn: 想象一间大厅，声音轮流响起，每个声音拼出一个词。

examples.en: Wild bees pollinate most of the orchard before the honeybee hives arrive.
examples.cn: 在蜜蜂箱运来之前，野生蜂群已经为果园完成了大部分传粉。

examples.en: The children's spelling bee ended in a tie after forty rounds.
examples.cn: 儿童拼写比赛经过四十轮后以平局收场。

examples.en: She keeps two hives and sells bee pollen at the weekend market.
examples.cn: 她养了两箱蜂，周末市场上卖蜂花粉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「bee（必）」——必到花前去采蜜的小虫 → 蜜蜂；bee 又指大家聚在一起的「蜂会」

root: 古英语 bēo「蜜蜂」；日耳曼语同源词指向重构形式 *bijō；更早的印欧来源不确定，拟声假说（嗡嗡声）未获证实。拉丁 apis 与英语 bee 不是同源词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one insect: a forager loads pollen, returns to a colony, is imitated as a model of hard work, and finally lends its name to communal gatherings and a spelling contest.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一只昆虫展开：采粉者装满花粉、回到群体，被当作勤劳的样板，最后把名字借给了邻里聚会与拼写比赛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a forager leaving a flower with full pollen baskets and heading for a hexagonal hive door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只采粉者带着装满花粉的后腿，从花朵飞向六角形的蜂巢门洞。

branches.en: NECTAR AND POLLEN: the insect body itself, and the whole family of such insects.
branches.cn: 花蜜与花粉：昆虫本体，以及这一整类昆虫。

branches.en: POLLINATION SERVICE: the colony read as unpaid labour in the orchard.
branches.cn: 传粉服务：把蜂群读作果园里的无偿劳力。

branches.en: COMMUNAL LABOUR: human diligence and the neighbour work party borrow the hive's example.
branches.cn: 集体劳动：人的勤勉与邻里互助都借用了蜂巢的样板。

branches.en: HIVE PRODUCTS: the name attaches to what the hive yields, not to the animal.
branches.cn: 蜂巢产物：名字附着在蜂巢的产出上，而非动物本身。

branches.en: BUZZING CROWD: any crowded gathering inherits the hum of the hive.
branches.cn: 嗡鸣的人群：任何拥挤的场合都继承了蜂巢的嗡鸣。

intro.en: Bee is a bare Germanic root; the derived words are English compounds and suffixes attached to it, plus a Latin family borrowed for technical use.
intro.cn: bee 是光秃秃的日耳曼词根；派生词是英语复合与缀合，另有借入技术领域的拉丁词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin apis and its diminutive apicula supply apiary, apiculture and apiarist, none of them cognate with English bee.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 apis 及其指小形式 apicula 衍生出 apiary、apiculture、apiarist，与英语 bee 并不同源。

items.example: A bee works the clover row by row.
items.exampleCN: 一只蜜蜂一行行地采三叶草。

items.example: The honeybee is the most managed pollinator.
items.exampleCN: 蜜蜂是最常被管理的传粉者。

items.example: Smoke calms the beehive before inspection.
items.exampleCN: 检查前先熏烟让蜂群安静。

items.example: The beekeeper moved the hives uphill.
items.exampleCN: 养蜂人把蜂箱移到了高处。

items.example: Beeswax seals the cells of the comb.
items.exampleCN: 蜂蜡封住巢房的孔口。

items.example: A bumblebee queened the nest under the shed.
items.exampleCN: 一只熊蜂在棚下建起了群体。

items.example: She made a beeline for the exit.
items.exampleCN: 她径直朝出口走去。

items.example: He entered the spelling bee at nine.
items.exampleCN: 他九岁参加了拼写比赛。

items.example: Bee pollen is sold as a food supplement.
items.exampleCN: 蜂花粉被当作膳食补充剂出售。

definition_zh: 黄蜂；胡蜂（细腰、有蜇针的膜翅目昆虫）；纸巢蜂；寄生蜂；无花果小蜂；黄蜂腰（束腰）；脾气尖刻的人；蜂蜇式的刺痛
definition_en: a slender-waisted stinging insect of the order Hymenoptera, including social paper wasps and solitary parasitic kinds; also used of a thin waist or a sharp temper
core_image: 屋檐下倒悬一只灰白色的纸巢，一只细腰黄蜂停在巢口，翅膀收拢成一条窄线
scene: 屋檐下的纸巢边缘，一只细腰黄蜂收紧翅膀停住。A wasp settles on the rim of the paper nest under the eaves.
sceneCN: 这里 wasp 指「细腰、有蜇针的膜翅目昆虫」（第 1 个义项：黄蜂这种昆虫）；句意为一只黄蜂停在屋檐下纸巢的边缘。可辨识物件：倒悬的纸巢、六角巢房、细腰、收拢的翅膀。

pos.zh: 黄蜂；胡蜂；脾气尖刻的人；黄蜂腰

senses.title: A slender-waisted stinging insect
senses.titleCN: 黄蜂：细腰、带蜇针的昆虫
senses.definition: a stinging insect with a narrow waist between thorax and abdomen, usually banded in yellow and black
senses.definitionCN: 胸腹之间有细腰、常带黄黑条纹的蜇人昆虫
senses.example: A wasp settles on the rim of the paper nest under the eaves.
senses.exampleCN: 一只黄蜂停在屋檐下纸巢的边缘。
senses.why: The core sense rests on two visible marks: the pinched waist and the sting, which separate wasps from bees in ordinary speech.
senses.whyCN: 核心义靠两个可见特征站住：掐细的腰与蜇针，日常说法靠这两点把黄蜂与蜜蜂分开。

senses.title: A social paper-nest builder
senses.definition: a social wasp that chews wood fibre into a grey paper nest with hexagonal cells
senses.definitionCN: 把木纤维嚼成灰色纸巢、巢内有六角巢房的社会性黄蜂
senses.example: Paper wasps raise their brood in a comb hung from a single stalk.
senses.exampleCN: 纸巢蜂把幼虫养在由一根短柄悬挂的巢脾里。
senses.why: The paper nest is the clearest everyday sign of this sense, because the material looks like grey cardboard.
senses.whyCN: 纸巢是这一义最直观的标志，因为材料看上去就像灰色硬纸板。

senses.title: A solitary hunting wasp
senses.definition: a solitary wasp that hunts insects or spiders and stocks a nest cell with them for its larva
senses.definitionCN: 单独捕猎昆虫或蜘蛛、把猎物储进巢房供幼虫食用的黄蜂
senses.example: The digger wasp paralyses a caterpillar and drags it into a burrow.
senses.exampleCN: 掘土蜂把一条毛虫麻痹后拖进地穴。
senses.why: Many wasps are not social at all; the hunting habit, not the nest, defines this group.
senses.whyCN: 许多黄蜂根本不成群；界定这一组的是捕猎习性，而非巢。

senses.title: A parasitic wasp used in pest control
senses.titleCN: 用于害虫防治的寄生蜂
senses.definition: a small wasp that lays its eggs inside or on another insect, killing the host as the larva grows
senses.definitionCN: 把卵产在另一昆虫体内或体表、幼虫成长时杀死寄主的小型黄蜂
senses.example: Farmers release a parasitic wasp that targets aphids.
senses.exampleCN: 农民释放一种专门寄生蚜虫的寄生蜂。
senses.why: Agriculture turned the parasitic habit into a service, so the word now names a biological control agent.
senses.whyCN: 农业把寄生习性变成一项服务，这个词因此也指生物防治手段。

senses.title: A fig-pollinating wasp
senses.definition: a tiny wasp that enters a fig and both pollinates the flowers and lays its eggs there
senses.definitionCN: 进入无花果内部、既为花传粉又产卵的小型黄蜂
senses.example: Each fig species depends on its own pollinating wasp.
senses.exampleCN: 每一种无花果都依赖各自专属的传粉小蜂。
senses.why: This sense is a precise partnership: the insect's life cycle and the fruit's seed set are locked together.
senses.whyCN: 这一义是一种精确的共生：昆虫的生命周期与果实的结籽彼此锁定。

senses.title: A very thin waist
senses.definition: a waist so narrow that it looks pinched, named after the insect's body
senses.definitionCN: 细得像被掐住一样的腰，因这种昆虫的体形得名
senses.example: The dress was cut to give a wasp waist above a full skirt.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裙子裁成上收的黄蜂腰，下接宽裙摆。
senses.why: The metaphor works by shape alone: the insect's waist is the standard image of an exaggerated cinch.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻只靠形状成立：黄蜂的腰就是「勒得极细」的标准图像。

senses.title: A sharp-tongued person
senses.definition: a person whose remarks sting, described as waspish rather than bee-like
senses.definitionCN: 言语像蜇人一样刺痛别人的人，用「waspish」而非像蜜蜂那样形容
senses.example: Her waspish reply ended the argument at once.
senses.exampleCN: 她尖刻的回应立刻终止了争论。
senses.why: The sting supplies the metaphor: honey is sweet, but this insect only stings, so the adjective marks a biting manner.
senses.whyCN: 蜇针提供了比喻：蜜是甜的，而这种昆虫只会蜇人，形容词因此标出刺人的态度。

senses.title: A painful stinging encounter
senses.definition: the sting of a wasp treated as a memorable event, as in a wasp sting on the arm
senses.definitionCN: 把被黄蜂蜇到当作一件难忘的事，如手臂上的黄蜂蜇伤
senses.example: A wasp sting swelled his wrist for two days.
senses.exampleCN: 一处黄蜂蜇伤让他的手腕肿了两天。
senses.why: Here the insect name works as a modifier on the injury, a common pattern in medical and everyday description.
senses.whyCN: 此处昆虫名作伤情的修饰语，是医学与日常描述中常见的模式。

intro.en: Wasp comes from Old English wæsp, wæps, a Germanic word for the stinging insect. Latin vespa is a distant cousin in form and meaning but not the source of the English word.
intro.cn: wasp 来自古英语 wæsp、wæps，是日耳曼语中指这种蜇人昆虫的词。拉丁 vespa 在形义上都相近，却不是英语这个词的来源。

items.en: Old English wæsp and wæps both occur; the modern spelling settled on wasp, with the s and p kept in that order.
items.cn: 古英语中 wæsp 与 wæps 两种写法都出现；现代拼写定为 wasp，s 与 p 保持这一顺序。

items.en: Dutch wesp and German Wespe belong with the English word to a Germanic group, reconstructed as *wapsu or *wabswō; the exact shape is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 荷兰语 wesp、德语 Wespe 与英语词同属一个日耳曼词组，重构为 *wapsu 或 *wabswō；确切形式属重构。

items.en: Latin vespa 'wasp' and English wasp look alike and mean the same thing, but each descends through its own branch; the similarity reflects a shared older source, not borrowing.
items.cn: 拉丁 vespa「黄蜂」与英语 wasp 形似义同，却各自沿不同分支传下；相似反映更早的共同来源，而非借词。

items.en: A link to a root meaning 'weave' has been proposed because paper wasps build comb from chewed fibre; this remains a hypothesis about the older root.
items.cn: 有人因纸巢蜂用嚼碎的纤维筑巢，提出该词与意为「编织」的词根有关；这仍只是关于更早词根的假说。

items.en: From the seventeenth century waspish described a stinging manner of speech, and later the wasp waist named a tightly cinched shape.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起 waspish 形容刺人的说话方式，后来黄蜂腰又指勒得极细的体形。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the deeper origin and the exact first citation are not settled, so any pre-Latin form offered here is a reconstruction and competing hypotheses are left side by side.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：更深的来源与确切最早书证均无定论，此处给出的拉丁语之前形式属重构形式，并列假说一并保留、不作定论。

note.en: Group one sets out words that share letters with wasp but have nothing to do with the insect; group two lists the stinging insects people confuse it with.
note.cn: 第一组列出与 wasp 共享字母、却与昆虫无关的词；第二组列出人们常与之混淆的蜇人昆虫。

entries.definition: A wisp is a thin strand of hair or smoke; the shared letters are pure coincidence.
entries.definitionCN: wisp 指一缕头发或烟；共享的字母纯属巧合。

entries.definition: Rasp means to scrape or speak harshly and has no insect sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: rasp 意为刮擦或声音刺耳，完全没有昆虫义。

entries.definition: Gasp is a breathing verb; only the final letters overlap.
entries.definitionCN: gasp 是呼吸动词，仅末尾字母相同。

entries.definition: Warp comes from a weaving term meaning to twist, a different root despite the near-identical sound.
entries.definitionCN: warp 来自织造术语，意为扭曲，读音几乎相同但词根不同。

entries.definition: A bee is a fuzzy pollen collector that makes honey; a wasp is smooth, hunts or parasitises and does not make honey.
entries.definitionCN: 蜜蜂毛茸、采集花粉并酿蜜；黄蜂体表光滑、捕猎或寄生，不酿蜜。

entries.definition: A hornet is a large social wasp, so it is a kind of wasp rather than a separate thing.
entries.definitionCN: 胡蜂是体大的社会性黄蜂，因此是黄蜂的一种，而非另一类。

entries.definition: Yellow jacket is the American name for a small aggressive social wasp that nests in the ground.
entries.definitionCN: yellow jacket 是美式说法，指体小、攻击性强、在地下筑巢的社会性黄蜂。

entries.definition: A bumblebee is a large hairy bee that pollinates; its sting is mild compared with a wasp's.
entries.definitionCN: 熊蜂是体大、多毛的传粉蜂，蜇痛远轻于黄蜂。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Germanic root wæsp gives the noun, the plural wasps and the adjective waspish.
normal.cn: 日耳曼词根 wæsp 给出名词、复数 wasps 与形容词 waspish。

normal.en: The family runs wasp, waspish, waspishly, waspishness and waspie.
normal.cn: 词族包括 wasp、waspish、waspishly、waspishness 与 waspie。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: paper wasp, solitary wasp, wasp waist, wasp sting.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：纸巢蜂、独居黄蜂、黄蜂腰、黄蜂蜇伤。

normal.en: Latin vespa looks like the English word but is a separate branch, not its source.
normal.cn: 拉丁 vespa 形似英语词，却是另一支，并非其来源。

normal.en: The narrowed waist is the quickest way to tell a wasp from a bee.
normal.cn: 掐细的腰是区分黄蜂与蜜蜂最快的办法。

abstract.en: Picture a grey paper city hanging from one stalk, each cell a nursery.
abstract.cn: 想象一座灰纸做的城挂在单根细柄上，每个小格都是育儿室。

abstract.en: Picture a waist pulled so tight that the body looks divided in two.
abstract.cn: 想象腰被勒得极紧，身体看上去分成两截。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence that leaves a red mark wherever it lands.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话落到哪里，就在哪里留下红痕。

examples.en: A single paper wasp can build a nest the size of a fist in one summer.
examples.cn: 一只纸巢蜂一个夏天就能造出拳头大的巢。

examples.en: The parasitic wasp lays one egg in each aphid, and the larva eats it from inside.
examples.cn: 寄生蜂在每只蚜虫体内产一枚卵，幼虫从内部把它吃掉。

examples.en: His waspish comment about the plan silenced the whole room.
examples.cn: 他对该方案尖刻的评论让全场沉默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「wasp（瓦斯扑）」——带着刺、脾气像瓦斯一样冲的细腰虫 → 黄蜂

root: 古英语 wæsp / wæps「黄蜂」；与荷兰语 wesp、德语 Wespe 同出日耳曼语，重构形式 *wapsu / *wabswō（重构形式）。拉丁 vespa 属另一分支，非英语词来源；「编织」词根联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the insect's body to its nests, its hunting and parasitic habits, and then to human shapes and tempers that the sting supplies.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从昆虫的身体移到它的巢、捕猎与寄生习性，再转到蜇针所供给的人体形状与脾气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow-waisted body with a sting at the tip, hanging beside a grey paper comb.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具细腰的躯体，末端带蜇针，悬在灰色纸巢旁。

branches.en: BODY SHAPE: the pinched waist belongs to the insect and to the dress cut after it.
branches.cn: 体形：掐细的腰既属昆虫，也属仿它裁剪的衣裙。

branches.en: NEST AND STING: the paper comb and the injury are the two facts people meet first.
branches.cn: 巢与蜇：纸巢与伤处是人最先遇到的两件事。

branches.en: HUNTING WAYS: solitary hunters and parasitic kinds show how varied the family is.
branches.cn: 捕猎方式：独居猎手与寄生种类显示这一科的多样。

branches.en: FIG PARTNERSHIP: one fig, one wasp, a locked life cycle.
branches.cn: 无花果共生：一种果、一种蜂，生命周期彼此锁定。

branches.en: SHARP TONGUE: the sting becomes a metaphor for speech that wounds.
branches.cn: 尖刻的舌头：蜇针变成伤人言语的比喻。

intro.en: Wasp is a Germanic root with only a few English derivatives; the technical vocabulary around it is mostly formed from Latin and Greek elements.
intro.cn: wasp 是日耳曼词根，英语派生词很少；围绕它的技术词汇多由拉丁与希腊成分构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin vespa gives vespid and vespiary in zoology, but these are learned borrowings, not relatives of the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vespa 在动物学中衍生出 vespid 与 vespiary，但那是学术借词，并非英语名词的同族。

items.example: A wasp patrols the eaves each summer.
items.exampleCN: 每年夏天都有黄蜂在屋檐巡飞。

items.example: He answered in a waspish tone.
items.exampleCN: 他用尖刻的语气回答。

items.example: She remarked waspishly that the plan was late.
items.exampleCN: 她尖刻地说这个方案来晚了。

items.example: His waspishness cost him two friends.
items.exampleCN: 他的尖刻让他失去了两个朋友。

items.example: The jacket is cut with a wasp waist.
items.exampleCN: 这件外套裁成黄蜂腰。

items.example: The dancer wore a waspie under the gown.
items.exampleCN: 舞者在长裙下穿了束腰。

items.meaning: a wasp that builds paper comb
items.example: A paper wasp founded her colony on the porch.
items.exampleCN: 一只纸巢蜂在门廊建起了群体。

items.meaning: a wasp that lives on a host
items.example: The parasitic wasp controls the moth population.
items.exampleCN: 寄生蜂控制着蛾的数量。

items.example: The wasp beetle's bands imitate a stinging insect.
items.exampleCN: 蜂形天牛的色带模仿蜇人的昆虫。

definition_zh: 蚊子；蚊虫滋扰；蚊媒疾病的传播者；蚊的幼虫（作定语）；蚊帐等防蚊用品（作定语）；小型舰艇编队（蚊队）；蚊叮的小伤；被当作猎物的小飞虫（如蚊鹰）
definition_en: a small two-winged fly whose female bites and sucks blood, often carrying disease; also used of the nuisance, the diseases it spreads and small craft fleets
core_image: 水面上倒立着一只细腿小虫，口器像一根细针，背后是静止的池水与一圈涟漪
scene: 池塘边，一只蚊子把细长的口器刺进人的前臂。A mosquito pierces the skin of a sleeper's forearm with its needle-like mouthparts.
sceneCN: 这里 mosquito 指「吸血的小型双翅目昆虫」（第 1 个义项：蚊）；句意为一只蚊子用针状口器刺入睡者前臂的皮肤。可辨识物件：细长口器、透明翅膀、前臂、池水。

senses.title: A small blood-sucking fly
senses.titleCN: 蚊子：吸血的小型双翅目昆虫
senses.definition: a small two-winged fly whose female pierces skin and takes blood
senses.definitionCN: 雌虫刺穿皮肤吸血的细小双翅目昆虫
senses.example: A mosquito pierces the skin of a sleeper's forearm with its needle-like mouthparts.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蚊子用针状口器刺入睡者前臂的皮肤。
senses.why: Only the female bites, because she needs blood protein for her eggs; the everyday word still names the whole insect.
senses.whyCN: 只有雌虫叮咬，因为它需要血液中的蛋白质来产卵；日常用词仍指整个虫体。

senses.title: A biting nuisance
senses.definition: mosquitoes treated collectively as an irritating swarm that drives people indoors
senses.definitionCN: 把蚊虫看成一群扰人的飞虫，能把人赶进屋里
senses.example: The mosquitoes drove the whole camp indoors before dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊群还没到黄昏就把整个营地的人赶进了屋。
senses.why: When the plural is used this way, the word names an annoyance rather than a species.
senses.whyCN: 复数这样用时，词指的是扰人的麻烦，而不是某个物种。

senses.title: A disease vector
senses.definition: the insect understood as the carrier that passes malaria, dengue or other infections between people
senses.definitionCN: 被理解为在人与人之间传递疟疾、登革热等感染的媒介昆虫
senses.example: Mosquitoes carry malaria in lowland regions.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊子在低地地区传播疟疾。
senses.why: Public health shifted the emphasis from the bite to the transmission chain, and this sense now dominates medical writing.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生把重点从叮咬转到传播链，这一义如今在医学写作中占主导。

senses.title: The aquatic young stage
senses.definition: the larval form that hangs at the water surface, usually named in the compound mosquito larva
senses.definitionCN: 倒悬在水面的幼虫，通常以「mosquito larva」这一复合形式出现
senses.example: Mosquito larvae hang head-down just beneath the surface film.
senses.exampleCN: 孑孓头朝下挂在表面水膜之下。
senses.why: The adult name is reused as a modifier for its own young, a common pattern in entomology.
senses.whyCN: 成虫名被复用作自身幼期的修饰语，这是昆虫学中常见的模式。

senses.title: Protective gear against mosquitoes
senses.definition: the equipment named after the insect, such as a mosquito net, coil or repellent
senses.definitionCN: 以这种昆虫命名的防护用品，如蚊帐、蚊香或驱蚊剂
senses.example: A mosquito net over the bed is the cheapest protection.
senses.exampleCN: 床上挂一顶蚊帐是最便宜的防护。
senses.why: The word marks what the object is used against, so the insect name becomes a label for the defence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出物件用来对付什么，昆虫名于是成了防护手段的标签。

senses.title: A fleet of small craft
senses.definition: a group of tiny, fast boats or warships, historically called a mosquito fleet
senses.definitionCN: 一群小而快的船或军舰，历史上称作蚊队
senses.example: A mosquito fleet of wooden gunboats patrolled the river.
senses.exampleCN: 一支由木制炮艇组成的蚊队巡弋河面。
senses.why: The metaphor compares small, numerous, stinging craft to a swarm of biting insects.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把数量多、体量小、能刺痛人的舰艇比作一群叮人的虫。

senses.title: A small irritating wound
senses.definition: the itchy swelling left by a bite, commonly called a mosquito bite
senses.definitionCN: 叮咬留下的发痒肿块，通常说成「mosquito bite」
senses.example: A mosquito bite on his ankle kept him awake.
senses.exampleCN: 脚踝上的蚊叮让他一夜没睡好。
senses.why: Metonymy moves the name from the biter to the mark it leaves, a very common shift in medical everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把名字从叮咬者移到留下的痕迹，这是医学口语中极常见的转移。

senses.title: A tiny flying prey
senses.titleCN: 被当作猎物的小飞虫（如蚊鹰）
senses.definition: a small flying insect understood as food for a predator, as in the folk name mosquito hawk
senses.definitionCN: 被看作捕食者食物的小飞虫，如俗称蚊鹰的蜻蜓
senses.example: Children call the dragonfly a mosquito hawk because it catches small flies.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把蜻蜓叫作蚊鹰，因为它捕食小飞虫。
senses.why: Here mosquito names the prey, and the compound tells what the larger insect feeds on.
senses.whyCN: 此处 mosquito 指猎物，复合词说明那种更大的昆虫吃什么。

intro.en: Mosquito is a Spanish and Portuguese diminutive of mosca 'fly', from Latin musca. English borrowed it in the sixteenth century during exploration of the Americas.
intro.cn: mosquito 是西班牙语与葡萄牙语中 mosca「苍蝇」的指小形式，源自拉丁 musca。英语在 16 世纪探索美洲期间把它借入。

items.en: Latin musca meant 'fly'; its own deeper origin is not settled, and the Indo-European forms sometimes cited for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 拉丁 musca 意为「苍蝇」；它更深的来源并无定论，偶尔为其引用的印欧形式属重构。

items.en: Spanish and Portuguese added the diminutive suffix -ito to mosca, giving mosquito 'little fly', the form English borrowed.
items.cn: 西班牙语与葡萄牙语给 mosca 加上指小后缀 -ito，构成 mosquito「小苍蝇」，英语借的就是这一形式。

items.en: English recorded mosquito in the late sixteenth century in travel accounts of the Caribbean and South America.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪后期的加勒比与南美游记中记录了 mosquito。

items.en: After the discovery that the insect transmits malaria and yellow fever, the word moved into public health vocabulary in the late nineteenth century.
items.cn: 在发现这种昆虫传播疟疾与黄热病之后，这个词于 19 世纪后期进入公共卫生词汇。

items.en: Both mosquitoes and mosquitos are accepted plurals; the longer form follows the older English habit of doubling the final consonant before -es.
items.cn: mosquitoes 与 mosquitos 两种复数都被接受；较长的一种沿用英语在 -es 前双写末尾辅音的老习惯。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the deeper origin and the exact first citation are not settled, so any pre-Latin form offered here is a reconstruction and competing hypotheses are left side by side.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：更深的来源与确切最早书证均无定论，此处给出的拉丁语之前形式属重构形式，并列假说一并保留、不作定论。

note.en: Group one collects words that look or sound close but come from other roots; group two collects the small biting flies people mix up with mosquitoes.
note.cn: 第一组收形近音近但来源不同的词；第二组收人们常与蚊子混淆的小型叮咬蝇类。

entries.definition: Mosque comes from Arabic masjid, a place of prostration; the resemblance to mosquito is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: mosque 来自阿拉伯语 masjid，意为叩拜之处；与 mosquito 的相似纯属偶然。

entries.definition: Miskito names a people and a coast of Central America and is spelled with a k; it is not the insect.
entries.definitionCN: Miskito 指中美洲的一个民族与一片海岸，拼写带 k，不是这种昆虫。

entries.definition: This plural is a spelling variant of mosquitoes, not a different word with a different meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 这个复数只是 mosquitoes 的拼写变体，并非意义不同的另一个词。

entries.definition: The compound names the bed net, so the insect word is working as a modifier rather than as the subject.
entries.definitionCN: 这个复合词指床上用的蚊帐，昆虫词在此作修饰语而非主语。

entries.definition: A gnat is a very small biting fly, often a midge; it bites but does not transmit malaria.
entries.definitionCN: gnat 指极小的叮咬蝇，常为蠓；会叮人但不传播疟疾。

entries.definition: A midge is a minute two-winged fly, some species of which bite in swarms near water.
entries.definitionCN: midge 是极小的双翅目蝇，有些种类在水边成群叮人。

entries.definition: Fly is the general name for the order, of which the mosquito is one family.
entries.definitionCN: fly 是这一目的通称，蚊子只是其中一科。

entries.definition: A flea is a wingless jumping insect that bites; it belongs to a different order entirely.
entries.definitionCN: flea 是无翅跳跃的叮咬昆虫，属于完全不同的目。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Spanish mosca 'fly' plus the diminutive -ito gives mosquito, literally 'little fly'.
normal.cn: 西班牙语 mosca「苍蝇」加指小后缀 -ito 构成 mosquito，字面就是「小苍蝇」。

normal.en: The family runs mosquito, mosquitoes, mosquitos, mosquitofish and mosquitocide.
normal.cn: 词族包括 mosquito、mosquitoes、mosquitos、mosquitofish 与 mosquitocide。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: mosquito net, mosquito coil, mosquito-borne disease.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：蚊帐、蚊香、蚊媒疾病。

normal.en: Only the female bites; males feed on nectar.
normal.cn: 只有雌虫叮咬，雄虫吸食花蜜。

normal.en: The larval stage is the wriggler that hangs at the water surface.
normal.cn: 幼虫期就是倒悬在水面的孑孓。

abstract.en: Picture a needle so fine that the sleeper never feels it enter.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细到睡者完全察觉不到的针。

abstract.en: Picture a whole village sleeping under white gauze, one net per bed.
abstract.cn: 想象整个村子睡在白纱之下，每张床一顶帐。

abstract.en: Picture a hundred small boats stinging a harbour like a swarm.
abstract.cn: 想象上百条小船像虫群一样刺痛一座港口。

examples.en: The mosquito net was treated with insecticide and hung over both beds.
examples.cn: 蚊帐经杀虫剂处理，挂在两张床的上方。

examples.en: Mosquitoes breeding in standing water made the drainage project urgent.
examples.cn: 蚊子在积水中繁殖，使排水工程变得紧迫。

examples.en: A mosquito bite on her wrist swelled into a hard red lump.
examples.cn: 她手腕上的蚊叮肿成了一个硬红的包。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mosquito（莫斯基托）」——在池边「莫」名其妙被叮一口的小虫 → 蚊子

root: 西班牙语/葡萄牙语 mosquito「小苍蝇」= mosca「苍蝇」+ 指小后缀 -ito；mosca 源自拉丁 musca「苍蝇」。拉丁 musca 更早来源不确定，所引印欧形式属重构形式。与 mosque（阿拉伯语 masjid）无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from the biting insect, spread to the swarm, the disease chain, its water-borne young, the gear used against it, small warships, the mark it leaves and the prey it becomes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从叮人的昆虫出发，扩展到虫群、疾病链、水中幼期、对付它的器物、小型舰艇、留下的包以及它作为猎物的一面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle-thin mouthpart breaking the skin while a gauze net hangs above the bed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细如针的口器刺破皮肤，床的上方挂着纱帐。

branches.en: THE BITE: the insect and the itchy mark it leaves are two ends of one act.
branches.cn: 叮咬：昆虫与它留下的痒包是同一动作的两端。

branches.en: THE SWARM: the nuisance and the wriggling young both present the insect in numbers.
branches.cn: 虫群：扰人的成蚊与扭动的幼虫都以数量呈现这种昆虫。

branches.en: TRANSMISSION: the bite becomes a link in a chain between patients.
branches.cn: 传播：叮咬成为病人之间链条上的一环。

branches.en: DEFENCE AND METAPHOR: nets and coils answer the bite, and small fast boats borrow it.
branches.cn: 防护与比喻：蚊帐蚊香回应叮咬，小而快的船借用了它。

branches.en: THE PREY: the name finally marks a food item for a larger hunter.
branches.cn: 猎物：名字最后标出一种更大捕食者的食物。

intro.en: Mosquito is a Spanish diminutive built on a Latin root; its English derivatives are compounds, while the Latin family supplies the technical terms.
intro.cn: mosquito 是在拉丁词根上构成的西班牙语指小词；英语派生词多为复合，技术术语则来自拉丁词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin musca 'fly' gives muscid and musciform in zoology; the Spanish diminutive is the branch that produced the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 musca「苍蝇」在动物学中给出 muscid 与 musciform；产生英语名词的是西班牙语指小这一支。

items.example: A mosquito rests on the shaded wall.
items.exampleCN: 一只蚊子在背阴的墙上停歇。

items.example: Mosquitoes breed wherever water stands.
items.exampleCN: 凡有积水处蚊子就能繁殖。

items.meaning: a net hung over a bed
items.example: The mosquito net kept the room quiet at night.
items.exampleCN: 蚊帐让夜里屋里安静下来。

items.example: A mosquito coil smoked in the corner.
items.exampleCN: 角落里点着一盘蚊香。

items.meaning: a substance that keeps the insect off
items.example: The mosquito repellent smelled of lemon grass.
items.exampleCN: 驱蚊剂有柠檬草的味道。

items.meaning: a small fish that eats larvae
items.example: Mosquitofish were introduced to clear the ponds.
items.exampleCN: 人们引入食蚊鱼来清理池塘。

items.meaning: a substance that kills the insect
items.example: The spray is a mosquitocide for drains.
items.exampleCN: 这种喷雾是用于排水沟的灭蚊剂。

items.example: A mosquito hawk hovered over the path.
items.exampleCN: 一只蚊鹰在小径上方悬停。

items.example: Malaria is a mosquito-borne infection.
items.exampleCN: 疟疾是一种蚊媒感染。

definition_zh: 幼虫；昆虫自卵孵化后的幼期形态；毛虫、蛆、蛴螬等幼体；水生无脊椎动物的自由生活幼体；蝌蚪式的水生幼期；生命史中的幼体阶段；不成熟的雏形；面具与幽灵（拉丁语旧义）
definition_en: the immature feeding stage of an insect or other invertebrate, which later changes into the adult form; historically also a mask or ghost
core_image: 叶片背面趴着一条肉虫，身体一节一节，六只真足紧贴叶脉，身边是被啃出的缺口
scene: 叶片背面，一条幼虫紧贴叶脉啃出月牙形的缺口。A larva chews a crescent hole in the leaf while clinging to the vein.
sceneCN: 这里 larva 指「昆虫自卵孵化后的幼期取食形态」（第 1 个义项：幼虫）；句意为一条幼虫紧贴叶脉、在叶片上啃出月牙形缺口。可辨识物件：分节体躯、六只真足、叶脉、月牙形缺口。

pos.zh: 幼虫；幼体（昆虫或其它无脊椎动物）

senses.title: The immature feeding stage of an insect
senses.titleCN: 昆虫自卵孵化后的取食幼期
senses.definition: the wingless, often worm-like stage that hatches from an egg and feeds before transforming
senses.definitionCN: 从卵中孵出、通常无翅且形似蠕虫、取食之后才转变的幼期
senses.example: A larva chews a crescent hole in the leaf while clinging to the vein.
senses.exampleCN: 一条幼虫紧贴叶脉，在叶片上啃出月牙形缺口。
senses.why: The word marks a stage, not a species: any insect that undergoes complete change passes through a larva before the pupa.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标的是阶段而非物种：任何完全变态的昆虫都要经过幼虫才到蛹。

senses.title: A caterpillar or grub
senses.titleCN: 毛虫、蛆、蛴螬等具体幼体
senses.definition: the familiar worm-like young of butterflies, beetles or flies, named by shape in everyday speech
senses.definitionCN: 蝴蝶、甲虫或蝇类的幼体，日常说法按形状称呼
senses.example: The caterpillar is the larva of a moth or butterfly.
senses.exampleCN: 毛虫是蛾或蝴蝶的幼虫。
senses.why: Everyday names such as grub, maggot and caterpillar split the general stage into recognizable shapes.
senses.whyCN: 蛴螬、蛆、毛虫这些日常名把笼统的幼期拆成可辨认的形状。

senses.title: The free-living young of water animals
senses.titleCN: 水生无脊椎动物的自由生活幼体
senses.definition: a swimming young stage of many marine invertebrates, such as the trochophore of a worm or the nauplius of a crustacean
senses.definitionCN: 许多海洋无脊椎动物的游泳幼期，如环节动物的担轮幼虫或甲壳类的无节幼虫
senses.example: The barnacle passes through a swimming larva before it settles.
senses.exampleCN: 藤壶在定居之前要经过一个游泳的幼体阶段。
senses.why: Zoology generalized the term from insects to any animal whose young differs sharply from the adult.
senses.whyCN: 动物学把这个词从昆虫扩大到任何幼体与成体差别很大的动物。

senses.title: The tadpole stage of amphibians
senses.titleCN: 两栖类的水生幼期（蝌蚪）
senses.definition: the aquatic, gilled young of a frog or salamander, which later metamorphoses into the adult
senses.definitionCN: 蛙或蝾螈具鳃的水生幼体，之后变态为成体
senses.example: The tadpole is the larva of a frog, and it breathes with gills.
senses.exampleCN: 蝌蚪是蛙的幼虫，用鳃呼吸。
senses.why: Amphibian biology borrowed the insect term because the same two-stage pattern appears, water young then land adult.
senses.whyCN: 两栖动物学借用了昆虫术语，因为出现了同样的两段式格局：水中幼体，陆生成体。

senses.title: A stage in a life cycle
senses.definition: the phase of a life cycle entered after hatching and left at metamorphosis, treated as a unit of timing
senses.definitionCN: 孵化之后进入、变态时结束的生命史阶段，被当作计时单位
senses.example: Larvae feed for weeks before the pupal stage begins.
senses.exampleCN: 幼虫取食数周之后才进入蛹期。
senses.why: This abstract sense measures development by stages; the noun becomes a slot in a schedule rather than an animal.
senses.whyCN: 这一抽象义用阶段来度量发育；名词成了时间表上的格子，而非动物。

senses.title: An undeveloped early form
senses.definition: anything that exists in an early, unformed state, compared to an insect that has not yet taken its adult shape
senses.definitionCN: 任何处于早期、尚未成形状态的事物，比作尚未长成成虫形态的昆虫
senses.example: The proposal is still a larva, all appetite and no structure.
senses.exampleCN: 这份提案还只是个幼虫，只有胃口，没有结构。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the biological core: what is describes is feeding and growing, not yet finished.
senses.whyCN: 比喻保留了生物核心：所描述之物正在取食与生长，尚未完成。

senses.title: A mask or ghost
senses.definition: the original Latin sense of a mask, especially one worn by an actor, or a ghost haunting a house
senses.definitionCN: 拉丁语原义：面具，尤指演员所戴，或出没于屋中的幽灵
senses.example: In Latin, larva could mean a mask worn on the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 在拉丁语中，larva 可以指舞台上戴的面具。
senses.why: Linnaeus took an old word for mask and ghost and made it a scientific term, so the modern sense carries a trace of disguise.
senses.whyCN: 林奈把一个意为面具与幽灵的旧词变成科学术语，现代义因此带着伪装的痕迹。

senses.title: A juvenile form used as food or pest
senses.titleCN: 作为饵料或害虫的幼体
senses.definition: the young stage considered as a resource or a pest, as when larvae are sold as fish food or sprayed as crop pests
senses.definitionCN: 把幼期当作资源或害物，如作为鱼饲料出售或作为作物害虫喷杀
senses.example: Anglers buy larvae by the tub for bait.
senses.exampleCN: 钓鱼人按盒购买幼虫作饵。
senses.why: Economics and agriculture recast the stage as a product or a target, which is a further extension of the biological sense.
senses.whyCN: 经济与农业把这个阶段改读为产品或清除对象，是生物义的进一步延伸。

intro.en: Larva is Latin for 'mask, ghost'. Linnaeus adopted it in the eighteenth century for the young stage of an insect, and the entomological sense drove out the older one.
intro.cn: larva 在拉丁语中意为「面具、幽灵」。林奈在 18 世纪把它采用为昆虫幼期的名称，昆虫学义后来压过了旧义。

items.en: Latin larva meant a mask, especially a frightening one, and by extension a ghost or spectre.
items.cn: 拉丁 larva 指面具，尤指吓人的面具，并引申为幽灵、鬼魂。

items.en: Latin plural larvae came into English with the scientific term; the English plural larvas is rare and mainly historical.
items.cn: 拉丁复数 larvae 随科学术语进入英语；英语式复数 larvas 罕见，主要用于历史文献。

items.en: The step from 'mask' to 'caterpillar' is not fully explained; a common suggestion is that the young insect looks like a disguise of the adult, but this is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 从「面具」到「毛虫」的一步没有得到完整解释；常见说法是幼体看起来像成虫的伪装，但这只是假说。

items.en: Linnaeus fixed larva as the term for the immature stage in his eighteenth-century classification, and the word entered general English through natural history.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪分类学中把 larva 定为幼期的术语，这个词经自然史著作进入一般英语。

items.en: Zoology later applied the term to the young of crustaceans, molluscs and amphibians, widening it well beyond insects.
items.cn: 动物学后来把这个词用于甲壳类、软体动物与两栖类的幼体，范围远超昆虫。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the deeper origin and the exact first citation are not settled, so any pre-Latin form offered here is a reconstruction and competing hypotheses are left side by side.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：更深的来源与确切最早书证均无定论，此处给出的拉丁语之前形式属重构形式，并列假说一并保留、不作定论。

note.en: Group one holds words whose spelling or sound invites confusion with larva; group two holds biological terms for young animals.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音易与 larva 混淆的词；第二组收表示幼体动物的生物学术语。

entries.definition: Lava comes from Italian and Latin labes 'a fall, a slide' and has nothing to do with insects; the two words differ by one letter.
entries.definitionCN: lava 来自意大利语与拉丁 labes「滑落」，与昆虫无关；两词只差一个字母。

entries.definition: Larval is the adjective built on larva, not a separate noun.
entries.definitionCN: larval 是由 larva 构成的形容词，不是另一个名词。

entries.definition: Larvae is simply the Latin plural of larva; using it as a singular is a common error.
entries.definitionCN: larvae 只是 larva 的拉丁复数；把它当单数用是常见错误。

entries.definition: This English-style plural appears in older texts but is not the standard form today.
entries.definitionCN: 这一英语式复数见于较早文献，今天并非标准形式。

entries.definition: A nymph is the young of an insect with incomplete metamorphosis; it already resembles the adult and has no pupal stage.
entries.definitionCN: nymph 指不完全变态昆虫的幼期；它已形似成虫，没有蛹期。

entries.definition: A grub is a thick, legless larva, typically of a beetle, and names one shape rather than the stage.
entries.definitionCN: grub 指粗壮无足的幼虫，多见于甲虫，是一个形状名称而非阶段名称。

entries.definition: Caterpillar names the larva of a butterfly or moth, usually with visible legs and a segmented body.
entries.definitionCN: caterpillar 指蝴蝶或蛾的幼虫，通常有明显足与分节的身体。

entries.definition: A maggot is the legless larva of a fly, found in decaying matter and used in medicine to clean wounds.
entries.definitionCN: maggot 是蝇类的无足幼虫，见于腐败物中，医学上也用于清创。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin larva first meant a mask or ghost; the insect sense is a later scientific borrowing.
normal.cn: 拉丁 larva 本指面具或幽灵；昆虫义是后来的科学借用。

normal.en: The family runs larva, larvae, larval, larvicide and larviparous.
normal.cn: 词族包括 larva、larvae、larval、larvicide 与 larviparous。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: larva stage, insect larva, larva migrans.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：幼虫期、昆虫幼虫、游走性幼虫。

normal.en: The standard plural is larvae, following Latin first-declension nouns.
normal.cn: 标准复数是 larvae，遵循拉丁第一变格法名词。

normal.en: Complete metamorphosis runs egg, larva, pupa, adult.
normal.cn: 完全变态依次为卵、幼虫、蛹、成虫。

abstract.en: Picture a mask left on a chair, still shaped like the face that wore it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张留在椅子上的面具，仍带着戴它那张脸的轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture a body that is all appetite and no wings.
abstract.cn: 想象一具只有胃口、没有翅膀的身体。

abstract.en: Picture a swimmer that will later glue itself to a rock and never move again.
abstract.cn: 想象一个游泳者，日后会把自己粘在岩石上，再也不动。

examples.en: Each larva moults several times before it is ready to pupate.
examples.cn: 每条幼虫在准备化蛹前要蜕皮数次。

examples.en: The larvae of mosquitoes breathe through a tube at the water surface.
examples.cn: 蚊的幼虫通过水面上的呼吸管呼吸。

examples.en: Fossil larvae show the feeding marks of ancient insects on leaves.
examples.cn: 化石幼虫在叶片上留下了远古昆虫的取食痕迹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「larva（拉瓦）」——从卵里「拉」出来的小肉虫 → 幼虫

root: 拉丁 larva「面具、幽灵」；林奈 18 世纪采用为昆虫幼期术语。「面具」到「毛虫」的过渡未获完整解释，相关说法仅为假说。复数 larvae 为拉丁式，larvas 罕见。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one stage: a worm-like feeder, its named shapes, its water-borne cousins, the amphibian version, the slot in a life cycle, the metaphor of immaturity, the old mask sense and the stage as product.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个阶段展开：蠕虫状的取食者、各种形状名称、水中同族、两栖版本、生命史中的一格、不成熟的比喻、旧时的面具义，以及作为产品的幼体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a segmented worm-like body with six true legs clamped to a leaf vein, eating a crescent hole.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具分节的蠕虫状身体，六只真足扣住叶脉，啃出月牙形缺口。

branches.en: THE FEEDER: the stage and its everyday shapes, caterpillar, grub and maggot.
branches.cn: 取食者：这一阶段及其日常形状——毛虫、蛴螬、蛆。

branches.en: OTHER WATERS: crustacean and amphibian young repeat the pattern outside insects.
branches.cn: 别处的水域：甲壳类与两栖类的幼体在昆虫之外重复同一格局。

branches.en: THE SLOT: life cycle timing turns the animal into a stage and a product.
branches.cn: 那一格：生命史的计时把动物变成阶段与产品。

branches.en: IMMATURE FORM: the metaphor keeps feeding and growing, without a finished shape.
branches.cn: 未成形：比喻保留取食与生长，尚无完成的形状。

branches.en: MASK AND GHOST: the Latin word for a disguise is the origin of the scientific term.
branches.cn: 面具与幽灵：意为伪装的那个拉丁词正是科学术语的来源。

intro.en: Larva is a Latin noun; English builds its family with Latin plurals and suffixes, and the larv- stem also appears in learned compounds.
intro.cn: larva 是拉丁名词；英语用拉丁复数与后缀构成词族，larv- 词干也出现在学术复合词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin larva, plural larvae, gives larval, larvicide and larviparous; the same stem appears in larvarium, a place for keeping larvae.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 larva（复数 larvae）衍生 larval、larvicide、larviparous；同一词干亦见于 larvarium，指饲养幼虫的场所。

items.example: Each larva feeds on one leaf.
items.exampleCN: 每条幼虫取食一片叶子。

items.example: The larvae hatch within three days.
items.exampleCN: 幼虫在三天内孵化。

items.example: Larval fish are almost transparent.
items.exampleCN: 幼鱼几乎透明。

items.example: The pond was treated with a larvicide.
items.exampleCN: 池塘用了杀幼虫剂。

items.example: Some flies are larviparous rather than egg-laying.
items.exampleCN: 有些蝇类直接产幼虫而非产卵。

items.example: The female beetle remains larviform as an adult.
items.exampleCN: 这种雌甲虫成年后仍保持幼虫形。

items.example: The lab keeps a larvarium beside the microscope.
items.exampleCN: 实验室在显微镜旁设了幼虫饲养箱。

items.example: Larva migrans produces a creeping skin line.
items.exampleCN: 游走性幼虫在皮肤上留下爬行线。

latinEntries.structure: larva, larvae (f., first declension, zoological use)
latinEntries.meaning: the young stage of an animal

definition_zh: 「larva」的拉丁式复数：幼虫（复数）；一巢同批孵出的幼虫；蚊的孑孓；蜂巢中的蜂幼虫；成群暴食的毛虫；水产养殖中的幼虫饵料；被误作单数使用的 larvae；化石或遗迹中的幼虫群
definition_en: the Latin plural of larva, naming the immature feeding stages of insects and other invertebrates, and used collectively for a brood, a swarm of caterpillars or a batch of water-borne young
core_image: 蜂巢的巢房里，一排乳白色的幼虫蜷成小环，蜡壁上映着工蜂的影子
scene: 蜂巢的巢房里，一排蜂幼虫蜷成乳白色的小环。The larvae curl inside their wax cells like small pale rings.
sceneCN: 这里 larvae 是 larva 的复数形式，指「一巢同批孵出的幼虫」（第 2 个义项：巢内整批幼虫）；句意为蜂幼虫在蜡质巢房里蜷成一个个乳白色的小环。可辨识物件：六角巢房、蜷曲的幼虫、蜡壁、工蜂影子。

pos.zh: 幼虫（larva 的复数形式；生物学术语）

senses.title: The Latin plural of larva
senses.definition: the standard plural of larva, used in zoology for immature feeding stages of many animals
senses.definitionCN: larva 的标准复数，动物学中用来指许多动物的幼期取食阶段
senses.example: Biologists count the larvae under a dissecting scope.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家在解剖镜下清点幼虫。
senses.why: English borrowed the whole Latin pair larva and larvae, so the plural is not formed with -s but by changing the ending.
senses.whyCN: 英语整套借入拉丁的 larva 与 larvae 一对，因此复数不是加 -s，而是换词尾。

senses.title: A brood inside a nest
senses.definition: the whole group of young larvae living together in a nest, comb or gallery
senses.definitionCN: 同一巢、巢脾或虫道中共同生活的一整批幼虫
senses.example: The larvae curl inside their wax cells like small pale rings.
senses.exampleCN: 蜂幼虫在蜡质巢房里蜷成一个个乳白色的小环。
senses.why: A plural used collectively turns many individuals into one brood, which is how beekeepers and entomologists usually speak.
senses.whyCN: 集合用法的复数把许多个体说成一巢幼虫，养蜂人与昆虫学家通常这样表述。

senses.title: Mosquito wrigglers
senses.definition: the water-borne young of mosquitoes, which hang at the surface and breathe through a siphon
senses.definitionCN: 蚊的水生幼体，倒悬在水面并通过呼吸管呼吸
senses.example: Mosquito larvae rise to the surface when the water warms.
senses.exampleCN: 水温升高时，孑孓会浮到水面。
senses.why: This sense fixes the word to one family and one habitat, water, where the plural is nearly always used.
senses.whyCN: 这一义把词固定在一个科与一种生境——水中，此处几乎总用复数。

senses.title: Bee grubs in the comb
senses.definition: the legless white young of bees, reared in cells provisioned by workers
senses.definitionCN: 蜂类无足的白色幼体，由工蜂在备好食物的巢房里养育
senses.example: Worker bees feed the larvae a diet of pollen and nectar.
senses.exampleCN: 工蜂用花粉与花蜜喂养这些幼虫。
senses.why: Beekeeping uses the plural for the whole rearing unit, because a cell block is managed as one batch.
senses.whyCN: 养蜂业用复数指整个抚育单元，因为一整块巢房是当作一批来管理的。

senses.title: A defoliating swarm of caterpillars
senses.definition: caterpillars present in numbers large enough to strip foliage
senses.definitionCN: 数量大到能把叶片吃光的毛虫群
senses.example: The larvae stripped the oak copse in a single week.
senses.exampleCN: 这些幼虫一周之内就把橡树矮林吃光了。
senses.why: Pest reports speak of larvae rather than caterpillars when the damage is counted by area, which shifts the word toward a population.
senses.whyCN: 虫害报告按面积计算损失时说的是 larvae 而非毛虫，词因此偏向「种群」。

senses.title: A feed batch in aquaculture
senses.titleCN: 水产养殖中的幼虫饵料
senses.definition: the young stage sold or reared as food for fish and other farmed animals
senses.definitionCN: 作为鱼类或其它养殖动物饲料而出售或培育的幼期
senses.example: The hatchery buys live larvae by weight each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 孵化场每天早上按重量购买活幼虫。
senses.why: The word names the stage as a commodity when it is sold by weight rather than studied as an animal.
senses.whyCN: 当幼期按重量出售而非作为动物被研究时，这个词就把这个阶段说成一种商品。

senses.title: The mistaken singular use
senses.titleCN: 被误当单数使用的 larvae
senses.definition: a non-standard use of the plural form as if it were singular, common in informal writing
senses.definitionCN: 把复数形式当作单数用的非标准写法，常见于非正式文字
senses.example: The sign read 'one larvae per jar', which is a grammatical slip.
senses.exampleCN: 标牌上把复数当成单数来写，这是语法上的失误。
senses.why: Because the ending -ae is unfamiliar, writers sometimes treat larvae as a singular and invent the plural larvaes.
senses.whyCN: 由于 -ae 词尾不常见，写作者有时把 larvae 当单数，并生造出复数 larvaes。

senses.title: Young stages preserved as fossils
senses.titleCN: 化石或遗迹中的幼虫群
senses.definition: larval remains or traces preserved in rock, amber or sediment, studied as a group
senses.definitionCN: 保存在岩石、琥珀或沉积物中的幼虫遗骸或痕迹，作为群体研究
senses.example: Amber preserved a cluster of larvae beside a drop of resin.
senses.exampleCN: 琥珀把一小群幼虫保存在一滴树脂旁。
senses.why: Palaeontology uses the plural for an assemblage, so the word names a sample rather than a life stage.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学用复数指一个组合，词因此指一份标本，而非某个生命阶段。

intro.en: Larvae is the Latin plural of larva, literally 'masks, ghosts'. English took the pair larva and larvae straight from Latin, so the plural changes the ending rather than adding -s.
intro.cn: larvae 是拉丁 larva 的复数，字面为「面具、幽灵」。英语把 larva 与 larvae 一对直接借入，因此复数靠换词尾而非加 -s。

items.en: Latin larva belongs to the first declension, so its plural is larvae, with the ending -ae; English kept the Latin form unchanged.
items.cn: 拉丁 larva 属第一变格法，复数为 larvae，词尾 -ae；英语原样保留。

items.en: English also keeps larva as the singular, which makes the pair look irregular to speakers used to adding -s.
items.cn: 英语同时保留 larva 作单数，这对习惯了加 -s 的使用者来说显得不规则。

items.en: In Latin the word meant a mask or a ghost before zoology gave it the sense of an immature animal.
items.cn: 在拉丁语中，这个词在动物学赋予「幼体」义之前，意为面具或幽灵。

items.en: Eighteenth-century natural history fixed larva for the stage and larvae for the stage in numbers, and both forms spread through English science writing.
items.cn: 18 世纪的自然史把 larva 定为该阶段、larvae 定为群体的复数，两种形式随英语科学写作传播。

items.en: Because the -ae ending is opaque to most readers, larvae is sometimes misused as a singular, and the invented plural larvaes occasionally appears in unedited text.
items.cn: 由于 -ae 词尾对多数读者不透明，larvae 有时被误作单数，生造的复数 larvaes 偶尔出现在未校对的文字中。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the pre-Latin origin of larva is unsettled, and the shift from 'mask' to 'immature insect' is explained only by hypothesis, so the account here is not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：larva 的拉丁语之前来源无定论，从「面具」到「幼体」的转变只有假说解释，因此此处并不构成已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one separates larvae from the singular and from look-alike words; group two lists the collective nouns for young animals that overlap with it.
note.cn: 第一组把 larvae 与单数形式及形近词分开；第二组列出与它语义重叠的幼体集合名词。

entries.definition: Larva is the singular; larvae is what you get when there is more than one.
entries.definitionCN: larva 是单数；多于一只时用 larvae。

entries.definition: Larvas follows the English pattern but is rare and mainly found in older texts.
entries.definitionCN: larvas 按英语规则构成，但罕见，主要见于较早文献。

entries.definition: Lava differs by one letter and comes from a Latin word for a slide or fall, not from larva.
entries.definitionCN: lava 只差一个字母，源出意为滑落的拉丁词，与 larva 无关。

entries.definition: Larval is an adjective, so it cannot replace the plural noun in a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: larval 是形容词，不能在一句中替代复数名词。

entries.definition: A brood is the young hatched together from one batch of eggs, a collective noun that overlaps with larvae in a nest.
entries.definitionCN: brood 指同一批卵孵出的一窝幼体，作为集合名词与巢中的 larvae 重叠。

entries.definition: Grubs names thick legless larvae by shape, whereas larvae is the neutral scientific plural.
entries.definitionCN: grubs 按形状称呼粗壮无足的幼虫，larvae 则是中性的科学复数。

entries.definition: Caterpillars are the larvae of butterflies and moths, a subset of all larvae.
entries.definitionCN: caterpillars 是蝴蝶与蛾的幼虫，只是所有幼虫中的一部分。

entries.definition: Nymphs are young of insects with incomplete metamorphosis, which are not usually called larvae.
entries.definitionCN: nymphs 是不完全变态昆虫的幼期，通常不称作 larvae。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin first declension turns -a into -ae, so larva becomes larvae.
normal.cn: 拉丁第一变格法把 -a 变 -ae，因此 larva 成为 larvae。

normal.en: English keeps both forms, so the singular and plural look like a mismatched pair.
normal.cn: 英语两种形式都保留，单复数看上去并不配对。

normal.en: The family runs larva, larvae, larval, larvicide and larviparous.
normal.cn: 词族包括 larva、larvae、larval、larvicide 与 larviparous。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: mosquito larvae, bee larvae, insect larvae.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：孑孓、蜂幼虫、昆虫幼虫。

normal.en: If in doubt about number, ask whether the sentence counts one animal or a brood.
normal.cn: 拿不准单复数时，先问这句是在数一只还是一窝。

abstract.en: Picture a row of small pale rings, each in its own wax room.
abstract.cn: 想象一排乳白色的小环，每个都待在自己的蜡室里。

abstract.en: Picture a pond surface dotted with commas that breathe.
abstract.cn: 想象池面布满会呼吸的逗号。

abstract.en: Picture a rock that kept a whole nursery for a hundred million years.
abstract.cn: 想象一块把整间育儿室保存了一亿年的石头。

examples.en: The larvae hatched within three days of the eggs being laid.
examples.cn: 卵产下三天之内，幼虫就孵化了。

examples.en: Fish farmers buy larvae to feed the fry in the nursery ponds.
examples.cn: 养鱼户购买幼虫来喂养育苗池里的鱼苗。

examples.en: A cluster of larvae in amber shows the group behaviour of an extinct moth.
examples.cn: 琥珀中的一群幼虫显示了已灭绝蛾类的群体行为。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「larvae（拉维）」——被「拉」出来的一窝小虫 → 幼虫（复数）

root: 拉丁 larva「面具、幽灵」的第一变格法复数 larvae（-a 变 -ae）。英语整套借入 larva / larvae 一对。larva 的拉丁语之前来源不确定，面具义到幼体义的转变仅有假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from the plural form itself and then apply it to a brood in a nest, mosquito wrigglers, bee grubs, a defoliating swarm, a feed batch, the mistaken singular and a fossil assemblage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从复数形式本身出发，再用于巢内的一窝、孑孓、蜂幼虫、暴食的毛虫群、一批饵料、误作单数的用法与化石组合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of pale comma-shaped bodies, each sealed in its own wax cell of a comb.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排乳白色逗号状的躯体，每个都封在自己的蜡质巢房里。

branches.en: THE FORM: the borrowed plural and its misuse both concern grammar rather than nature.
branches.cn: 形式：借入的复数与误用都属于语法问题，而非自然。

branches.en: THE NEST: a brood in comb and the hive's reared young are managed as one batch.
branches.cn: 巢内：巢房中的一窝与蜂群抚育的幼体都当作一批管理。

branches.en: WATER AND FEED: wrigglers and hatchery larvae are counted by volume.
branches.cn: 水中与饵料：孑孓与孵化场的幼虫按体积计数。

branches.en: THE SWARM: a population large enough to strip a tree.
branches.cn: 虫群：数量大到能把一棵树吃光。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: an assemblage kept in amber or rock.
branches.cn: 深时：封在琥珀或岩石中的组合。

intro.en: Larvae is a Latin plural form; its family is shared with larva, and the endings -al, -cide, -form and -parous build the adjectives and nouns around it.
intro.cn: larvae 是拉丁复数形式；词族与 larva 共用，-al、-cide、-form、-parous 等词尾构成周围的形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin larva and its plural larvae supply the stem larv-, which English extends with -al, -cide, -form and -arium.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 larva 及其复数 larvae 提供词干 larv-，英语用 -al、-cide、-form、-arium 等扩展。

items.example: The larvae feed for a week.
items.exampleCN: 幼虫取食一周。

items.example: One larva hatched early.
items.exampleCN: 一条幼虫提早孵化。

items.example: Larval skin is thin and soft.
items.exampleCN: 幼虫的皮薄而软。

items.example: The larvicide broke the breeding cycle.
items.exampleCN: 杀幼虫剂打断了繁殖周期。

items.meaning: having the shape of a larva
items.example: The larviform female never grows wings.
items.exampleCN: 幼虫形的雌虫从不长翅。

items.example: Larviparous flies skip the egg stage.
items.exampleCN: 产幼虫的蝇类跳过卵期。

items.example: The larvarium is kept at constant humidity.
items.exampleCN: 幼虫饲养箱保持恒湿。

items.example: A larvate symptom hides the real disease.
items.exampleCN: 隐蔽的症状掩盖了真正的病。

latinEntries.structure: plural of larva (nominative and accusative plural)

definition_zh: 幼虫的；幼期的；幼虫形态的；幼虫栖境的；幼体发育的；幼鱼或幼两栖类的；雏形未成的（比喻）；蛆疗所用的
definition_en: relating to or being a larva, the immature stage of an animal before metamorphosis; also used figuratively for something still in an undeveloped form
core_image: 一只透明的小鱼贴着池底，身体上还看不到成鱼的条纹，只有一根细脊在动
scene: 池底的幼鱼身体透明，成鱼的条纹还没有出现。Larval fish remain almost transparent until their scales form.
sceneCN: 这里 larval 指「属幼体阶段的；幼体形态的」（第 6 个义项：幼鱼或幼两栖类的）；句意为处于幼鱼阶段的鱼几乎透明，直到鳞片长出。可辨识物件：透明身体、细脊、池底砂粒、未成形的鳍。

pos.zh: 幼虫的；幼期的；幼虫形态的；未成形的

senses.title: Of or belonging to a larva
senses.definition: relating to a larva or to the stage it represents, rather than to the adult
senses.definitionCN: 与幼虫或幼虫所代表的阶段有关，而非与成虫有关
senses.example: The larval skin is soft and never hardened like the adult cuticle.
senses.exampleCN: 幼虫的皮柔软，从不象成虫的外皮那样硬化。
senses.why: The suffix -al turns the noun into a plain relational adjective: whatever belongs to the larva is larval.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把名词变成纯粹的关系形容词：凡属于幼虫的都叫 larval。

senses.title: The stage before metamorphosis
senses.definition: the period of growth between hatching and the pupal or adult stage
senses.definitionCN: 从孵化到蛹期或成虫期之间的生长期
senses.example: Most of the insect's life is spent in the larval stage.
senses.exampleCN: 这种昆虫一生的大部分时间都在幼虫期度过。
senses.why: This sense is about time rather than body: larval marks the stretch in which feeding and growth happen.
senses.whyCN: 这一义讲的是时间而非身体：larval 标出取食与生长所发生的那一段。

senses.title: The body plan of the young
senses.definition: the shape and structure typical of a larva, such as a worm-like body with chewing mouthparts
senses.definitionCN: 幼虫典型的外形与结构，如蠕虫状身体配咀嚼式口器
senses.example: The larval form has no wings and no compound eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 幼虫形态没有翅膀，也没有复眼。
senses.why: Here the adjective contrasts two body plans, the young one and the adult one, within a single life.
senses.whyCN: 此处形容词在一个生命内部对比两套身体构型：幼体与成体。

senses.title: The habitat of the young
senses.definition: the environment where larvae live, such as still water, soil, leaf litter or a host body
senses.definitionCN: 幼虫生活的环境，如静水、土壤、落叶层或寄主体内
senses.example: The larval habitat of this mosquito is any standing water near houses.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蚊的幼虫栖境是房屋附近的任何积水。
senses.why: Ecology attaches larval to the place as well as the animal, which is useful in control programmes.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把 larval 既挂到动物上也挂到地点上，这在防治规划中很有用。

senses.title: Development before maturity
senses.definition: growth and differentiation that occur before the adult form is reached
senses.definitionCN: 在达到成体形态之前发生的生长与分化
senses.example: Larval development speeds up as the water warms.
senses.exampleCN: 水温升高时，幼体发育加快。
senses.why: The phrase larval development treats the whole process as a measurable period of growth.
senses.whyCN: 「larval development」这一说法把整个过程当作可测量的生长期。

senses.title: Young fish or amphibians
senses.definition: describing the young of fish or amphibians while they still differ from the adult in shape and habit
senses.definitionCN: 描述鱼或两栖类的幼体，其形状与习性仍与成体不同
senses.example: Larval fish remain almost transparent until their scales form.
senses.exampleCN: 处于幼鱼阶段的鱼几乎透明，直到鳞片长出。
senses.why: The adjective generalizes from insects to vertebrates whose young also change shape radically.
senses.whyCN: 形容词从昆虫扩大到幼体同样发生剧烈形变的脊椎动物。

senses.title: An undeveloped first attempt
senses.definition: used figuratively for a plan, idea or institution that exists only in a rudimentary form
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指只以雏形存在的方案、想法或机构
senses.example: The committee is still larval, meeting in a borrowed room.
senses.exampleCN: 这个委员会还处在雏形阶段，在一间借来的屋子里开会。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the idea of a stage that must still feed and grow before it can act.
senses.whyCN: 比喻保留了「还需取食与生长才能行动」的阶段意思。

senses.title: Of maggot therapy
senses.definition: describing medicinal maggots used to clean a wound, in the phrase larval therapy
senses.definitionCN: 描述用于清理创口的药用蛆，见于「larval therapy」一语
senses.example: Larval therapy removes dead tissue without antibiotics.
senses.exampleCN: 蛆疗不用抗生素就能清除坏死组织。
senses.why: Medicine narrowed the adjective to a specific treatment, so a general biological word names a clinical procedure.
senses.whyCN: 医学把形容词收窄到一种特定治疗，一个通用生物词因此成了临床术名。

intro.en: Larval is larva plus the Latin-derived adjective ending -al, meaning 'relating to'. The base noun is Latin larva 'mask, ghost', adopted by Linnaeus for the immature insect stage.
intro.cn: larval 由 larva 加拉丁来源的形容词后缀 -al（意为「与……有关的」）构成。基名词是拉丁 larva「面具、幽灵」，由林奈采用为昆虫幼期。

items.en: The noun larva first meant a mask or a ghost; its use for the young insect is a later scientific decision.
items.cn: 名词 larva 本指面具或幽灵；用于昆虫幼期是后来的科学决定。

items.en: Latin adjectives in -alis, borrowed into English as -al, relate a noun to another noun, giving the pattern noun + al.
items.cn: 拉丁 -alis 形容词借入英语作 -al，把一个名词与另一个名词联系起来，形成「名词 + al」的模式。

items.en: English formed larval inside its own vocabulary on the model of pairs such as fate and fatal, so the word is an English construction on a Latin base.
items.cn: 英语按 fate 与 fatal 这类配对，在自己的词汇内部构成了 larval，因此是以拉丁词基为底的英语构造。

items.en: Natural history applied larval to stages, habits and habitats, and the adjective became a standard label in entomology and fisheries.
items.cn: 自然史把 larval 用于阶段、习性与栖境，这个形容词在昆虫学与渔业中成为标准标签。

items.en: Larval therapy, the deliberate use of sterile maggots to clean wounds, brought the adjective into clinical language.
items.cn: 蛆疗即有意用无菌蛆清理创口，把这个形容词带入临床语言。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the deeper origin and the exact first citation are not settled, so any pre-Latin form offered here is a reconstruction and competing hypotheses are left side by side.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：更深的来源与确切最早书证均无定论，此处给出的拉丁语之前形式属重构形式，并列假说一并保留、不作定论。

note.en: Group one separates larval from the noun and from near-identical spellings; group two lists adjectives that describe early or unfinished stages.
note.cn: 第一组把 larval 与名词及拼写极近的形式分开；第二组收描述早期或未完成阶段的形容词。

entries.definition: Larva is the animal; larval is the adjective that describes it.
entries.definitionCN: larva 是动物本身；larval 是描述它的形容词。

entries.definition: Larvae is a plural noun and cannot stand where an adjective is needed.
entries.definitionCN: larvae 是复数名词，不能出现在需要形容词的位置。

entries.definition: Larvate is a medical adjective meaning hidden or masked, built on the older 'mask' sense.
entries.definitionCN: larvate 是医学形容词，意为隐蔽的、面具状的，建立在较早的「面具」义上。

entries.definition: Lava is a different word with a different origin, despite the almost identical spelling.
entries.definitionCN: lava 是另一个词，来源不同，尽管拼写几乎一样。

entries.definition: Immature is the general word for anything not yet adult, and it applies to behaviour as well as bodies.
entries.definitionCN: immature 是泛指尚未成熟，可用于行为也可用于身体。

entries.definition: Juvenile is the usual term for young vertebrates, while larval is standard for insects and amphibian young.
entries.definitionCN: juvenile 是脊椎动物幼体的常用词，larval 则多用于昆虫与两栖类幼体。

entries.definition: Embryonic covers the stage before birth or hatching, one step earlier than larval.
entries.definitionCN: embryonic 指出生或孵化之前的阶段，比 larval 更早一步。

entries.definition: Pupal names the resting stage after the larva, so the two adjectives mark consecutive stages.
entries.definitionCN: pupal 指幼虫之后的休眠阶段，两个形容词标出相邻的两个阶段。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Larva plus -al gives the relational adjective, exactly as fate plus -al gives fatal.
normal.cn: larva 加 -al 构成关系形容词，正如 fate 加 -al 构成 fatal。

normal.en: The family runs larva, larvae, larval, larvally, larvicide and larviparous.
normal.cn: 词族包括 larva、larvae、larval、larvally、larvicide 与 larviparous。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: larval stage, larval fish, larval therapy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：幼虫期、幼鱼、蛆疗。

normal.en: Complete metamorphosis gives four stages, and only the second is larval.
normal.cn: 完全变态有四个阶段，其中只有第二个是幼体阶段。

normal.en: The adjective generalizes to any young animal whose shape differs from the adult.
normal.cn: 这个形容词可推广到任何幼体形状与成体不同的动物。

abstract.en: Picture a body that is only a stomach with legs.
abstract.cn: 想象一具只有胃和腿的身体。

abstract.en: Picture a committee that has not yet grown its own walls.
abstract.cn: 想象一个还没长出自己墙壁的委员会。

abstract.en: Picture a transparent fish that will only show its stripes later.
abstract.cn: 想象一条透明的鱼，条纹要到后来才显出。

examples.en: The larval stage of this beetle lasts almost two years underground.
examples.cn: 这种甲虫的幼虫期在地下持续近两年。

examples.en: Larval fish drift with the current before they can swim against it.
examples.cn: 幼鱼在能逆流游动之前随水流漂流。

examples.en: Larval therapy is used when antibiotics fail and dead tissue must be removed.
examples.cn: 当抗生素无效、必须清除坏死组织时会用蛆疗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「larval（拉窝）」——把一窝幼虫「拉」出来的样子 → 幼虫的

root: larva（拉丁「面具、幽灵」，林奈采用为昆虫幼期）+ 拉丁来源形容词后缀 -al「与……有关的」。属英语在拉丁词基上自行构成的形容词，模式同 fate / fatal。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one adjective to body, time, shape, place, growth, vertebrates, an unfinished plan and finally a clinical treatment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个形容词用于身体、时间、形状、地点、生长、脊椎动物、未完成的方案，最后用于一项临床治疗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft, wingless body with chewing mouthparts, sealed in a cell and still growing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具柔软无翅、带咀嚼式口器的身体，封在巢房里，仍在生长。

branches.en: PLAIN RELATION: the suffix simply says 'of the larva'.
branches.cn: 纯粹关系：后缀只表示「属于幼虫」。

branches.en: TIME: the stage and its measurable growth are two ways of saying 'before the adult'.
branches.cn: 时间：阶段与可测量的生长是「成体之前」的两种说法。

branches.en: SHAPE: insect young and vertebrate young share a different body plan from the adult.
branches.cn: 形状：昆虫幼体与脊椎动物幼体都拥有与成体不同的身体构型。

branches.en: PLACE: the adjective attaches to the habitat as well as the animal.
branches.cn: 地点：形容词既附于动物，也附于栖境。

branches.en: OUTSIDE BIOLOGY: an unfinished committee and a maggot treatment both keep the idea of a stage not yet adult.
branches.cn: 生物学之外：未成形的委员会与蛆疗都保留了「尚未成年」的阶段意思。

intro.en: Larval is built inside English from a Latin noun and the suffix -al; the wider family uses -cide, -form, -parous and -arium on the same stem.
intro.cn: larval 由拉丁名词加后缀 -al 在英语内部构成；更大词族在同一词干上使用 -cide、-form、-parous 与 -arium。

latinIntro.en: Latin larva supplies larv-, and English suffixes -al, -cide, -form, -parous and -arium all attach to it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 larva 提供词干 larv-，英语后缀 -al、-cide、-form、-parous、-arium 均可附加其上。
