items.exampleCN: 幼虫的皮容易受损。

items.example: The species overwinters larvally.
items.exampleCN: 这个物种以幼体形态越冬。

items.example: The larva has no wings.
items.exampleCN: 幼虫没有翅膀。

items.example: The larvae cluster under the leaf.
items.exampleCN: 幼虫聚集在叶下。

items.example: Larvicide is applied to standing water.
items.exampleCN: 杀幼虫剂施用于积水。

items.example: The adult female is larviform.
items.exampleCN: 成年雌虫为幼虫形。

items.example: Larviparous species bypass the egg.
items.exampleCN: 产幼虫的种类跳过卵期。

items.example: The larvarium holds twelve trays.
items.exampleCN: 幼虫饲养处有十二个托盘。

definition_zh: 蛹；完全变态昆虫由幼虫变为成虫之间的静止阶段；蝶类的蛹（日常也称蝶蛹）；蛹体本身；茧内之物（须与茧壳区分）；介壳虫等类群的蛹状期；蛰伏待变的比喻；拉丁语旧义「玩偶、女孩」
definition_en: the resting stage of an insect with complete metamorphosis, between larva and adult, during which the body is rebuilt inside a protective case
core_image: 枝条上，一枚褐色的蛹挂在叶柄旁，外壳坚硬，末端有几粒金点
scene: 叶片旁挂着一枚褐色的蛹，外壳末端有几粒金点。A brown pupa hangs beside the leaf stalk, its hard case tipped with gold spots.
sceneCN: 这里 pupa 指「完全变态昆虫幼虫与成虫之间的静止阶段」（第 1 个义项：蛹期个体）；句意为叶片旁挂着一枚褐色蛹，坚硬外壳的末端带金点。可辨识物件：悬挂的蛹壳、叶柄、外壳、金点。

senses.title: The resting stage of complete metamorphosis
senses.titleCN: 完全变态中的静止阶段
senses.definition: the stage between larva and adult in which the insect stops feeding and rebuilds its body
senses.definitionCN: 幼虫与成虫之间停止取食、重建身体的阶段
senses.example: A brown pupa hangs beside the leaf stalk, its hard case tipped with gold spots.
senses.exampleCN: 叶片旁挂着一枚褐色的蛹，坚硬外壳的末端带金点。
senses.why: The stage exists only in insects with complete metamorphosis, so pupa marks a rebuilt body rather than a smaller adult.
senses.whyCN: 只有完全变态的昆虫才有这一阶段，因此 pupa 标出的是被重建的身体，而非缩小的成虫。

senses.title: A butterfly's chrysalis
senses.titleCN: 蝶类的蛹（日常也称蝶蛹）
senses.definition: the naked, often green or brown case of a butterfly, commonly called a chrysalis
senses.definitionCN: 蝴蝶裸露的、常为绿或褐色的蛹壳，日常称「chrysalis」
senses.example: The butterfly pupa split open in the afternoon heat.
senses.exampleCN: 蝶蛹在午后的热气中裂开。
senses.why: A chrysalis is one kind of pupa, the uncovered butterfly version; the two words overlap but are not identical.
senses.whyCN: 「chrysalis」是蛹的一种，指蝴蝶那种裸露形式；两词重叠但并不等同。

senses.title: The pupal body inside the case
senses.definition: the transforming insect itself, considered apart from the shell that protects it
senses.definitionCN: 正在进行改造的昆虫本体，与保护它的外壳分开来看
senses.example: Inside the pupa, wings and legs are already folded into place.
senses.exampleCN: 蛹体内部，翅与足已经折叠到位。
senses.why: This sense separates the animal from its case, which matters when the shell is called a puparium.
senses.whyCN: 这一义把动物与外壳分开，当外壳被称作「puparium」时尤其重要。

senses.title: A cocoon's contents
senses.titleCN: 茧内之物（须与茧壳区分）
senses.definition: the pupa enclosed in a silk cocoon, often confused with the cocoon itself
senses.definitionCN: 被丝茧包裹的蛹，常与茧壳本身混淆
senses.example: Moth pupae are usually hidden inside a silk cocoon.
senses.exampleCN: 蛾蛹通常藏在丝茧里。
senses.why: A cocoon is silk spun around the pupa, so the two nouns name different objects even when they appear together.
senses.whyCN: 茧是绕在蛹周围的丝，两个名词指不同物件，即使同时出现。

senses.title: A pupa-like stage in other groups
senses.definition: a resting stage of some scale insects or other arthropods that resembles a pupa though it is not one
senses.definitionCN: 某些介壳虫或其它节肢动物的静止期，形似蛹却不属真正的蛹
senses.example: Male scale insects pass through a pupa-like stage before they fly.
senses.exampleCN: 雄性介壳虫在飞行之前会经历一个似蛹的阶段。
senses.why: Comparative entomology uses the word loosely for any quiescent remodelling stage, which is convenient but imprecise.
senses.whyCN: 比较昆虫学把这个词宽松地用于任何静止的重塑阶段，方便但不精确。

senses.title: A dormant state before change
senses.definition: a person or thing in a quiet, closed state that is expected to emerge in a new form
senses.definitionCN: 处于安静封闭、预期将以新形态出现的人或事物
senses.example: The project sat in its pupa for a year before anyone noticed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目在「蛹」里待了一年，才有人注意到。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the case and the stillness, then promises a later emergence.
senses.whyCN: 比喻借用外壳与静止，随后许诺日后的羽化。

senses.title: A puppet or a girl in Latin
senses.titleCN: 拉丁语中的玩偶、女孩（旧义）
senses.definition: the original Latin sense of a doll, a girl or a puppet, which survives in English only inside borrowed words
senses.definitionCN: 拉丁语原义：玩偶、女孩或木偶，在英语中只保留在借入词里
senses.example: Latin pupa named a doll, and the modern insect term keeps only the shape of the word.
senses.exampleCN: 拉丁 pupa 指玩偶，现代昆虫术语只保留了词的外形。
senses.why: The scientific sense is a deliberate reuse of an old noun, not a development of the doll meaning.
senses.whyCN: 科学义是对旧名词的有意借用，并非玩偶义的发展。

senses.title: A stage counted in rearing
senses.titleCN: 饲养中按头数统计的蛹
senses.definition: the stage as a unit in laboratory rearing, counted and timed rather than described
senses.definitionCN: 实验室饲养中的计量单位，只清点与计时，不作描述
senses.example: The lab keeps fifty pupae at constant temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在恒温下保存五十头蛹。
senses.why: This practical sense turns the animal into a countable unit of a protocol, a common shift in laboratory language.
senses.whyCN: 这一实用义把动物变成方案中的一个可数单位，是实验室语言的常见转移。

intro.en: Pupa is Latin for 'girl, doll'. Linnaeus reused the old noun for the insect stage, and the scientific sense now dominates in English.
intro.cn: pupa 在拉丁语中意为「女孩、玩偶」。林奈把这个旧名词改用于昆虫阶段，科学义如今在英语中占主导。

items.en: Latin pupa meant a girl or a doll, and pupus meant a boy; both belonged to everyday domestic vocabulary, not to natural history.
items.cn: 拉丁 pupa 指女孩或玩偶，pupus 指男孩；两者都属日常家庭词汇，与自然史无关。

items.en: Pupilla, a little girl, also named the pupil of the eye, and pupillus, a little boy, named a ward; these senses survive in English pupil.
items.cn: 指小的 pupilla（小女孩）也指眼睛的瞳孔，pupillus（小男孩）指受监护的孤儿；这些意义保存在英语 pupil 中。

items.en: Linnaeus adopted pupa in the eighteenth century for the quiescent stage of insects, and the entomological sense spread through European science.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪把 pupa 采用为昆虫的静止阶段，昆虫学义随之传遍欧洲科学界。

items.en: English already had chrysalis for a butterfly's uncovered case and cocoon for silk covering; pupa was needed as the general stage name.
items.cn: 英语原有 chrysalis 指蝶的裸露蛹壳、cocoon 指丝茧；pupa 则被需要为概括性的阶段名。

items.en: Puppet and pupa descend from the same Latin noun through different routes, so the toy and the insect share a distant ancestor.
items.cn: puppet 与 pupa 经不同路径出自同一拉丁名词，玩具与昆虫因此共享一个遥远的祖先。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin origin of pupa is not established, and the exact date of its adoption for insects rests on Linnaeus's usage rather than on a single citation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：pupa 的拉丁语之前来源未获证明，它被用于昆虫的确切年代依据是林奈的用法，而非某一条书证。

note.en: Group one separates pupa from its plural, its adjective and Latin relatives that now mean other things; group two lists the casings and stages people confuse with a pupa.
note.cn: 第一组把 pupa 与复数、形容词及已转义的拉丁亲属分开；第二组列出人们常与蛹混淆的外壳与阶段。

entries.definition: Pupae is the standard plural, formed by changing the ending rather than adding -s.
entries.definitionCN: pupae 是标准复数，靠换词尾而非加 -s。

entries.definition: Pupal is the adjective, so it describes the stage while pupa names the animal.
entries.definitionCN: pupal 是形容词，描述该阶段；pupa 则指这个动物。

entries.definition: Pupil descends from Latin pupilla or pupillus, little girl or boy, so it shares the root but not the insect sense.
entries.definitionCN: pupil 出自拉丁 pupilla 或 pupillus，即小女孩或小男孩，词根相同而昆虫义不同。

entries.definition: Puppet came through Old French from Latin pupa, a doll, so the toy and the insect are distant cousins.
entries.definitionCN: puppet 经古法语出自拉丁 pupa「玩偶」，玩具与昆虫因此是远亲。

entries.definition: A chrysalis is the uncovered pupa of a butterfly, one subtype of the general stage.
entries.definitionCN: chrysalis 指蝴蝶裸露的蛹，是这一阶段的一个子类。

entries.definition: A cocoon is silk spun around a pupa, a covering rather than the stage itself.
entries.definitionCN: cocoon 是绕在蛹外的丝，是包被物而非阶段本身。

entries.definition: A nymph is the young of an insect without a pupal stage, so it never becomes a pupa.
entries.definitionCN: nymph 是没有蛹期的不完全变态昆虫的幼期，因此永远不会变成 pupa。

entries.definition: The larva feeds and grows; the pupa stops feeding and rebuilds.
entries.definitionCN: larva 取食生长；pupa 停止取食并重建身体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin pupa 'doll' was reused by Linnaeus, so the scientific sense is a deliberate borrowing.
normal.cn: 拉丁 pupa「玩偶」被林奈改用，科学义是有意的借用。

normal.en: The family runs pupa, pupae, pupal, pupate, pupation and puparium.
normal.cn: 词族包括 pupa、pupae、pupal、pupate、pupation 与 puparium。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: pupa stage, butterfly pupa, emerge from the pupa.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：蛹期、蝶蛹、从蛹中羽化。

normal.en: Latin first declension gives the plural pupae, parallel to larvae.
normal.cn: 拉丁第一变格法给出复数 pupae，与 larvae 同理。

normal.en: Pupa, puppet and pupil all descend from the same Latin domestic words.
normal.cn: pupa、puppet 与 pupil 都出自同一批拉丁家庭词汇。

abstract.en: Picture a locked room where a body is rebuilt in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一间上锁的屋子，一具身体在黑暗中重建。

abstract.en: Picture a doll that will one day walk away on its own.
abstract.cn: 想象一个玩偶，有一天会自己走开。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase that opens into a winged traveller.
abstract.cn: 想象一只行李箱打开后成为一个有翅的旅人。

examples.en: The pupa does not feed; it only waits while its tissues reorganise.
examples.cn: 蛹不取食，只是等待组织重组。

examples.en: Moth pupae are usually hidden inside a silk cocoon on the ground.
examples.cn: 蛾蛹通常藏在地面的丝茧里。

examples.en: The lab records the duration of each pupa at two temperatures.
examples.cn: 实验室记录每头蛹在两种温度下的持续时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pupa（普帕）」——包在壳里、像玩偶一样不动的阶段 → 蛹

root: 拉丁 pupa「女孩、玩偶」（pupus「男孩」）；林奈 18 世纪改用为昆虫的静止阶段。pupa 的拉丁语之前来源不确定；puppet、pupil 由同一拉丁词族经不同路径借入，属远亲而非同义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses take a doll's name into biology: a resting rebuilt body, a butterfly case, the body inside the shell, the contents of a cocoon, a look-alike stage, a metaphor of dormancy, the Latin doll and a counted unit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把一个玩偶之名带入生物学：静止重建的身体、蝶蛹、壳内的蛹体、茧中之物、似蛹的阶段、蛰伏的比喻、拉丁的玩偶义，以及可计数的单位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard brown case hanging from a leaf stalk, with a folded body rebuilding inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚坚硬的褐色外壳挂在叶柄上，里面有一具折叠的身体正在重建。

branches.en: THE NAME: a Latin doll word became the label for a stage.
branches.cn: 名字：一个拉丁玩偶词成了阶段的标签。

branches.en: THE CASE AND THE BODY: the shell and the animal inside are distinct, which is why puparium has its own name.
branches.cn: 壳与体：外壳与里面的动物彼此不同，puparium 因此另有其名。

branches.en: OTHER COVERINGS: a cocoon wraps it, and some groups imitate the stage without being it.
branches.cn: 其它包被：茧把它包住，有些类群只是形似而非真蛹。

branches.en: STILLNESS BEFORE FLIGHT: the closed quiet state becomes a metaphor for waiting.
branches.cn: 飞行之前的静止：封闭安静的状态成为等待的比喻。

branches.en: COUNTED UNIT: laboratory practice turns the animal into a number.
branches.cn: 可数单位：实验室实践把动物变成一个数。

intro.en: Pupa is a Latin noun; English forms the verb pupate and the nouns pupation and puparium, while pupal is the relational adjective.
intro.cn: pupa 是拉丁名词；英语构成动词 pupate 与名词 pupation、puparium，pupal 则是关系形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pupa, plural pupae, gives pupal, pupate, pupation and puparium; puppet and pupil come from the same domestic root by other routes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pupa（复数 pupae）衍生 pupal、pupate、pupation、puparium；puppet 与 pupil 经别的路径出自同一家庭词根。

items.example: The pupa hangs from a twig.
items.exampleCN: 蛹挂在细枝上。

items.example: Fifty pupae were kept at constant heat.
items.exampleCN: 五十头蛹被置于恒温。

items.example: Pupal colour often matches the surface.
items.exampleCN: 蛹的颜色常与背景一致。

items.example: The larva pupates in the soil.
items.exampleCN: 幼虫在土中化蛹。

items.meaning: the act of becoming a pupa
items.example: Pupation begins after the last moult.
items.exampleCN: 最后一次蜕皮之后开始化蛹。

items.meaning: the hardened larval skin around a fly pupa
items.example: The fly emerged from its puparium.
items.exampleCN: 那只蝇从蛹壳中钻出。

items.meaning: producing young at the pupal stage
items.example: Pupiparous flies give birth to a ready larva.
items.exampleCN: 蛹生蝇类直接产下即将化蛹的幼虫。

items.example: The pupigerous cell was sealed with wax.
items.exampleCN: 带蛹的巢房被蜡封住。

latinEntries.meaning: little girl; pupil of the eye

definition_zh: 蛹的；蛹期的；蛹壳的；蛹室的；蛹体发育的；蛹期蜕皮的；蛰伏静止的（比喻）；寄生于蛹的
definition_en: relating to a pupa or to the stage between larva and adult, when an insect stops feeding and its body is rebuilt inside a case
core_image: 土室里裂开一枚蛹壳，旁边还留着幼虫蜕下的干皮，翅已在壳内折好
scene: 土室中，一枚蛹壳裂开，旁边留着幼虫蜕下的干皮。A pupal case lies split in the soil chamber beside the larva's shed skin.
sceneCN: 这里 pupal 指「与蛹、蛹壳有关的」（第 3 个义项：蛹壳的）；句意为土室中的蛹壳裂开，旁边留着幼虫蜕下的皮。可辨识物件：裂开的蛹壳、干皮、土室壁、折好的翅。

senses.title: Of or belonging to a pupa
senses.definition: relating to a pupa, the stage between larva and adult in complete metamorphosis
senses.definitionCN: 与蛹有关，即完全变态中幼虫与成虫之间的阶段
senses.example: The pupal skin hardens within a day of formation.
senses.exampleCN: 蛹的皮在形成后一天之内变硬。
senses.why: The suffix -al makes a plain relational adjective, so pupal answers the question 'which stage?' rather than describing a quality.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 构成纯粹的关系形容词，因此 pupal 回答的是「哪个阶段」，而非描述某种性质。

senses.title: The interval before adulthood
senses.titleCN: 化蛹到羽化之间的时段
senses.definition: the period during which the insect does not feed and its tissues are reorganised
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫不取食、组织被重组的那段时间
senses.example: Pupal duration depends strongly on temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 蛹期的长短高度依赖温度。
senses.why: This sense measures time, and in rearing records it is a number of days rather than a description.
senses.whyCN: 这一义度量时间，在饲养记录中是一串天数而非描述。

senses.title: The hardened case
senses.definition: the protective outer case of the pupa, including the hardened last larval skin of many flies
senses.definitionCN: 蛹的保护性外壳，包括许多蝇类硬化后的末龄幼虫皮
senses.example: A pupal case lies split in the soil chamber beside the larva's shed skin.
senses.exampleCN: 土室中的蛹壳裂开，旁边留着幼虫蜕下的皮。
senses.why: The case is not the animal; distinguishing them matters because fly puparia are modified larval skins.
senses.whyCN: 壳不是动物本身；区分两者很重要，因为蝇类的蛹壳是改造过的幼虫皮。

senses.title: The chamber built for pupation
senses.definition: the cavity or cell an insect prepares for pupation, in soil, wood or a silk shelter
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫为化蛹准备的腔室或巢房，可在土中、木内或丝质庇护所里
senses.example: The beetle excavated a pupal chamber beneath the bark.
senses.exampleCN: 甲虫在树皮下挖出一个蛹室。
senses.why: This sense attaches the adjective to a place, a common pattern in ecology and behaviour studies.
senses.whyCN: 这一义把形容词挂到地点上，是生态与行为研究中常见的模式。

senses.title: Development inside the case
senses.definition: the internal growth and differentiation that turns larval tissue into adult structures
senses.definitionCN: 把幼虫组织转变为成虫结构的内部生长与分化
senses.example: Pupal development reconstructs the wings and eyes entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 蛹期发育把翅与眼完全重建。
senses.why: The phrase pupal development names a process, not an object, and it is the sense used in physiology.
senses.whyCN: 「pupal development」指一个过程而非物件，是生理学中使用的义。

senses.title: The pupal moult
senses.definition: the shedding of the last larval skin that produces the pupa, or the moult that releases the adult
senses.definitionCN: 产生蛹时蜕去末龄幼虫皮，或羽化时进行的那次蜕皮
senses.example: The pupal moult leaves a dry skin beside the case.
senses.exampleCN: 蛹期蜕皮在壳旁留下了一张干皮。
senses.why: Moulting bookends the stage, so the adjective can mark either the entry or the exit.
senses.whyCN: 蜕皮在这一阶段的两端，因此形容词既可指进入也可指离开。

senses.title: A dormant, waiting state
senses.definition: used figuratively for a quiet interval in which something is being remade before it reappears
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指某物在重新出现之前被改造的安静间歇
senses.example: The old factory spent a pupal winter and reopened as a studio.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧工厂度过了一个「蛹期」的冬天，重新开张时成了工作室。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the stillness and the promise of emergence, which is why it suits institutions as well as insects.
senses.whyCN: 比喻保留了静止与将要羽化的许诺，因此既适用于机构也适用于昆虫。

senses.title: Living on a pupa
senses.definition: describing a parasitoid that attacks the pupal stage and emerges from it
senses.definitionCN: 描述攻击蛹期并从蛹中出来的寄生蜂或寄生昆虫
senses.example: A pupal parasitoid emerged from the moth's case in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蛹寄生蜂在春天从蛾蛹壳中钻出。
senses.why: This technical sense narrows the adjective to a host stage, a standard usage in biological control.
senses.whyCN: 这一技术义把形容词收窄到寄主阶段，是生物防治中的标准用法。

intro.en: Pupal is pupa plus the relational suffix -al. The base noun is Latin pupa 'girl, doll', which Linnaeus reused for the insect stage.
intro.cn: pupal 由 pupa 加关系后缀 -al 构成。基名词是拉丁 pupa「女孩、玩偶」，林奈改用于昆虫阶段。

items.en: Latin pupa meant a doll or a girl; the entomological sense came only in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 拉丁 pupa 指玩偶或女孩；昆虫学义到 18 世纪才出现。

items.en: Latin -alis became English -al and forms relational adjectives from nouns, as in fate and fatal or nation and national.
items.cn: 拉丁 -alis 变成英语 -al，从名词构成关系形容词，如 fate 与 fatal、nation 与 national。

items.en: Pupal was coined in English on this pattern inside natural-history writing, not borrowed as a whole word from Latin.
items.cn: pupal 是英语在自然史写作中按这一模式新造的，并非整词借自拉丁。

items.en: Entomology uses pupal for stage, case, chamber and development, so one adjective covers time, object, place and process.
items.cn: 昆虫学把 pupal 用于阶段、壳、室与发育，一个形容词覆盖时间、物件、地点与过程。

items.en: Biological control writes of pupal parasitoids, and laboratory protocols write of pupal duration, extending the word beyond description.
items.cn: 生物防治写「pupal parasitoid」，实验室方案写「pupal duration」，把词扩展到描述之外。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the deeper origin and the exact first citation are not settled, so any pre-Latin form offered here is a reconstruction and competing hypotheses are left side by side.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：更深的来源与确切最早书证均无定论，此处给出的拉丁语之前形式属重构形式，并列假说一并保留、不作定论。

note.en: Group one separates pupal from the noun and from look-alike words; group two lists adjectives for neighbouring stages.
note.cn: 第一组把 pupal 与名词及形近词分开；第二组列出相邻阶段的形容词。

entries.definition: Pupa names the animal; pupal describes it, so the two are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: pupa 指动物；pupal 描述它，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: Pupae is a plural noun, not an adjective, and cannot modify stage or case.
entries.definitionCN: pupae 是复数名词，不是形容词，不能修饰 stage 或 case。

entries.definition: Pupil sounds identical but means a student or the eye's opening, from a different branch of the same Latin family.
entries.definitionCN: pupil 读音相同，却指学生或瞳孔，出自同一拉丁词族的另一分支。

entries.definition: Puppet shares the doll ancestor but has no biological sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: puppet 共享玩偶这一祖先，却完全没有生物学义。

entries.definition: Larval marks the feeding, growing stage that precedes the pupa.
entries.definitionCN: larval 标出蛹之前取食、生长的阶段。

entries.definition: Nymphal describes the young of insects that have no pupal stage at all.
entries.definitionCN: nymphal 描述完全没有蛹期的不完全变态昆虫幼期。

entries.definition: Chrysalid is a rare adjective for the butterfly's uncovered pupal case.
entries.definitionCN: chrysalid 是描述蝴蝶裸露蛹壳的罕见形容词。

entries.definition: Dormant is the general word for an inactive period, which pupal only implies.
entries.definitionCN: dormant 是一般的「不活动」说法，pupal 只暗含这一层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Pupa plus -al gives the relational adjective, the same pattern as fate and fatal.
normal.cn: pupa 加 -al 构成关系形容词，与 fate / fatal 同一模式。

normal.en: The family runs pupa, pupae, pupal, pupate, pupation and puparium.
normal.cn: 词族包括 pupa、pupae、pupal、pupate、pupation 与 puparium。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: pupal stage, pupal case, pupal chamber.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：蛹期、蛹壳、蛹室。

normal.en: The adjective covers time, shell, place and process, four different questions.
normal.cn: 这个形容词覆盖时间、外壳、地点与过程四类不同问题。

normal.en: Do not confuse pupal with pupil: one is a stage, the other a student or an eye.
normal.cn: 别把 pupal 与 pupil 混淆：一个是阶段，一个是学生或瞳孔。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed workshop where the old body is taken apart.
abstract.cn: 想象一间封闭的工场，旧身体正在被拆开。

abstract.en: Picture a dry skin left on the floor like a receipt for the change.
abstract.cn: 想象一张干皮留在地上，像这场变化的收据。

abstract.en: Picture a factory that goes quiet for one winter and reopens as something else.
abstract.cn: 想象一座工厂静默一个冬天，再开时已换了个模样。

examples.en: Pupal colour often matches the bark so the case is hard to see.
examples.cn: 蛹的颜色常与树皮一致，使蛹壳很难被发现。

examples.en: The wasp searches for a pupal host beneath the leaf litter.
examples.cn: 这种蜂在落叶层下寻找蛹期寄主。

examples.en: Pupal duration fell by three days when the rearing room was warmed.
examples.cn: 饲养室升温后，蛹期缩短了三天。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pupal（普泡）」——泡在壳里不动的阶段 → 蛹的

root: pupa（拉丁「女孩、玩偶」，林奈改用为蛹）+ 关系后缀 -al（拉丁 -alis）。属英语在拉丁词基上构成的形容词。pupa 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply the adjective to the animal, the interval, the shell, the chamber, the inner development, the moult, a metaphor of dormancy and a parasitoid's host stage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把形容词用于动物、时段、外壳、蛹室、内部发育、蜕皮、蛰伏比喻，以及寄生者的寄主阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a split case in a soil chamber, a shed larval skin beside it and folded wings inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：土室中裂开的蛹壳，旁边是蜕下的幼虫皮，壳内是折好的翅。

branches.en: PLAIN RELATION: the suffix asks only which stage is meant.
branches.cn: 纯粹关系：后缀只问指的是哪个阶段。

branches.en: TIME AND PROCESS: duration, inner rebuilding and the moult all describe a remaking that takes time.
branches.cn: 时间与过程：时长、内部重建与蜕皮都描述一段耗时的改造。

branches.en: CASE AND PLACE: the shell protects and the chamber hides.
branches.cn: 壳与地点：外壳保护，蛹室隐藏。

branches.en: DORMANCY: the quiet interval becomes a metaphor for reinvention.
branches.cn: 蛰伏：安静的间歇成为再造的比喻。

branches.en: HOST STAGE: another insect uses the pupa as food.
branches.cn: 寄主阶段：另一种昆虫把蛹当作食物。

intro.en: Pupal is the relational adjective of pupa; the family's other members add -ate, -ation, -arium and -parous to the same stem.
intro.cn: pupal 是 pupa 的关系形容词；词族其它成员在同一词干上加 -ate、-ation、-arium 与 -parous。

latinIntro.en: Latin pupa and its plural pupae supply pup-, which English extends with -al, -ate, -ation, -arium and -gerous.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pupa 及其复数 pupae 提供词干 pup-，英语用 -al、-ate、-ation、-arium、-gerous 扩展。

items.example: The pupal case is hard and dry.
items.exampleCN: 蛹壳坚硬干燥。

items.example: The pupa does not move.
items.exampleCN: 蛹不活动。

items.example: Larvae pupate in autumn.
items.exampleCN: 幼虫在秋天化蛹。

items.example: Pupation lasts a single night.
items.exampleCN: 化蛹只持续一夜。

items.example: The puparium split along its top.
items.exampleCN: 蛹壳沿顶部裂开。

items.example: The pupigerous cell was capped.
items.exampleCN: 带蛹的巢房已封盖。

items.example: Pupiparous flies avoid the larval stage.
items.exampleCN: 蛹生蝇类跳过幼虫阶段。

items.example: The species overwinters pupally.
items.exampleCN: 该物种以蛹越冬。

definition_zh: 变态（昆虫由幼体到成体的形态剧变）；完全变态；不完全变态；岩石的变质作用（地质学旧用）；彻底的形态改变；神话与文学中的变形；组织或制度的转型；医学上组织的变性
definition_en: a complete change of form, especially the biological process in which an insect or amphibian changes from its young stage into its adult shape
core_image: 饲养箱里，蛹壳裂开，一对湿翅从皱缩的身体中缓缓展开
scene: 饲养箱里，蛹壳裂开，一对湿翅从皱缩的身体中展开。After weeks in the case, metamorphosis ends with wet wings opening in the rearing box.
sceneCN: 这里 metamorphosis 指「昆虫由幼体到成体的形态剧变」（第 1 个义项：变态）；句意为在壳中待了数周之后，变态以一对湿翅在饲养箱里展开而告终。可辨识物件：裂开的壳、湿翅、皱缩的身体、饲养箱。

pos.zh: 变态；变形；彻底改变；地质学上的变质作用

senses.title: The change from young to adult form
senses.titleCN: 由幼体到成体的形态剧变
senses.definition: the biological process in which an animal's body is rebuilt from the young form into the adult form
senses.definitionCN: 动物的身体由幼体形态被重建为成体形态的生物过程
senses.example: After weeks in the case, metamorphosis ends with wet wings opening in the rearing box.
senses.exampleCN: 在壳中待了数周之后，变态以一对湿翅在饲养箱里展开而告终。
senses.why: The Greek word means a change of form, and biology narrowed it to the radical rebuilding that separates a larva from an adult.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词意为形态的改变，生物学把它收窄为把幼虫与成虫截然分开的那次彻底重建。

senses.title: Complete metamorphosis
senses.definition: the four-stage pattern of egg, larva, pupa and adult, in which the young look nothing like the adult
senses.definitionCN: 卵、幼虫、蛹、成虫四阶段、幼体与成虫外形完全不同的模式
senses.example: Butterflies show complete metamorphosis, with a pupal stage in between.
senses.exampleCN: 蝴蝶行完全变态，中间有一个蛹期。
senses.why: The adjective complete marks the presence of a pupa; without it the change is gradual and the young already resembles the adult.
senses.whyCN: 「complete」标出有蛹期；没有蛹期时变化是渐进的，幼体已形似成虫。

senses.title: Incomplete metamorphosis
senses.definition: the pattern in which a nymph hatches looking like a small adult and grows without a pupal stage
senses.definitionCN: 若虫孵出时已形似小型成虫、没有蛹期而逐渐长大的模式
senses.example: Grasshoppers undergo incomplete metamorphosis and never form a pupa.
senses.exampleCN: 蝗虫行不完全变态，从不形成蛹。
senses.why: Here the change is gradual, so the word applies to a lesser degree of rebuilding and the nymph is not called a larva.
senses.whyCN: 此处变化是渐进的，词所指的是程度较轻的重建，若虫也不称作幼虫。

senses.title: The old geological sense
senses.titleCN: 地质学旧义：岩石的变质作用
senses.definition: the alteration of rock by heat and pressure, a sense used in early geology before metamorphism became the standard term
senses.definitionCN: 岩石在高温高压下发生的改变，早期地质学用法，后来标准术语改为「metamorphism」
senses.example: Early writers spoke of the metamorphosis of limestone into marble.
senses.exampleCN: 早期作者会说石灰岩变质成大理岩。
senses.why: Geology borrowed the biological word for deep change in rock, then replaced it with metamorphism to keep the two fields apart.
senses.whyCN: 地质学借用了生物学词来指岩石的深层改变，后来又改用「metamorphism」以区分两个领域。

senses.title: A total change of shape or character
senses.titleCN: 彻底的形态或性质改变
senses.definition: any radical transformation in appearance, function or character, not necessarily biological
senses.definitionCN: 外观、功能或性质上的任何彻底转变，未必是生物的
senses.example: The old harbour underwent a metamorphosis into a park.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧港经历了蜕变，成了一座公园。
senses.why: The metaphor generalizes the biological rebuilding into any process that leaves something unrecognizable.
senses.whyCN: 比喻把生物性的重建推广到任何使事物面目全非的过程。

senses.title: A tale of transformation
senses.definition: a story in which a person or thing is changed into another form, as in Ovid's poem of that name
senses.definitionCN: 人或物被变成另一形态的故事，如奥维德以此为题的长诗
senses.example: Ovid's Metamorphoses retells myths of transformation.
senses.exampleCN: 奥维德的《变形记》重述了许多变形神话。
senses.why: Literature kept the word close to its Greek sense and used the plural for a collection of such tales.
senses.whyCN: 文学让这个词贴近希腊原义，并用复数指这类故事的合集。

senses.title: An institutional transformation
senses.definition: a thorough restructuring of an organization, economy or system into a different form
senses.definitionCN: 组织、经济或制度被彻底改组为另一种形态
senses.example: The industry's metamorphosis from coal to services took thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个行业从煤炭转向服务业用了三十年。
senses.why: Policy writing borrows the word when the change is structural rather than cosmetic, which is the test the metaphor applies.
senses.whyCN: 政策写作在变化属结构而非表面时借用这个词，这正是比喻所设的判准。

senses.title: A medical distortion of tissue
senses.definition: a pathological change of tissue form, as in the older phrase metamorphosis of a cell
senses.definitionCN: 组织形态的病理性改变，如较早文献中「细胞变性」的说法
senses.example: Nineteenth-century reports describe a metamorphosis of the liver cells.
senses.exampleCN: 19 世纪的报告描述了肝细胞的变性。
senses.why: This clinical sense is largely obsolete, but it shows the word reaching any field where form changes.
senses.whyCN: 这一临床义已基本废弃，却显示这个词进入了任何涉及形态改变的领域。

intro.en: Metamorphosis comes from Greek meta 'change' plus morphē 'form' plus the noun ending -ōsis, literally 'a changing of form'. Latin and English took the whole word.
intro.cn: metamorphosis 来自希腊 meta「改变」加 morphē「形态」，再加名词词尾 -ōsis，字面即「形态的改变」。拉丁语与英语整套借入。

items.en: Meta- meant 'change, beyond, after' and was the standard prefix for transformation in Greek compounds.
items.cn: meta- 意为「改变、超越、之后」，是希腊复合词中表示转变的常用前缀。

items.en: Morphē meant 'form, shape'. It survives in English in morphology, amorphous and polymorphous.
items.cn: morphē 意为「形态、形状」，在英语的 morphology、amorphous、polymorphous 中留存。

items.en: The suffix -ōsis named a process or condition, so the compound named the process of changing form rather than a single shape.
items.cn: 后缀 -ōsis 表示过程或状态，因此这个复合词指形态改变的过程，而非某一形状。

items.en: Ovid's Metamorphoses made the plural famous in literature, and English kept both the singular for the process and the plural for a collection of tales.
items.cn: 奥维德的《变形记》使复数形式在文学中闻名，英语既保留单数指过程，也用复数指故事集。

items.en: Biology applied the word to insect and amphibian development, and the phrase complete metamorphosis fixed the four-stage pattern.
items.cn: 生物学把这个词用于昆虫与两栖类的发育，「complete metamorphosis」一语固定了四阶段模式。

items.en: Geology first borrowed the word for rock alteration and later switched to metamorphism; medicine used it briefly for tissue change before pathologists adopted other terms.
items.cn: 地质学先借这个词指岩石改变，后来改用 metamorphism；医学曾短暂用它指组织改变，之后病理学家采用了别的术语。

note.en: Group one separates the noun from its plural, verb and adjective; group two lists the biological and general words for change that overlap with it.
note.cn: 第一组把名词与复数、动词、形容词分开；第二组列出与之重叠的生物学与一般「变化」词。

entries.definition: Metamorphoses is both the plural of the process and the title of Ovid's poem.
entries.definitionCN: metamorphoses 既是该过程名词的复数，也是奥维德长诗的标题。

entries.definition: Metamorphose means to change into another form, so it supplies the action that the noun names.
entries.definitionCN: metamorphose 意为变成另一形态，提供名词所指的动作。

entries.definition: Metamorphic describes what has been changed, and in geology it names altered rock.
entries.definitionCN: metamorphic 描述已被改变之物，在地质学中指变质岩。

entries.definition: Metamorphism is the geological term for rock alteration, a narrower noun than metamorphosis.
entries.definitionCN: metamorphism 是岩石改变的地质学术语，比 metamorphosis 更窄。

entries.definition: Transformation is the everyday word for any change of form and lacks the biological stage meaning.
entries.definitionCN: transformation 是泛指形态改变的日常词，没有生物学阶段义。

entries.definition: A moult is the shedding of an outer layer, one step within growth, not the whole rebuilding.
entries.definitionCN: moult 指蜕去外层，是生长中的一步，而非整体重建。

entries.definition: Transmutation stresses a change of substance, as in alchemy, rather than of shape.
entries.definitionCN: transmutation 强调物质的改变，如炼金术，而非形态。

entries.definition: Development is the broad word for growth; metamorphosis is one dramatic pattern within it.
entries.definitionCN: development 是生长的宽泛说法；metamorphosis 是其中一种剧烈的模式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek meta 'change' plus morphē 'form' gives the literal meaning 'change of form'.
normal.cn: 希腊 meta「改变」加 morphē「形态」，字面即「形态的改变」。

normal.en: The family runs metamorphosis, metamorphoses, metamorphose, metamorphic and metamorphism.
normal.cn: 词族包括 metamorphosis、metamorphoses、metamorphose、metamorphic 与 metamorphism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: complete metamorphosis, undergo metamorphosis, insect metamorphosis.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：完全变态、经历变态、昆虫变态。

normal.en: The plural metamorphoses follows the Greek -sis to -ses pattern.
normal.cn: 复数 metamorphoses 遵循希腊语 -sis 变 -ses 的模式。

normal.en: Ovid's Metamorphoses is the literary home of the plural form.
normal.cn: 奥维德的《变形记》是这一复数形式的文学家园。

abstract.en: Picture a body dissolved and rebuilt inside a sealed room.
abstract.cn: 想象一具身体在密闭的屋子里被拆解再重建。

abstract.en: Picture a harbour that wakes up as a garden.
abstract.cn: 想象一座港口醒来时变成了花园。

abstract.en: Picture a story in which a person ends as a tree and still remembers.
abstract.cn: 想象一个故事，其中的人最后成了一棵树，却仍记得从前。

examples.en: Complete metamorphosis protects the young and the adult from competing for the same food.
examples.cn: 完全变态使幼体与成虫不必为同一食物竞争。

examples.en: The frog's metamorphosis turns gills into lungs within a few weeks.
examples.cn: 蛙的变态在几周内把鳃变成肺。

examples.en: Ovid's Metamorphoses shaped how European literature imagines transformation.
examples.cn: 奥维德的《变形记》塑造了欧洲文学想象变形的方式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「meta（变）+ morph（形）」——形态整个换掉 → 变态、蜕变

root: 希腊 meta-「改变」+ morphē「形态」+ -ōsis（过程名词词尾），字面「形态的改变」。经拉丁进入英语；复数 metamorphoses 循希腊语 -sis/-ses 模式。地质学旧用后改称 metamorphism。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one word from a biological rebuilding to its complete and incomplete patterns, an old geological use, a general transformation, literary tales, institutional change and an obsolete medical sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一个词从生物性重建走到完全与不完全两种模式、旧的地质用法、一般转变、文学故事、制度变革，以及一个已废弃的医学义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed case splitting open while folded wings unfold into a shape that was never there before.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚封闭的壳裂开，折叠的翅展开成此前从未存在的形状。

branches.en: THE BIOLOGICAL CORE: a body rebuilt from young to adult.
branches.cn: 生物核心：身体由幼体被重建为成体。

branches.en: TWO PATTERNS: a pupa inside the change, or a nymph growing without one.
branches.cn: 两种模式：变化中含蛹，或若虫不经蛹而长大。

branches.en: ROCK: early geology borrowed the word, then narrowed it to metamorphism.
branches.cn: 岩石：早期地质学借用了这个词，后来收窄为 metamorphism。

branches.en: GENERAL AND INSTITUTIONAL: any change that leaves the thing unrecognizable.
branches.cn: 一般与制度：任何使事物面目全非的改变。

branches.en: STORIES AND CLINICS: myth and early medicine extend the word to bodies that change or distort.
branches.cn: 故事与临床：神话与早期医学把词扩展到变形或病变的身体。

intro.en: Metamorphosis is a Greek compound; its family is built from meta-, morph- and the suffixes -osis, -ic and -ism, all of which English still uses productively.
intro.cn: metamorphosis 是希腊复合词；词族由 meta-、morph- 与后缀 -osis、-ic、-ism 构成，这些成分英语至今仍在活用。

latinIntro.en: Greek meta- 'change' and morphē 'form' also give amorphous, polymorphous and morphology; Latin metamorphosis is a straight borrowing of the Greek noun.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 meta-「改变」与 morphē「形态」也构成 amorphous、polymorphous、morphology；拉丁 metamorphosis 是对希腊名词的直接借入。

items.example: The prefix announces a transformation.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀宣告一次转变。

items.example: The root supplies the shape that changes.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供被改变的形态。

items.example: Metamorphosis reshapes the whole body.
items.exampleCN: 变态重塑整个身体。

items.example: The larva metamorphoses into a moth.
items.exampleCN: 幼虫变态成蛾。

items.meaning: changed in form; of altered rock
items.example: Metamorphic rock records great heat.
items.exampleCN: 变质岩记录着高温。

items.example: Metamorphism folded the beds.
items.exampleCN: 变质作用使岩层褶皱。

items.example: Glass is amorphous rather than crystalline.
items.exampleCN: 玻璃是无定形的，而非晶质的。

items.example: The species is polymorphous in colour.
items.exampleCN: 这个物种在体色上多形。

items.example: Insect morphology explains the stages.
items.exampleCN: 昆虫形态学解释了这些阶段。

definition_zh: 变质岩的；变质作用的（岩石在高温高压下改变结构）；变质程度的；变质矿物的；变质带的；变态的（生物学，罕用）；发生彻底改变的（比喻）；接触变质晕的
definition_en: relating to rock that has been altered by heat and pressure, or more rarely to the biological process of changing form
core_image: 采石场的岩壁上，原来的水平层理被压成波状褶皱，云母片在光下闪出一层银亮
scene: 采石场的岩壁上，原来的层理被压成波状褶皱。In the quarry wall, metamorphic rock has been folded until the old bedding waves.
sceneCN: 这里 metamorphic 指「经高温高压而改变结构与矿物组成的岩石」（第 1 个义项：变质岩的）；句意为采石场岩壁上的变质岩被压成波状褶皱，原有层理不再平直。可辨识物件：波状层理、云母闪光、采石场岩壁、褶皱。

pos.zh: 变质岩的；变质作用的；变态的（罕用）；彻底改变的

senses.title: Rock altered by heat and pressure
senses.titleCN: 经高温高压改变的岩石
senses.definition: describing rock whose minerals and texture have been changed by heat, pressure or hot fluids
senses.definitionCN: 矿物与结构因热、压力或热液而改变的岩石
senses.example: In the quarry wall, metamorphic rock has been folded until the old bedding waves.
senses.exampleCN: 采石场岩壁上的变质岩被压成波状褶皱，原有层理不再平直。
senses.why: The adjective marks a origin: the rock was once something else, and heat or pressure rewrote its minerals.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标出来历：岩石原本是别的东西，热或压力改写了它的矿物。

senses.title: The process of alteration
senses.definition: relating to the process by which such change occurs, as in metamorphic processes at depth
senses.definitionCN: 与这种改变发生的过程有关，如深部的变质过程
senses.example: Metamorphic processes at depth recrystallise limestone into marble.
senses.exampleCN: 深部的变质过程把石灰岩重结晶为大理岩。
senses.why: Here the adjective attaches to the process rather than the product, a distinction geologists keep carefully.
senses.whyCN: 此处形容词附于过程而非产物，地质学家严格区分这两者。

senses.title: A grade or intensity of change
senses.definition: describing the level of alteration, from low grade to high grade, as shown by index minerals
senses.definitionCN: 描述改变的等级，从低级到高级，由指示矿物显示
senses.example: The metamorphic grade rises toward the granite contact.
senses.exampleCN: 越靠近花岗岩接触带，变质程度越高。
senses.why: Grade turns the adjective into a scale, so one rock can be more metamorphic than another.
senses.whyCN: 程度把这个形容词变成一把标尺，因此一块岩石可以比另一块更变质。

senses.title: Minerals produced by alteration
senses.definition: describing minerals that grow during alteration, such as garnet, staurolite or kyanite
senses.definitionCN: 在变质过程中生长的矿物，如石榴石、十字石或蓝晶石
senses.example: Garnet is a metamorphic mineral in this schist.
senses.exampleCN: 石榴石是这片片岩中的变质矿物。
senses.why: Index minerals let geologists read temperature and pressure from a hand sample.
senses.whyCN: 指示矿物让地质学家能从一块手标本读出温度与压力。

senses.title: A belt or zone of altered rock
senses.definition: describing a mapped region where rocks share a history of alteration, as in a metamorphic belt
senses.definitionCN: 描述一片岩石共享变质历史的填图区域，如变质带
senses.example: The metamorphic belt runs along the old continental edge.
senses.exampleCN: 这条变质带沿古老的陆缘延伸。
senses.why: Mapping turns the adjective into a spatial label, which is how regional geology is organized.
senses.whyCN: 填图把这个形容词变成空间标签，区域地质即以此组织。

senses.title: The contact aureole
senses.definition: describing the zone around an intrusion where heat altered the surrounding rock
senses.definitionCN: 描述侵入体周围受热改变的那一圈围岩
senses.example: The metamorphic aureole around the granite is only a few metres wide.
senses.exampleCN: 花岗岩周围的接触变质晕只有几米宽。
senses.why: The aureole records a local heat source, so the adjective points to a cause as well as a result.
senses.whyCN: 变质晕记录了局部的热源，形容词因此既指结果也指原因。

senses.title: Biological change of form
senses.definition: a rare biological use meaning 'of or showing metamorphosis', mostly replaced by the noun and verb
senses.definitionCN: 罕见的生物学用法，意为「变态的」，多被名词与动词取代
senses.example: Older texts call the pupal stage a metamorphic phase.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的文献把蛹期称为变态阶段。
senses.why: Geology took over the adjective, so the biological sense survives mostly in older writing.
senses.whyCN: 地质学占用了这个形容词，生物义因此主要残存在较早的写作中。

senses.title: Thoroughly transformed
senses.definition: used figuratively for something changed so deeply that its earlier state is hard to recognize
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指被改变得极深、以致早期状态难以辨认的事物
senses.example: The metamorphic economy of the town no longer resembles its mining past.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇蜕变后的经济已看不出采矿业时期的模样。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the geologists' idea of a rock rewritten from within, not merely repainted.
senses.whyCN: 比喻借用地质学家「岩石从内部被改写」的想法，而非仅仅重新刷漆。

intro.en: Metamorphic is meta- 'change' plus morphē 'form' plus -ic 'relating to', the adjective partner of metamorphosis. Geology adopted it in the nineteenth century for altered rock.
intro.cn: metamorphic 是 meta-「改变」加 morphē「形态」再加 -ic「与……有关的」，是 metamorphosis 的形容词伙伴。地质学在 19 世纪把它用于变质岩。

items.en: Meta- meant 'change, beyond' and morphē meant 'form'; the two already combined in Greek to name transformation.
items.cn: meta- 意为「改变、超越」，morphē 意为「形态」；两者在希腊语中已组合表示变形。

items.en: The suffix -ic, from Greek -ikos, means 'relating to', so metamorphic says 'pertaining to a change of form'.
items.cn: -ic 后缀出自希腊 -ikos，意为「与……有关」，因此 metamorphic 表示「与形态改变有关的」。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geology needed a word for rock whose minerals had been recrystallised, and metamorphic filled the gap alongside metamorphism.
items.cn: 19 世纪地质学需要一个词来描述矿物已重结晶的岩石，metamorphic 与 metamorphism 一同补上这个空缺。

items.en: The adjective became standard in phrases such as metamorphic rock, metamorphic grade and metamorphic facies, which now dominate all usage.
items.cn: 这个形容词在「metamorphic rock」「metamorphic grade」「metamorphic facies」等短语中成为标准，如今主导全部用法。

items.en: The older biological sense survives in a few phrases such as metamorphic phase, but the noun and verb carry that meaning today.
items.cn: 较早的生物义残存在「metamorphic phase」这类短语里，今天该意义由名词与动词承担。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and attribution): the exact first geological use and the writer who fixed the term are not settled, so no single citation should be treated as definitive.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与归属）：最早的地质学用法与确立该术语的作者均无定论，不应把某一条书证当作定论。

note.en: Group one separates metamorphic from the noun, verb and similar-looking words; group two lists the rock-class words it is contrasted with.
note.cn: 第一组把 metamorphic 与名词、动词及形近词分开；第二组列出与它对照的岩石分类词。

entries.definition: Metamorphosis is the process; metamorphic describes what the process produced.
entries.definitionCN: metamorphosis 是过程；metamorphic 描述该过程的产物。

entries.definition: Metamorphose is the action, so it cannot replace the adjective before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: metamorphose 是动作，不能替代名词前的形容词。

entries.definition: Metamorphism names the geological process, a narrower noun than metamorphosis.
entries.definitionCN: metamorphism 指地质过程，是比 metamorphosis 更窄的名词。

entries.definition: Metaphoric comes from metaphor and Greek pherein 'to carry', so it is not related to form at all.
entries.definitionCN: metaphoric 出自 metaphor 与希腊 pherein「携带」，与形态无关。

entries.definition: Igneous rock solidified from melt, so heat made it but did not alter an earlier rock.
entries.definitionCN: igneous 指由熔体凝固的岩石，热产生了它，却没有改造先前的岩石。

entries.definition: Sedimentary rock formed from deposited material; metamorphic rock may have started as sediment and been rewritten.
entries.definitionCN: sedimentary 由沉积物形成；变质岩可能原本就是沉积物，之后被改写。

entries.definition: Recrystallised describes the mineral change itself, the mechanism behind a metamorphic texture.
entries.definitionCN: recrystallised 描述矿物改变本身，是变质结构背后的机制。

entries.definition: Altered is the general word for any change and lacks the specific pressure-and-heat meaning.
entries.definitionCN: altered 是泛指改变，不含特定的高温高压义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Meta- 'change' plus morph- 'form' plus -ic 'relating to' gives the meaning directly.
normal.cn: meta-「改变」加 morph-「形态」加 -ic「与……有关」，意义直接可得。

normal.en: The family runs metamorphosis, metamorphose, metamorphic and metamorphism.
normal.cn: 词族包括 metamorphosis、metamorphose、metamorphic 与 metamorphism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: metamorphic rock, metamorphic grade, metamorphic facies.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：变质岩、变质程度、变质相。

normal.en: The three rock classes are igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic.
normal.cn: 三大岩石类别是岩浆岩、沉积岩与变质岩。

normal.en: A metamorphic rock was something else first; that is the whole point of the word.
normal.cn: 变质岩原本是别的东西，这正是这个词的全部要点。

abstract.en: Picture a limestone bed squeezed until its grains lock into a new mosaic.
abstract.cn: 想象一层石灰岩被挤压，直到颗粒嵌成新的镶嵌。

abstract.en: Picture a letter rewritten so often that only the handwriting is the same.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信被反复改写，只剩笔迹还是原来的。

abstract.en: Picture a town whose mine closes and whose streets fill with studios.
abstract.cn: 想象一座小镇矿井关闭，街道上开满了工作室。

examples.en: Metamorphic rock around the intrusion contains garnet and staurolite.
examples.cn: 侵入体周围的变质岩含石榴石与十字石。

examples.en: The map divides the region into three metamorphic belts.
examples.cn: 地图把该地区划分为三条变质带。

examples.en: Marble is metamorphic limestone, recrystallised under pressure.
examples.cn: 大理岩是受压重结晶的变质石灰岩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「meta（变）+ morph（形）+ ic」——形态被改过的 → 变质岩的

root: 希腊 meta-「改变」+ morphē「形态」+ -ic「与……有关的」，是 metamorphosis 的形容词形式。19 世纪地质学采用为「变质岩的」。最早地质学用法与确立者无定论，属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses take the adjective through altered rock, the altering process, its grade, its index minerals, its mapped belts, its contact aureole, a rare biological use and a general metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让这个形容词经过变质岩、变质过程、变质程度、指示矿物、填图变质带、接触变质晕、罕见的生物义与一般比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a once-flat limestone bed folded into waves, its grains grown into a new sparkling mosaic.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层原本平整的石灰岩被压成波状，颗粒长成新的闪光镶嵌。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT: rock that was something else before.
branches.cn: 产物：此前是别的东西的岩石。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: heat, pressure and fluids do the rewriting.
branches.cn: 过程：热、压力与流体完成改写。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: grade and index minerals turn the adjective into a thermometer.
branches.cn: 度量：变质程度与指示矿物把形容词变成温度计。

branches.en: SPACE: belts map the history and aureoles mark a local heat source.
branches.cn: 空间：变质带勾勒历史，变质晕标出局部热源。

branches.en: OUTSIDE GEOLOGY: a rare biological use and a metaphor for deep change.
branches.cn: 地质学之外：罕见的生物义与深层改变的比喻。

intro.en: Metamorphic is built from Greek meta-, morphē and the suffix -ic; the same elements form metamorphosis, metamorphism and many technical compounds.
intro.cn: metamorphic 由希腊 meta-、morphē 与后缀 -ic 构成；同一批成分也构成 metamorphosis、metamorphism 与许多技术复合词。

latinIntro.en: Greek meta- and morphē give metamorphosis, metamorphic, metamorphism and amorphous; -ic marks the relational adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 meta- 与 morphē 构成 metamorphosis、metamorphic、metamorphism 与 amorphous；-ic 标出关系形容词。

items.example: The prefix signals transformation.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示转变。

items.example: The root names what is altered.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指明被改变的东西。

items.example: Metamorphic rock is folded here.
items.exampleCN: 这里的变质岩发生褶皱。

items.example: Metamorphism erased the fossils.
items.exampleCN: 变质作用抹去了化石。

items.example: Pressure metamorphosed the shale.
items.exampleCN: 压力使页岩变质。

items.example: The insect completes metamorphosis.
items.exampleCN: 这种昆虫完成变态。

items.example: Metasedimentary layers still show bedding.
items.exampleCN: 变质沉积层仍显示层理。

items.example: Metavolcanic rocks underlie the valley.
items.exampleCN: 谷底之下是变质火山岩。

items.example: Metamorphopsia makes straight lines bend.
items.exampleCN: 视物变形症让直线变弯。

definition_zh: 外骨骼；节肢动物体表起支撑与保护作用的硬壳；几丁质表皮本身；甲壳类与贝类的钙质外壳；蜕下的旧壳；化石中的外骨骼；可穿戴的机械外骨骼；建筑或器械的外部承力骨架（比喻）
definition_en: a hard outer covering that supports and protects the body of an arthropod or other invertebrate, lying outside the soft tissues
core_image: 潮间带的石头上，一只蟹抬起青灰色的硬壳，关节间露出薄薄的软膜
scene: 潮间带的石头上，一只蟹抬起硬壳，关节间露出薄薄的软膜。On the tidal rock, a crab lifts its hard exoskeleton on thin flexible joints.
sceneCN: 这里 exoskeleton 指「节肢动物体表起支撑与保护作用的硬壳」（第 1 个义项：外骨骼）；句意为潮间带石头上的一只蟹抬起硬壳，关节处只留薄膜相连。可辨识物件：青灰硬壳、关节薄膜、石面、蟹步足。

pos.zh: 外骨骼；甲壳；外部承力骨架

senses.title: A hard outer support
senses.titleCN: 起支撑与保护作用的外部硬壳
senses.definition: a rigid outer covering that gives the body shape and protection while the muscles attach inside it
senses.definitionCN: 坚硬的包被，为身体定形并提供保护，肌肉在其内侧附着
senses.example: On the tidal rock, a crab lifts its hard exoskeleton on thin flexible joints.
senses.exampleCN: 潮间带的石头上，一只蟹抬起硬壳，关节处只留薄膜相连。
senses.why: The word says where the support lies: outside the soft body, opposite to our own internal frame.
senses.whyCN: 这个词说明了支撑的位置：在柔软身体之外，与我们的内置支架相反。

senses.title: The chitinous cuticle
senses.definition: the layered cuticle of chitin and protein that forms the outer body wall of insects and crustaceans
senses.definitionCN: 由几丁质与蛋白质分层构成、成为昆虫与甲壳类体壁的外层
senses.example: The insect's exoskeleton is a cuticle that must be shed to allow growth.
senses.exampleCN: 昆虫的外骨骼是一层必须蜕去才能生长的表皮。
senses.why: This technical sense identifies the material, not just the function, and it explains why the animal must moult.
senses.whyCN: 这一技术义指出材料而非仅指功能，也解释了动物为何必须蜕皮。

senses.title: A calcareous shell
senses.titleCN: 钙质外壳（甲壳类与贝类）
senses.definition: a shell hardened with calcium carbonate, as in crabs, barnacles or molluscs
senses.definitionCN: 以碳酸钙硬化的外壳，如蟹、藤壶或软体动物
senses.example: Barnacles build a calcareous exoskeleton around themselves.
senses.exampleCN: 藤壶在自己周围造出钙质外壳。
senses.why: Shells are one kind of exoskeleton, but not every shell is an arthropod cuticle, so the words overlap only partly.
senses.whyCN: 壳是外骨骼的一种，但并非所有壳都是节肢动物表皮，两词只是部分重叠。

senses.title: A cast-off outer casing
senses.definition: the old covering left behind after moulting, often found intact and empty
senses.definitionCN: 蜕皮后留下的旧包被，常完整而空心地被发现
senses.example: A dry exoskeleton clung to the reed at the pond edge.
senses.exampleCN: 一具干枯的旧壳粘在池边的芦苇上。
senses.why: This sense focuses on the object rather than the living animal, which matters when ecologists count moults.
senses.whyCN: 这一义聚焦物件而非活体，生态学家清点蜕壳时正需要这个意思。

senses.title: Fossil outer coverings
senses.definition: the preserved outer skeleton of extinct arthropods, often the only part that survives
senses.definitionCN: 已灭绝节肢动物被保存下来的外壳，常是唯一留存的部分
senses.example: Trilobite exoskeletons are common in Cambrian shale.
senses.exampleCN: 三叶虫的外骨骼在寒武纪页岩中很常见。
senses.why: Because the hard part is outside, fossil record is biased toward exoskeletons, a point palaeontology always notes.
senses.whyCN: 由于坚硬部分在体外，化石记录偏向保存外骨骼，古生物学总会强调这一点。

senses.title: A wearable mechanical frame
senses.definition: a powered frame worn outside the body to support or amplify movement
senses.definitionCN: 穿在身体外部、用于支撑或放大动作的动力框架
senses.example: The worker wore an exoskeleton that carried the load to his hips.
senses.exampleCN: 工人穿了一副把重量传到髋部的机械外骨骼。
senses.why: Engineering copied the biological word because the frame, like a shell, carries forces outside the soft body.
senses.whyCN: 工程学仿用了这个生物词，因为框架如外壳一样，在柔软身体之外承担力量。

senses.title: An external load-bearing frame
senses.titleCN: 建筑或器械的外部承力骨架
senses.definition: a structure that carries loads on its outside, as in some towers or vehicle chassis
senses.definitionCN: 在外侧承担荷载的结构，如某些塔架或车辆底盘
senses.example: The tower's exoskeleton of steel tubes takes the wind load.
senses.exampleCN: 这座塔的钢管外骨架承受风荷载。
senses.why: The metaphor moves from animals to structures but keeps the key idea: strength outside, softness inside.
senses.whyCN: 比喻从动物移到结构，却保留了要点：外强内柔。

senses.title: A protective outward manner
senses.definition: a hard outward manner or system that shields something softer inside
senses.definitionCN: 一层坚硬的对外姿态或制度，保护其中较柔软的部分
senses.example: His exoskeleton of rules hid a very anxious man.
senses.exampleCN: 他那层规章的外壳藏着一个极焦虑的人。
senses.why: The metaphor is emotional rather than mechanical: the shell protects but also isolates.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻是情感性的而非机械性的：外壳既保护也隔离。

intro.en: Exoskeleton joins Greek exo- 'outside' to skeleton, from Greek skeletos 'dried up, a mummy'. Nineteenth-century comparative anatomy coined the term to contrast with endoskeleton.
intro.cn: exoskeleton 把希腊 exo-「外面」与 skeleton 组合，后者出自希腊 skeletos「干枯的、木乃伊」。19 世纪比较解剖学造出这个词，与 endoskeleton 对照。

items.en: Exo- meant 'outside, outward' and remains productive in English, as in exoskeleton, exothermic and exoplanet.
items.cn: exo- 意为「外面、向外」，在英语中仍能产词，如 exoskeleton、exothermic、exoplanet。

items.en: Skeleton came from Greek skeletos 'dried up', used of a mummy or a withered body, and only later meant the bony frame.
items.cn: skeleton 出自希腊 skeletos「干枯的」，本用于木乃伊或干瘪的尸体，后来才指骨性支架。

items.en: Nineteenth-century anatomists needed paired terms for internal and external supports, and exoskeleton was formed against the older endoskeleton.
items.cn: 19 世纪解剖学家需要一对表示内外支撑的术语，exoskeleton 是对较早的 endoskeleton 造出的对应词。

items.en: The word was applied to insects, crustaceans and molluscs, and to the cuticle as well as the shell.
items.cn: 这个词被用于昆虫、甲壳类与软体动物，既指外壳也指表皮。

items.en: In the twentieth and twenty-first centuries the term was borrowed for wearable frames and external building structures.
items.cn: 在 20 与 21 世纪，这个词被借用于可穿戴框架与建筑外骨架。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and coiner): the exact first use and whether one anatomist coined both terms together are not settled, so no single attribution should be treated as certain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与首创者）：确切最早的用法、以及是否由同一位解剖学家造出这对术语，均无定论，不应把单一归属当作确定。

note.en: Group one sets exoskeleton against the internal frame and its own derivatives; group two lists the outer coverings that overlap with it.
note.cn: 第一组把 exoskeleton 与内骨骼及自身派生词对照；第二组列出与它语义重叠的外层包被。

entries.definition: An endoskeleton lies inside the soft tissue, as in vertebrates, so the two words name opposite arrangements.
entries.definitionCN: endoskeleton 位于软组织之内，如脊椎动物，两词指相反的布局。

entries.definition: Skeleton is the general word and can mean either arrangement, or a framework of any kind.
entries.definitionCN: skeleton 是通称，可指任一种布局，也可指任何骨架。

entries.definition: Exoskeletal describes what belongs to an outer skeleton and cannot replace the noun.
entries.definitionCN: exoskeletal 描述属外骨骼之物，不能替代名词。

entries.definition: The adverb is rare and mainly appears in technical description, not in general prose.
entries.definitionCN: 这个副词罕见，主要用于技术描述，不用于一般行文。

entries.definition: A shell is a hard outer covering, often calcareous; it may or may not be a true exoskeleton.
entries.definitionCN: shell 是坚硬外层，常为钙质；它可能是也可能不是真正的外骨骼。

entries.definition: A carapace is the shield covering the back of a crab or similar animal, part of its exoskeleton.
entries.definitionCN: carapace 指蟹类背部的甲盾，是外骨骼的一部分。

entries.definition: A cuticle is the outermost layer of an animal or plant; in arthropods it is the exoskeleton itself.
entries.definitionCN: cuticle 指动物或植物的最外层；在节肢动物身上它就是外骨骼。

entries.definition: Armour is the general word for protective covering, used of tanks and knights as well as animals.
entries.definitionCN: armour 是防护包被的通称，可用于坦克、骑士，也可用于动物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Exo- 'outside' plus skeleton says exactly where the support sits.
normal.cn: exo-「外面」加 skeleton 直接说明支撑的位置。

normal.en: The family runs exoskeleton, exoskeletons, exoskeletal and exoskeletally.
normal.cn: 词族包括 exoskeleton、exoskeletons、exoskeletal 与 exoskeletally。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: shed the exoskeleton, robotic exoskeleton, calcareous exoskeleton.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：蜕去外骨骼、机械外骨骼、钙质外壳。

normal.en: The pair endoskeleton and exoskeleton differ only in the first prefix, endo- versus exo-.
normal.cn: 内骨骼与外骨骼这一对只差前缀：endo- 与 exo-。

normal.en: Arthropods must moult because their support cannot grow with them.
normal.cn: 节肢动物必须蜕皮，因为它们的支撑结构不能随身体一同长大。

abstract.en: Picture a knight whose armour is grown, not worn.
abstract.cn: 想象一位骑士，盔甲是长出来的，不是穿上的。

abstract.en: Picture a building that wears its steel frame on the outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一座把钢架穿在外面的建筑。

abstract.en: Picture a person whose politeness is a shell with a soft animal inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人，礼貌是壳，里面藏着一只柔软的小动物。

examples.en: A crab must back out of its old exoskeleton before the new one hardens.
examples.cn: 蟹必须在新壳硬化之前从旧壳里退出来。

examples.en: Paleontologists rely on exoskeletons because soft parts rarely fossilise.
examples.cn: 古生物学家依赖外骨骼，因为软体部分极少形成化石。

examples.en: The warehouse adopted a robotic exoskeleton to help workers lift heavy crates.
examples.cn: 仓库采用机械外骨骼来帮助工人抬起重箱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exo（外）+ skeleton（骨架）」——长在身体外面的骨架 → 外骨骼

root: 希腊 exo-「外面」+ skeleton（希腊 skeletos「干枯的」，原指木乃伊或干瘪尸体）。19 世纪比较解剖学造词，与 endoskeleton 成对。确切首见年代与首创者不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move outward from the idea of support outside the body: the arthropod shell, the chitin layer, calcareous shells, cast moults, fossils, wearable frames, building frames and a defensive manner.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「支撑在身体之外」这一想法向外展开：节肢动物硬壳、几丁质层、钙质壳、蜕壳、化石、可穿戴框架、建筑骨架与防御性的姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard shell carried on the outside, muscles pulling from within, joints left soft.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具穿在外面的硬壳，肌肉从内侧牵引，关节处保持柔软。

branches.en: THE ARRANGEMENT: support outside, soft tissue inside.
branches.cn: 布局：支撑在外，软组织在内。

branches.en: THE MATERIALS: chitin and calcium carbonate are two ways of hardening the outside.
branches.cn: 材料：几丁质与碳酸钙是硬化外层的两种方式。

branches.en: WHAT IS LEFT: cast shells and fossils are the hard part without the animal.
branches.cn: 留下之物：蜕壳与化石都是失去动物后的硬部。

branches.en: ENGINEERING: wearable frames and building frames copy the load path.
branches.cn: 工程：可穿戴框架与建筑骨架复制了这条受力路径。

branches.en: PROTECTIVE MANNER: a hard outward habit shields something soft.
branches.cn: 防御姿态：坚硬的外在习惯护住柔软之物。

intro.en: Exoskeleton is a Greek-derived compound; the prefix exo-, the base skeleton and the adjective suffix -al all remain productive in English.
intro.cn: exoskeleton 是希腊来源的复合词；前缀 exo-、词基 skeleton 与形容词后缀 -al 在英语中均仍能产词。

latinIntro.en: Greek exō 'outside' gives the prefix exo-, as in exoskeleton and exothermic; Greek skeletos 'dried up' gives skeleton and skeletal.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 exō「外面」给出前缀 exo-，如 exoskeleton、exothermic；希腊 skeletos「干枯的」给出 skeleton 与 skeletal。

items.example: The prefix places the structure outside the body.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把结构置于体外。

items.example: The skeleton carries the body's weight.
items.exampleCN: 骨架承担身体的重量。

items.example: The exoskeleton protects the soft body.
items.exampleCN: 外骨骼保护柔软的身体。

items.example: Moulted exoskeletons litter the shore.
items.exampleCN: 蜕下的外骨骼散落岸边。

items.example: Exoskeletal plates overlap like tiles.
items.exampleCN: 外骨骼板像瓦片一样重叠。

items.meaning: by means of an outer skeleton
items.example: The animal is exoskeletally supported.
items.exampleCN: 这种动物靠外骨骼支撑。

items.example: The reaction is exothermic.
items.exampleCN: 这个反应是放热的。

items.meaning: a planet outside the solar system
items.example: An exoplanet passed before its star.
items.exampleCN: 一颗系外行星从它的恒星前经过。

items.example: The exoskeleton suit halved the lifting effort.
items.exampleCN: 外骨骼服把举重费力减半。

definition_zh: 内骨骼；位于软组织内部的支撑骨架（脊椎动物的骨与软骨）；棘皮动物的钙质内板；某些软体动物的内壳；海绵的骨针框架；中轴骨与附肢骨的统称；化石中的内骨骼；器械或建筑的内承力骨架（比喻）
definition_en: a supporting framework lying inside the soft tissues of an animal, as in the bony skeleton of vertebrates or the plates of an echinoderm
core_image: 透视影像上，一节节脊椎排成链，细弧状的肋骨把胸腔围住
scene: 透视影像上，一节节脊椎排成一条链。On the radiograph, the endoskeleton shows a chain of vertebrae closed by thin curved ribs.
sceneCN: 这里 endoskeleton 指「位于软组织内部的支撑骨架」（第 1 个义项：脊椎动物的骨与软骨）；句意为透视影像上，内骨骼呈现为一串脊椎，由细弧状肋骨围合。可辨识物件：椎节、肋骨弧线、胸腔轮廓、影像底片。

senses.title: A framework inside the body
senses.definition: a rigid or semi-rigid supporting structure lying within the soft tissues, where muscles can attach around it
senses.definitionCN: 位于软组织之内、肌肉可在其周围附着的坚硬或半坚硬支撑结构
senses.example: On the radiograph, the endoskeleton shows a chain of vertebrae closed by thin curved ribs.
senses.exampleCN: 透视影像上，内骨骼呈现为一串脊椎，由细弧状肋骨围合。
senses.why: The prefix endo- says the support is inside; this is the arrangement familiar in vertebrate bodies.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 endo- 说明支撑在内部；这是脊椎动物身上熟悉的布局。

senses.title: Bone and cartilage together
senses.titleCN: 骨与软骨构成的内骨骼
senses.definition: the bony or cartilaginous skeleton of a vertebrate, including skull, spine, ribs and limbs
senses.definitionCN: 脊椎动物的骨性或软骨性骨架，含颅骨、脊柱、肋骨与四肢
senses.example: A shark's endoskeleton is cartilage rather than bone.
senses.exampleCN: 鲨鱼的内骨骼是软骨而非硬骨。
senses.why: This sense names the material range, which is why the same word covers both bone and cartilage.
senses.whyCN: 这一义标出材料范围，因此同一个词既覆盖硬骨也覆盖软骨。

senses.title: The plates of an echinoderm
senses.definition: the calcite plates embedded in the tissue of a starfish or sea urchin, forming an internal skeleton
senses.definitionCN: 嵌在海星或海胆组织中的方解石板，构成内部骨架
senses.example: A starfish's endoskeleton is made of many small calcite plates.
senses.exampleCN: 海星的内骨骼由许多小方解石板组成。
senses.why: Invertebrates can also have an endoskeleton, which shows that the word is about position rather than about bones.
senses.whyCN: 无脊椎动物也可以有内骨骼，说明这个词讲的是位置而非骨骼。

senses.title: An internal shell
senses.definition: a shell enclosed within the body, such as the pen of a squid or the plate of a cuttlefish
senses.definitionCN: 包在体内的壳，如乌贼的羽状内壳或乌贼的钙质内板
senses.example: The squid's endoskeleton is a thin transparent pen.
senses.exampleCN: 乌贼的内骨骼是一片透明的薄羽。
senses.why: Here a shell, usually an outer thing, has moved inside, so the term follows position rather than origin.
senses.whyCN: 此处本属外部的壳移到了体内，说明术语跟随位置而非来源。

senses.title: The spicule frame of a sponge
senses.definition: the network of mineral spicules or spongin fibres that supports a sponge's body
senses.definitionCN: 支撑海绵身体的矿质骨针或海绵丝网络
senses.example: The sponge's endoskeleton keeps its canals open.
senses.exampleCN: 海绵的内骨骼使它的水道保持通畅。
senses.why: This sense extends the term to the simplest animals, where support is a mesh rather than a series of bones.
senses.whyCN: 这一义把术语扩展到最简单的动物，此处支撑是一张网而非一串骨。

senses.title: Axial and appendicular parts
senses.titleCN: 中轴骨与附肢骨的分部
senses.definition: the division of the vertebrate frame into the central axis and the attached limbs and girdles
senses.definitionCN: 脊椎动物骨架划分为中央轴与相连的肢带两部分
senses.example: The axial endoskeleton protects the nerve cord and organs.
senses.exampleCN: 中轴内骨骼保护神经管与内脏。
senses.why: Anatomy splits one structure into named parts, and this sense is the standard teaching frame.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把一个结构拆成命名部件，这一义是标准教学框架。

senses.title: Preserved internal frames
senses.definition: the fossilised remains of an internal skeleton, often the only evidence of a soft-bodied animal
senses.definitionCN: 内骨骼的化石遗存，常是软体动物存在的唯一证据
senses.example: The fossil preserves an endoskeleton but no trace of skin.
senses.exampleCN: 这件化石保存了内骨骼，却没有皮肤的痕迹。
senses.why: Because the inner frame is hard, it survives when soft tissue is lost, so the fossil record often keeps only the endoskeleton.
senses.whyCN: 由于内架坚硬，软组织丢失时它仍能留存，因此化石记录常常只剩内骨骼。

senses.title: An internal supporting frame in engineering
senses.titleCN: 器械或建筑的内承力骨架（比喻）
senses.definition: a hidden inner structure that carries loads or gives shape, used metaphorically of machines and organizations
senses.definitionCN: 隐藏在内部、承担荷载或定形的结构，比喻用于机械与组织
senses.example: The machine's endoskeleton is a cast frame under the panels.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器的内骨架是面板下的一具铸架。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the contrast with an outer shell: what holds the thing together is not what you see first.
senses.whyCN: 比喻保留了与外壳的对照：把东西撑住的，并不是最先看到的那一层。

intro.en: Endoskeleton joins Greek endon 'within' to skeleton, from Greek skeletos 'dried up'. It was formed in nineteenth-century anatomy as the counterpart of exoskeleton.
intro.cn: endoskeleton 把希腊 endon「在内」与 skeleton 组合，后者出自希腊 skeletos「干枯的」。它在 19 世纪解剖学中作为 exoskeleton 的对应词被造出。

items.en: Endon meant 'within' and gives the English prefix endo-, as in endoskeleton, endocrine and endoscope.
items.cn: endon 意为「在内」，给出英语前缀 endo-，如 endoskeleton、endocrine、endoscope。

items.en: Skeleton descends from skeletos 'dried up', first used of a mummy and later of the bony frame.
items.cn: skeleton 出自 skeletos「干枯的」，先用于木乃伊，后指骨性支架。

items.en: Anatomy needed two terms for supports inside and outside the body, and endoskeleton was set against exoskeleton.
items.cn: 解剖学需要两个术语分别指体内与体外的支撑，endoskeleton 与 exoskeleton 遂成一对。

items.en: The word travelled beyond vertebrates: echinoderm plates, squid pens and sponge spicules are all called endoskeletons because of their position.
items.cn: 这个词超出了脊椎动物：棘皮动物骨板、乌贼内壳与海绵骨针都因位置而被称为内骨骼。

items.en: Modern technical writing applies the term to hidden inner frames that carry loads out of sight.
items.cn: 现代技术写作把这个词用于藏在内部、在视线之外承受荷载的骨架。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and coiner): the earliest use and the anatomist who fixed the pair are not settled, so any single attribution is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与首创者）：最早的用法与确立这对术语的解剖学家均无定论，任何单一归属都属推测。

note.en: Group one contrasts endoskeleton with the outer arrangement and its own family; group two lists the internal supporting structures it overlaps with.
note.cn: 第一组把 endoskeleton 与外骨骼布局及自身词族对照；第二组列出与它重叠的内部支撑结构。

entries.definition: An exoskeleton lies outside the soft tissue; endoskeleton lies within it.
entries.definitionCN: exoskeleton 位于软组织之外；endoskeleton 位于其中。

entries.definition: Skeleton can mean either arrangement, so it is the broader word.
entries.definitionCN: skeleton 可指任一种布局，是更宽泛的词。

entries.definition: Endoskeletal describes what belongs to the inner frame and cannot replace the noun.
entries.definitionCN: endoskeletal 描述属内骨架之物，不能替代名词。

entries.definition: Endoscope shares endo- but combines it with scope 'look', so it is not a skeleton word at all.
entries.definitionCN: endoscope 共享 endo-，却与 scope「看」组合，完全不是骨架词。

entries.definition: Backbone names the spine only, a central part of the vertebrate endoskeleton.
entries.definitionCN: backbone 只指脊柱，是脊椎动物内骨骼的中央部分。

entries.definition: Cartilage is the flexible tissue that forms the endoskeleton of sharks and the joint surfaces of other vertebrates.
entries.definitionCN: cartilage 是形成鲨鱼内骨骼与其它脊椎动物关节面的柔性组织。

entries.definition: Framework is the general word for any supporting structure and carries no positional meaning.
entries.definitionCN: framework 是任何支撑结构的通称，不含位置信息。

entries.definition: A shell is typically outer, so it contrasts with an internal frame even when it lies inside a squid.
entries.definitionCN: shell 通常是外部的，因此即使位于乌贼体内，也与内骨架形成对照。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Endo- 'within' plus skeleton says the support is inside the body.
normal.cn: endo-「在内」加 skeleton 说明支撑在体内。

normal.en: The family runs endoskeleton, endoskeletons, endoskeletal and endoskeletally.
normal.cn: 词族包括 endoskeleton、endoskeletons、endoskeletal 与 endoskeletally。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: bony endoskeleton, cartilaginous endoskeleton, axial endoskeleton.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：骨性内骨骼、软骨内骨骼、中轴内骨骼。

normal.en: The pair differs only in the prefix: endo- inside, exo- outside.
normal.cn: 这对词只差前缀：endo- 在内，exo- 在外。

normal.en: Invertebrates such as starfish also have an endoskeleton, so bones are not required.
normal.cn: 海星等无脊椎动物也有内骨骼，因此并不需要骨头。

abstract.en: Picture a scaffold built inside a tent rather than around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座搭在帐篷里面而非外面的脚手架。

abstract.en: Picture a transparent squid carrying a thin pen where a shell used to be.
abstract.cn: 想象一只透明的乌贼，体内带着一片薄羽，那里原本是壳。

abstract.en: Picture an organization held up by rules nobody outside can see.
abstract.cn: 想象一个由外人看不见的规章撑起的组织。

examples.en: The axial endoskeleton of a mammal includes the skull, spine and rib cage.
examples.cn: 哺乳动物的中轴内骨骼包括颅骨、脊柱与胸廓。

examples.en: Sharks have a cartilaginous endoskeleton, which is lighter than bone.
examples.cn: 鲨鱼有软骨内骨骼，比硬骨更轻。

examples.en: A starfish's endoskeleton consists of calcite plates under the skin.
examples.cn: 海星的内骨骼由皮下的方解石板构成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「endo（内）+ skeleton（骨架）」——长在身体里面的骨架 → 内骨骼

root: 希腊 endon「在内」+ skeleton（希腊 skeletos「干枯的」）。19 世纪解剖学中作为 exoskeleton 的对应词。确切首见年代与首创者不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move inward from the idea of support inside the body: the vertebrate frame, bone and cartilage, echinoderm plates, an internal shell, sponge spicules, axial and limb divisions, fossils and an engineering metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「支撑在体内」这一想法向内展开：脊椎动物骨架、骨与软骨、棘皮动物骨板、内壳、海绵骨针、中轴与附肢分部、化石，以及工程比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain of vertebrae behind soft tissue, ribs curving forward around a cavity.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串脊椎藏在软组织之后，肋骨向前弯成腔室的围栏。

branches.en: THE VERTEBRATE CASE: an inner frame of bone or cartilage that muscles pull against.
branches.cn: 脊椎动物情形：骨或软骨构成的内架，肌肉在其上牵引。

branches.en: INVERTEBRATES: plates and spicules show position, not bone, is what defines the term.
branches.cn: 无脊椎动物：骨板与骨针说明定义这个词的是位置而非骨质。

branches.en: SHELL TURNED INWARD: a squid pen is an outer covering moved inside.
branches.cn: 壳转入体内：乌贼的羽状内壳是移到体内的外壳。

branches.en: PARTS AND DEEP TIME: anatomy divides the frame, and fossils keep only the hard inner part.
branches.cn: 分部与深时：解剖学把骨架分部，化石只留下坚硬的内层。

branches.en: HIDDEN ENGINEERING: what holds a machine together is not what you see first.
branches.cn: 隐藏的工程：撑住机器的并不是最先看到的那一层。

intro.en: Endoskeleton is a Greek-derived compound; endo- remains productive, and skeleton supplies the base for skeleton, skeletal and exoskeleton.
intro.cn: endoskeleton 是希腊来源复合词；endo- 仍能产词，skeleton 为 skeleton、skeletal、exoskeleton 提供词基。

latinIntro.en: Greek endon 'within' gives endo-, as in endocrine and endoscope; Greek skeletos 'dried up' gives skeleton and skeletal.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 endon「在内」给出 endo-，如 endocrine、endoscope；希腊 skeletos「干枯的」给出 skeleton 与 skeletal。

items.example: The prefix places the frame inside the tissue.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把骨架置于组织之内。

items.example: The skeleton supports the body.
items.exampleCN: 骨架支撑身体。

items.example: The endoskeleton lies under the muscles.
items.exampleCN: 内骨骼位于肌肉之下。

items.example: Endoskeletons of many shapes evolved.
items.exampleCN: 多种形状的内骨骼演化出来。

items.example: Endoskeletal cartilage resists compression.
items.exampleCN: 内骨骼软骨抗压。

items.example: The animal is endoskeletally supported.
items.exampleCN: 这种动物靠内骨骼支撑。

items.example: The endocrine gland releases hormones.
items.exampleCN: 内分泌腺释放激素。

items.example: The endoscope entered through a small cut.
items.exampleCN: 内窥镜通过小切口进入。

items.example: The endostyle helps filter food.
items.exampleCN: 内柱帮助滤食。

definition_zh: 骨骼；人体或动物的全部骨与软骨；一副骨架；骸骨、骷髅；建筑或船体的框架；梗概、纲要；骨干人员（最低限度的人手）；万能钥匙；化学中的碳骨架；极瘦的人（比喻）
definition_en: the bony or hard supporting framework of an animal body; also any bare supporting structure, an outline, a minimum staff or a thin person
core_image: 博物馆库房里，一副骨架按编号逐块摆开，肋骨弯成半圆，头骨垫在软布上
scene: 博物馆库房里，一副骨架按编号逐块摆开，头骨垫在软布上。In the store room, a skeleton is laid out bone by bone on padded cloth.
sceneCN: 这里 skeleton 指「动物体内起支撑作用的全部骨与软骨」（第 1 个义项：骨骼）；句意为库房里的骨架被逐块按编号摆开，头骨垫在软布上。可辨识物件：肋骨半圆、头骨、编号标签、软布。

pos.zh: 骨骼；骨架；（建筑等的）框架；梗概；骨干人员；万能钥匙
