骨干船员；值班最少人员

senses.title: The bony framework of a body
senses.definition: the whole set of bones and cartilage that supports and shapes an animal body
senses.definitionCN: 支撑并塑造动物身体的全部骨与软骨
senses.example: In the store room, a skeleton is laid out bone by bone on padded cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 库房里的骨架被逐块摆开，头骨垫在软布上。
senses.why: The core sense is anatomical: the frame that remains when soft tissue is removed.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是解剖学的：去掉软组织后留下的那副支架。

senses.title: A set of remains
senses.definition: the bones of a dead person or animal, especially when found or buried
senses.definitionCN: 死者或死动物的骨头，尤指被发现或埋葬时
senses.example: Police found a skeleton buried beneath the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在地板下发现了一具埋着的骸骨。
senses.why: The same object seen as a person's remains rather than as a structure, which shifts the tone toward death.
senses.whyCN: 同一物件被看作某人的遗骸而非结构，语气因此转向死亡。

senses.title: A hard supporting structure
senses.definition: any rigid supporting structure of an animal, including the shell of a crab or the plates of a starfish
senses.definitionCN: 动物身上任何坚硬的支撑结构，包括蟹壳或海星骨板
senses.example: The crab's skeleton is on the outside, so it must moult.
senses.exampleCN: 蟹的骨架长在外面，所以必须蜕皮。
senses.why: Comparative anatomy widened the word beyond bones, which is why exoskeleton and endoskeleton both exist.
senses.whyCN: 比较解剖学把这个词扩展到骨头之外，exoskeleton 与 endoskeleton 因此都存在。

senses.title: The frame of a building or ship
senses.definition: the bare structural frame that carries loads before cladding or plating is added
senses.definitionCN: 在覆面或铺板装上之前承担荷载的裸框架
senses.example: The steel skeleton of the tower was finished before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这座塔的钢骨架在入冬前完工。
senses.why: Engineering borrows the anatomical word because a frame, like bones, holds everything in place.
senses.whyCN: 工程学借用解剖词，因为框架如骨骼一样把一切都固定在位。

senses.title: An outline or plan
senses.definition: the bare outline of a document, argument or course, with details still to be filled in
senses.definitionCN: 文件、论证或课程的裸轮廓，细节仍留空
senses.example: She drafted a skeleton of the report before writing it out.
senses.exampleCN: 她在正式动笔前先写出了报告的提纲。
senses.why: The metaphor treats structure as bones and detail as flesh, a very old rhetorical habit.
senses.whyCN: 比喻把结构当作骨、细节当作肉，是一种很古老的修辞习惯。

senses.title: The minimum staff needed
senses.titleCN: 最低限度的人手；骨干班子
senses.definition: the smallest number of workers required to keep a service running, as in a skeleton staff
senses.definitionCN: 维持运转所需的最少人手，如「skeleton staff」
senses.example: Only a skeleton crew stayed aboard during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴期间船上只留了一个骨干班组。
senses.why: Here skeleton means stripped to essentials, the same idea as an outline but applied to people.
senses.whyCN: 此处 skeleton 指削到最基本的程度，与提纲同一思路，只是用于人。

senses.title: A master key
senses.definition: a key filed down so that it opens many locks, historically called a skeleton key
senses.definitionCN: 被锉成能开许多锁的钥匙，历史上称作「skeleton key」
senses.example: The caretaker opened every door with a skeleton key.
senses.exampleCN: 管理员用一把万能钥匙打开了每一扇门。
senses.why: The name comes from the key's bare, bone-like shaft rather than from any lock mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自钥匙光秃、似骨的柄杆，而非任何锁具机关。

senses.title: A carbon framework in chemistry
senses.definition: the arrangement of carbon atoms in a molecule, shown without most hydrogen atoms
senses.definitionCN: 分子中碳原子的排列，通常省略大部分氢原子
senses.example: The carbon skeleton decides whether the molecule is a chain or a ring.
senses.exampleCN: 碳骨架决定这个分子是链状还是环状。
senses.why: Chemistry borrows the image of a bare frame, because the skeleton is what remains when hydrogens are stripped away.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用「裸框架」的意象，因为去掉氢之后留下的正是骨架。

senses.title: An extremely thin person
senses.definition: a person so thin that bones show, described as a walking skeleton
senses.definitionCN: 瘦到骨头显露的人，被说成行走的骨架
senses.example: After the illness he was a walking skeleton.
senses.exampleCN: 病后他瘦得像一副行走的骨架。
senses.why: The metaphor is blunt rather than kind, and it works by removing flesh from the image.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻直白而不客气，靠从形象中抽掉肉来成立。

intro.en: Skeleton comes from Greek skeleton, the neuter of skeletos 'dried up', first used of a mummy or a withered body. English borrowed it through Latin and narrowed it to the bony frame.
intro.cn: skeleton 来自希腊 skeleton，是 skeletos「干枯的」的中性形式，最初用于木乃伊或干瘪的尸体。英语经拉丁借入，后收窄为骨性支架。

items.en: Skeletos meant 'dried up, withered'; the noun skeleton named a dried body, a mummy, not a living frame.
items.cn: skeletos 意为「干枯的、干瘪的」；名词 skeleton 指干瘪的尸体、木乃伊，而非活体的支架。

items.en: Latin sceleton or skeleton took the Greek noun over unchanged in meaning, and medieval anatomy kept the 'dried body' sense.
items.cn: 拉丁 sceleton 或 skeleton 原义不变地接过希腊名词，中世纪解剖学保留了「干尸」义。

items.en: In sixteenth-century anatomy the word came to mean the bony framework of a living body, and the older mummy sense faded.
items.cn: 在 16 世纪解剖学中，这个词转指活体的骨性支架，较早的木乃伊义逐渐消失。

items.en: From the eighteenth century skeleton named the bare frame of a building or ship, and later any stripped-down structure.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，skeleton 指建筑或船体的裸框架，后来指任何削简的结构。

items.en: Skeleton key, skeleton staff and skeleton in the closet all exploit the idea of something reduced to its bare minimum.
items.cn: 万能钥匙、骨干班子与家丑这三条短语都利用「削到最低限度」的想法。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the exact route from the Greek 'dried body' to the modern anatomical sense is not fully documented, and the earliest English citation is a matter of record rather than certainty.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：从希腊「干尸」到现代解剖义的具体路径缺乏完整文献，最早的英语书证属于记录问题而非确定结论。

note.en: Group one separates skeleton from its adjective and from the two positional variants; group two lists the frameworks and outlines people compare with it.
note.cn: 第一组把 skeleton 与形容词及两种位置变体分开；第二组列出人们拿来比较的框架与纲要。

entries.definition: Skeletal describes what belongs to a skeleton; skeleton is the thing itself.
entries.definitionCN: skeletal 描述属于骨架之物；skeleton 是物本身。

entries.definition: An exoskeleton is a skeleton outside the soft tissue, as in insects.
entries.definitionCN: exoskeleton 是位于软组织之外的骨架，如昆虫。

entries.definition: An endoskeleton is a skeleton inside the soft tissue, as in vertebrates.
entries.definitionCN: endoskeleton 是位于软组织之内的骨架，如脊椎动物。

entries.definition: Skeleton key is a fixed compound for a master key, not a kind of bone.
entries.definitionCN: skeleton key 是万能钥匙的固定复合词，不是某种骨头。

entries.definition: Framework is the general word for any supporting structure, including building frames and conceptual ones.
entries.definitionCN: framework 是任何支撑结构的通称，包括建筑框架与概念框架。

entries.definition: Outline is the ordinary word for a bare plan; skeleton is its more figurative, structural cousin.
entries.definitionCN: outline 是裸计划的日常说法；skeleton 是更形象、更结构化的近亲。

entries.definition: Carcass names the body of a dead animal, including its flesh, so it is not limited to bones.
entries.definitionCN: carcass 指死动物的躯体，含肉，因此不限于骨头。

entries.definition: Skull is only the head part of a skeleton, not the whole frame.
entries.definitionCN: skull 只是骨架的头部，而非整副支架。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek skeletos 'dried up' gave a word for a mummy, which anatomy later narrowed to bones.
normal.cn: 希腊 skeletos「干枯的」给出一个指木乃伊的词，解剖学后来把它收窄为骨头。

normal.en: The family runs skeleton, skeletons, skeletal, skeletally and skeletonize.
normal.cn: 词族包括 skeleton、skeletons、skeletal、skeletally 与 skeletonize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: skeleton key, skeleton staff, skeleton in the closet.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：万能钥匙、骨干班子、家丑。

normal.en: The positional pair is exoskeleton outside, endoskeleton inside.
normal.cn: 位置配对是：外骨骼在外，内骨骼在内。

normal.en: A skeleton crew is a crew reduced to its bones.
normal.cn: 骨干船员就是把船员削减到只剩骨架。

abstract.en: Picture a building stripped of every panel, showing only its girders.
abstract.cn: 想象一座拆掉所有面板的建筑，只剩梁架。

abstract.en: Picture a document reduced to headings with no sentences.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文件只剩标题，没有句子。

abstract.en: Picture a key filed down to a bare stem that fits many locks.
abstract.cn: 想象一把被锉成光杆、能开许多锁的钥匙。

examples.en: The museum mounted the dinosaur skeleton in a walking pose.
examples.cn: 博物馆把这具恐龙骨架装成行走的姿态。

examples.en: A skeleton staff kept the library open during the holidays.
examples.cn: 假期里一个骨干班子维持着图书馆开放。

examples.en: The report's skeleton was approved before any data were collected.
examples.cn: 报告的提纲在任何数据收集之前就通过了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「skeleton（斯凯利顿）」——只剩干骨头、别的一概没有 → 骨架、梗概

root: 希腊 skeletos「干枯的」→ 名词 skeleton 原指干尸、木乃伊；经拉丁进入英语，16 世纪解剖学收窄为骨性支架。更早的来源与确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from the anatomical frame to remains, hard shells, buildings, outlines, minimum staff, a master key, a carbon frame and a very thin person.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从解剖学的支架走到遗骸、硬壳、建筑、纲要、最少人手、万能钥匙、碳骨架与极瘦的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bare frame laid out bone by bone, ribs in arcs, everything soft removed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一副裸框架被逐块摆开，肋骨成弧，柔软部分全部除去。

branches.en: THE BODY: a living frame and the same frame as remains.
branches.cn: 身体：活的支架与作为遗骸的同一支架。

branches.en: MATERIAL WIDENED: shells and plates are skeletons too, if they support the body.
branches.cn: 材料放宽：只要支撑身体，壳与骨板也算骨架。

branches.en: BARE STRUCTURE: buildings, documents and molecules are all reduced to a frame.
branches.cn: 裸结构：建筑、文件与分子都被削成框架。

branches.en: REDUCED TO ESSENTIALS: minimum staff and a filed-down key keep the same image.
branches.cn: 削到基本：最少人手与被锉薄的钥匙沿用同一意象。

branches.en: FLESH REMOVED: a thin person is described as what is left without flesh.
branches.cn: 去肉：极瘦的人被描述成去掉肉之后剩下的部分。

intro.en: Skeleton is a Greek-derived noun; English adds -al for the adjective, -ize for the verb, and prefixes exo- or endo- to mark position.
intro.cn: skeleton 是希腊来源名词；英语加 -al 构成形容词、加 -ize 构成动词，并以前缀 exo- 或 endo- 标出位置。

latinIntro.en: Greek skeleton gives skeletal and skeletonize; Greek exō and endon attach to the same base in exoskeleton and endoskeleton.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 skeleton 给出 skeletal 与 skeletonize；希腊 exō 与 endon 在同一词基上构成 exoskeleton 与 endoskeleton。

items.example: The skeleton was complete except for one hand.
items.exampleCN: 这具骨架除一只手外完整。

items.example: Two skeletons lay side by side.
items.exampleCN: 两具骨架并排躺着。

items.example: Skeletal muscle pulls on bone.
items.exampleCN: 骨骼肌牵动骨头。

items.example: The two animals are skeletally similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两种动物在骨骼上相似。

items.meaning: to reduce to a skeleton; to strip down
items.example: Editors skeletonized the long report.
items.exampleCN: 编辑把冗长的报告大幅删减。

items.example: A skeleton key opened the cellar.
items.exampleCN: 一把万能钥匙打开了地窖。

items.example: A skeleton staff ran the office in August.
items.exampleCN: 八月由一个骨干班子维持办公室。

items.meaningCN: 骨干船员；最少值班人员
items.example: The skeleton crew kept the ship at anchor.
items.exampleCN: 骨干船员让船留在锚地。

items.example: The exoskeleton is shed twice a year.
items.exampleCN: 这层外骨骼一年蜕两次。

definition_zh: 骨骼的；骨架的；骨骼构成的；骨骼肌的；骸骨的；骨架式的、只剩轮廓的；骨瘦如柴的；化学结构式的；土层浅薄多石的
definition_en: relating to a skeleton or to bones; also used of a bare outline, an extremely thin body, or a chemical structure drawn as a frame
core_image: 影像上，骨架的轮廓细而清楚，肋骨像一道道细光弧
scene: 影像上，骨架的轮廓细而清楚。The skeletal outline is thin and sharp on the film, ribs drawn as arcs of light.
sceneCN: 这里 skeletal 指「与骨骼有关的」（第 1 个义项：骨骼的）；句意为骨头构成的轮廓在影像上细而清楚，肋骨被画成一道道弧光。可辨识物件：椎节轮廓、肋骨弧线、影像底片、清晰边缘。

pos.zh: 骨骼的；骨架的；骨瘦如柴的；只剩轮廓的

senses.title: Relating to a skeleton
senses.definition: concerning the bony or hard frame of a body, or the bones themselves
senses.definitionCN: 关于身体的骨性或硬质支架，或关于骨头本身
senses.example: The skeletal outline is thin and sharp on the film, ribs drawn as arcs of light.
senses.exampleCN: 骨头构成的轮廓在影像上细而清楚，肋骨被画成一道道弧光。
senses.why: The suffix -al makes a plain relational adjective, so skeletal simply answers 'of the skeleton'.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 构成纯粹关系形容词，skeletal 只回答「关于骨骼的」。

senses.title: Of skeletal muscle
senses.definition: describing the striped muscle attached to bones, the kind that moves the limbs
senses.definitionCN: 描述附着于骨头、能带动四肢的横纹肌
senses.example: Skeletal muscle tires faster than cardiac muscle.
senses.exampleCN: 骨骼肌比心肌更容易疲劳。
senses.why: Anatomy fixed the phrase skeletal muscle to distinguish it from smooth and cardiac muscle.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学固定了「skeletal muscle」这一说法，以区别于平滑肌与心肌。

senses.title: Of skeletal remains
senses.definition: describing bones found without flesh, as in skeletal remains at an archaeological site
senses.definitionCN: 描述没有肉、只剩骨头的遗存，如考古现场的白骨
senses.example: Skeletal remains were dated to the Bronze Age.
senses.exampleCN: 骨骼遗存被测定为青铜时代。
senses.why: This sense applies the adjective to what is left of a body once flesh is gone, a forensic and archaeological use.
senses.whyCN: 这一义把形容词用于肉体消失后留下的东西，属法医与考古用法。

senses.title: A bare supporting structure
senses.definition: describing a frame stripped to its essential members, as in a skeletal tower or chassis
senses.definitionCN: 描述削到基本构件的框架，如骨架式的塔架或底盘
senses.example: The engineer designed a skeletal frame of steel tubes.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师设计了一个钢管骨架。
senses.why: The adjective extends from anatomy to engineering, keeping the idea of only the load-bearing parts.
senses.whyCN: 形容词从解剖学扩到工程，保留「只剩承重构件」的意思。

senses.title: A stripped-down outline
senses.titleCN: 只剩轮廓的；骨架式提纲
senses.definition: describing a plan or account that gives only headings and main points
senses.definitionCN: 描述只给标题与要点的方案或叙述
senses.example: He submitted a skeletal outline of the thesis.
senses.exampleCN: 他提交了一份骨架式论文提纲。
senses.why: Writing uses the image of bones for structure and flesh for detail, a very productive metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 写作把结构比作骨、细节比作肉，是极能产的比喻。

senses.title: Extremely thin
senses.definition: describing a body so thin that the bones are visible beneath the skin
senses.definitionCN: 描述瘦到骨头在皮下清晰可见的身体
senses.example: The rescued dog was skeletal but recovering.
senses.exampleCN: 被救的狗骨瘦如柴，但正在恢复。
senses.why: This sense is the emotional peak of the metaphor: the person looks like what remains after flesh is removed.
senses.whyCN: 这一义是比喻的情感高峰：人看起来就像去掉肉之后剩下的东西。

senses.title: Drawn as a chemical frame
senses.titleCN: 化学结构式的；骨架式的
senses.definition: describing a molecular formula drawn as lines between carbon atoms with hydrogens omitted
senses.definitionCN: 描述只画碳原子间连线、省略氢的分子式
senses.example: The skeletal formula shows a six-membered ring.
senses.exampleCN: 骨架式显示出一个六元环。
senses.why: Chemistry reuses the bare-frame image literally: the drawing keeps only the carbon skeleton.
senses.whyCN: 化学字面上复用了「裸框架」意象：图里只保留碳骨架。

senses.title: Shallow stony soil
senses.definition: describing soil so thin and rocky that it is almost bare rock, a specialist use in soil science
senses.definitionCN: 描述土层极薄、多石、近乎裸岩，属土壤学的专门用法
senses.example: Only lichens grow on this skeletal soil.
senses.exampleCN: 这种浅薄多石的土上只长地衣。
senses.why: Soil science borrows the adjective for ground stripped to almost nothing, which is the same reduction.
senses.whyCN: 土壤学借这个形容词指被剥到几乎不剩东西的地面，仍是同一种削减。

intro.en: Skeletal is skeleton plus -al 'relating to'. Skeleton itself comes from Greek skeletos 'dried up', first naming a mummy and later the bony frame of a living body.
intro.cn: skeletal 是 skeleton 加 -al「与……有关的」。skeleton 本身出自希腊 skeletos「干枯的」，先指木乃伊，后指活体的骨性支架。

items.en: Skeleton began as a word for a dried body; only later did anatomy make it the living frame.
items.cn: skeleton 起初指干瘪的尸体；解剖学后来才让它指活体支架。

items.en: Latin -alis became English -al, forming relational adjectives from nouns, as in skeleton and skeletal.
items.cn: 拉丁 -alis 变成英语 -al，从名词构成关系形容词，如 skeleton 与 skeletal。

items.en: Skeletal was coined inside English anatomy writing on this pattern, not borrowed whole from another language.
items.cn: skeletal 是英语解剖学写作按这一模式新造的，并非整词借自其它语言。

items.en: Skeletal muscle was fixed as the anatomical name for striped muscle attached to bone, which stabilized one sense.
items.cn: 「skeletal muscle」被固定为附着于骨的横纹肌的解剖名，使一个义项稳定下来。

items.en: The adjective spread to outlines, thin bodies and stony soil, all cases of something reduced to almost nothing.
items.cn: 这个形容词扩到提纲、瘦削的身体与多石的土，都是被削到几乎不剩什么的情形。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the deeper origin and the exact first citation are not settled, so any pre-Latin form offered here is a reconstruction and competing hypotheses are left side by side.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：更深的来源与确切最早书证均无定论，此处给出的拉丁语之前形式属重构形式，并列假说一并保留、不作定论。

note.en: Group one separates skeletal from the noun and from the positional variants; group two lists the adjectives that overlap with it.
note.cn: 第一组把 skeletal 与名词及位置变体分开；第二组列出与它重叠的形容词。

entries.definition: Skeleton is the frame itself; skeletal describes it, so the two cannot swap places.
entries.definitionCN: skeleton 是骨架本身；skeletal 描述它，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: Exoskeletal means 'of an outer skeleton', a narrower adjective than skeletal.
entries.definitionCN: exoskeletal 意为「外骨骼的」，比 skeletal 更窄。

entries.definition: Endoskeletal means 'of an inner skeleton', again narrower than the general adjective.
entries.definitionCN: endoskeletal 意为「内骨骼的」，同样比一般形容词窄。

entries.definition: Skeletally is the adverb and is rare outside technical comparison.
entries.definitionCN: skeletally 是副词，技术比较之外很少见。

entries.definition: Bony means made of or full of bone, and also describes thin, angular bodies.
entries.definitionCN: bony 指由骨构成或富含骨，也形容瘦削有棱角的身形。

entries.definition: Thin is the plain word for narrow width; skeletal adds the image of visible bones.
entries.definitionCN: thin 是宽度的普通说法；skeletal 增加了骨头外露的意象。

entries.definition: Structural is the general adjective for structures and carries no anatomical sense.
entries.definitionCN: structural 是结构的通称形容词，不含解剖义。

entries.definition: Outline is the ordinary noun for a bare summary; skeletal outline is the more figurative phrase.
entries.definitionCN: outline 是裸摘要的日常名词；skeletal outline 是更形象的说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Skeleton plus -al gives the relational adjective, as nation gives national.
normal.cn: skeleton 加 -al 构成关系形容词，与 nation / national 同理。

normal.en: The family runs skeleton, skeletal, skeletally, skeletonize and musculoskeletal.
normal.cn: 词族包括 skeleton、skeletal、skeletally、skeletonize 与 musculoskeletal。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: skeletal muscle, skeletal remains, skeletal formula.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：骨骼肌、骨骼遗存、结构简式。

normal.en: The word covers bones, thin bodies, outlines and chemical frames, all 'bare' forms.
normal.cn: 这个词覆盖骨头、瘦削的身体、提纲与化学骨架，都是「裸形」。

normal.en: Skeletal muscle is the striped muscle attached to bone.
normal.cn: 骨骼肌是附着在骨头上的横纹肌。

abstract.en: Picture a body drawn in pencil with no shading.
abstract.cn: 想象一具只用铅笔勾线、没有明暗的身体。

abstract.en: Picture a report reduced to its headings and nothing else.
abstract.cn: 想象一份只剩标题、别无他物的报告。

abstract.en: Picture soil so thin that the rock shows through like a skull.
abstract.cn: 想象薄到岩石像头骨一样露出来的土。

examples.en: Skeletal muscle accounts for most of the body's voluntary movement.
examples.cn: 骨骼肌承担了身体大部分自主运动。

examples.en: Archaeologists found skeletal remains beneath the collapsed floor.
examples.cn: 考古学家在塌陷的地板下发现骨骼遗存。

examples.en: The plot is still skeletal, with characters but no scenes.
examples.cn: 情节还只是骨架，有人物却还没有场景。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「skeletal（斯凯利透）」——透出来的全是骨头 → 骨骼的；骨瘦如柴的

root: skeleton（希腊 skeletos「干枯的」，原指干尸，后指骨性支架）+ 关系后缀 -al（拉丁 -alis）。skeleton 更早来源与确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one adjective to bones, striped muscle, remains, bare frames, stripped outlines, thin bodies, chemical drawings and stony soil.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个形容词用于骨头、横纹肌、遗存、裸框架、削简提纲、瘦削身体、化学结构图与多石土层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bone frame visible through thin tissue, every rib a clean arc.
core.cn: 核心意象：透过薄薄的组织看到骨框架，每根肋骨都是一道干净的弧。

branches.en: PLAIN RELATION: the suffix asks only what it belongs to.
branches.cn: 纯粹关系：后缀只问它属于什么。

branches.en: ATTACHED MUSCLE: the striped muscle that pulls on bone.
branches.cn: 附着的肌肉：牵动骨头的横纹肌。

branches.en: WHAT REMAINS: bones without flesh and frames without panels.
branches.cn: 留下之物：没有肉的骨与没有面板的框架。

branches.en: BARE FORMS: a stripped outline and a stripped soil both show only structure.
branches.cn: 裸形：削简的提纲与浅薄的土都只显出结构。

branches.en: BONES SHOWING: extreme thinness and a chemical frame make bones visible by removing covering.
branches.cn: 骨外露：极度瘦削与化学骨架都靠去掉覆盖物让骨可见。

intro.en: Skeletal is skeleton plus -al; the family also contains the verb skeletonize, the adverb skeletally and the positional adjectives exoskeletal and endoskeletal.
intro.cn: skeletal 是 skeleton 加 -al；词族还含动词 skeletonize、副词 skeletally 以及位置形容词 exoskeletal、endoskeletal。

latinIntro.en: Greek skeleton supplies the base; -al, -ize and -ly attach in English, and exo- or endo- mark position.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 skeleton 提供词基；英语附加 -al、-ize、-ly，并用 exo- 或 endo- 标出位置。

items.example: Skeletal bone is dense outside.
items.exampleCN: 骨骼的外层致密。

items.example: The two species are skeletally distinct.
items.exampleCN: 这两个物种在骨骼上不同。

items.example: The skeleton is almost complete.
items.exampleCN: 这具骨架几乎完整。

items.example: Skeletons were found in the pit.
items.exampleCN: 坑中发现多具骨架。

items.example: The beetle skeletonizes leaves.
items.exampleCN: 这种甲虫把叶片吃成骨架。

items.example: Musculoskeletal pain is common.
items.exampleCN: 肌肉骨骼疼痛很常见。

items.example: Exoskeletal plates are chitinous.
items.exampleCN: 外骨骼板为几丁质。

items.example: Endoskeletal cartilage supports the shark.
items.exampleCN: 内骨骼软骨支撑着鲨鱼。

items.meaning: a line drawing of a molecule
items.example: The skeletal formula omits hydrogen atoms.
items.exampleCN: 结构简式省略氢原子。

definition_zh: 骨头；骨（组织）；一根骨；全身的骨骼；骸骨；骨材、骨制品；骨色、乳白色；争端所在、核心议题；彻底地、到骨子里；去骨（动词）；刻苦攻读（动词）
definition_en: one of the hard pieces of the vertebrate skeleton, or the material they are made of; also used for remains, carved material, the core of a dispute and the act of removing bones
core_image: 砧板上，厨师用刀沿着鱼脊划开，把整条脊骨完整地抽出来
scene: 砧板上，厨师用刀沿着鱼脊划开，把整条脊骨抽了出来。On the board, the cook slides the knife along the bone and lifts the spine out.
sceneCN: 这里 bone 指「脊椎动物体内的一根硬骨」（第 1 个义项：骨头、骨组织）；句意为砧板上厨师沿鱼脊下刀，把整条脊骨抽出来。可辨识物件：鱼脊骨、刀刃、砧板、剖开的鱼身。

pos.zh: 骨头；骨组织；骸骨；骨材；核心

senses.title: One hard piece of the skeleton
senses.titleCN: 脊椎动物体内的一根硬骨
senses.definition: one of the hard organs of the vertebrate skeleton, with a mineralised matrix and living cells inside
senses.definitionCN: 脊椎动物骨架中的坚硬器官，基质已矿化，内部有活细胞
senses.example: On the board, the cook slides the knife along the bone and lifts the spine out.
senses.exampleCN: 砧板上，厨师沿鱼脊下刀，把整条脊骨抽了出来。
senses.why: The core sense is a countable organ, not a mass of material, which is why bones can be counted one by one.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是可数的器官，而非一团材料，因此骨头可以一根一根地数。

senses.title: Bone as tissue
senses.definition: the living material of which bones are made, including mineral, collagen and bone cells
senses.definitionCN: 构成骨头的活组织，含矿物质、胶原与骨细胞
senses.example: Bone heals by laying down new tissue at the break.
senses.exampleCN: 骨在断裂处沉积新组织而愈合。
senses.why: As a mass noun the word names a tissue, which is how medicine speaks of bone loss or bone density.
senses.whyCN: 作不可数名词时，这个词指一种组织，医学谈骨量流失或骨密度时就这样用。

senses.title: The skeleton as a whole
senses.definition: the whole set of bones considered together as the body's frame
senses.definitionCN: 把全部骨头作为身体的支架整体看待
senses.example: The disease weakened his bones throughout.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病使他全身的骨头都变脆弱。
senses.why: The plural generalizes from single organs to the frame, a common shift from part to system.
senses.whyCN: 复数从单个器官推广到整副支架，是部分到系统的常见转移。

senses.title: Remains of the dead
senses.definition: the bones of a dead person or animal, often found or buried
senses.definitionCN: 死者或死动物的骨头，常被发现或埋葬
senses.example: Bones were found beneath the collapsed wall.
senses.exampleCN: 塌墙之下发现了骸骨。
senses.why: This sense shifts the referent from structure to evidence, and the tone becomes forensic or archaeological.
senses.whyCN: 这一义把所指从结构转为证据，语气随之为法医或考古的。

senses.title: Carved or fired bone material
senses.definition: bone used as a material for tools, ornaments or porcelain, as in bone china
senses.definitionCN: 用作工具、饰物或瓷器的骨材，如骨瓷
senses.example: The handle was carved from bone, not wood.
senses.exampleCN: 这把刀柄是骨雕的，不是木头的。
senses.why: Material culture treats bone as a substance with working properties, so the noun becomes a craft term.
senses.whyCN: 物质文化把骨当作有加工性能的材料，名词因此成为工艺术语。

senses.title: The point at issue
senses.definition: the central subject of a disagreement, in the fixed phrase bone of contention
senses.definitionCN: 分歧的核心议题，见于固定短语「bone of contention」
senses.example: The boundary fence was the bone of contention between the farms.
senses.exampleCN: 地界围栏是两家农场争执的焦点。
senses.why: The image is of two dogs worrying one bone, so the phrase names what both sides want to control.
senses.whyCN: 意象是两只狗争一根骨头，短语因此指双方都想控制的东西。

senses.title: Thoroughly, to the core
senses.definition: used in the phrase to the bone to mean completely, as in chilled to the bone or cut to the bone
senses.definitionCN: 见于「to the bone」一语，意为彻底，如冷到骨头里、削减到最低限度
senses.example: The wind chilled us to the bone before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 不到中午，风就把我们冷透了。
senses.why: The metaphor measures depth by anatomy: what reaches the bone has gone as far as it can.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用解剖来度量深度：到了骨头，就是能到的最深处。

senses.title: A grievance to settle
senses.definition: a complaint one wants to raise, in the fixed phrase have a bone to pick with someone
senses.definitionCN: 想提出的不满，见于「have a bone to pick with someone」
senses.example: I have a bone to pick with the driver who blocked the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 我要跟那个堵门的司机理论理论。
senses.why: The origin of the phrase is disputed, so it is best treated as an idiom whose image is a bone being gnawed over.
senses.whyCN: 这条短语的来源有争议，最好当作一个意象为「啃同一根骨头」的习语。

senses.title: To remove bones
senses.definition: to take the bones out of meat, fish or fruit before cooking or serving
senses.definitionCN: 在烹制或上桌前把肉、鱼或果子里的骨头去掉
senses.example: The butcher boned the leg of lamb in five minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 肉贩五分钟就把羊腿去了骨。
senses.why: The verb is a straightforward conversion from the noun, meaning 'to deprive of bones'.
senses.whyCN: 动词由名词直接转化而来，意为「去掉骨头」。

senses.title: To study hard
senses.definition: to learn a subject intensively, in the informal phrase bone up on
senses.definitionCN: 集中学习某科目，见于口语短语「bone up on」
senses.example: She boned up on geology before the field trip.
senses.exampleCN: 野外实习前她狠补了地质学。
senses.why: The origin of this slang is uncertain; suggestions include an old sense of bone meaning to apply oneself, but none is proven.
senses.whyCN: 这条俚语的来源不确定；有说法把它联系到 bone 旧义「专心用功」，但都未获证实。

intro.en: Bone comes from Old English bān, a Germanic word for bone that has cognates across the Germanic languages. Latin os 'bone' is a different family entirely.
intro.cn: bone 来自古英语 bān，是日耳曼语中指骨头的词，在诸日耳曼语中都有同源词。拉丁 os「骨」属完全不同的词族。

items.en: Old English bān meant bone, and compounds such as bānhus 'bone-house, body' show how early the word was productive.
items.cn: 古英语 bān 意为骨头，bānhus「骨之屋，即身体」这类复合词显示它很早就很能产。

items.en: German Bein, Dutch been and Old Norse bein belong with bān to a reconstructed Germanic form *bainam; the modern German word also means 'leg'.
items.cn: 德语 Bein、荷兰语 been、古北欧语 bein 与 bān 同属重构的日耳曼语形式 *bainam；现代德语这个词还指腿。

items.en: The earlier Indo-European source of *bainam is not established; the root sometimes cited for it is a reconstruction, and competing suggestions exist.
items.cn: *bainam 更早的印欧来源未获证明；偶尔为其引用的词根属重构形式，且并存多种说法。

items.en: Latin os, plural ossa, means 'bone' but is not related to English bone; it survives in English only in learned borrowings such as ossify and osteoporosis.
items.cn: 拉丁 os（复数 ossa）意为「骨」，却与英语 bone 无关；它只保留在 ossify、osteoporosis 这类学术借词中。

items.en: Bone of contention, to the bone and have a bone to pick all date from uses of bone as something fought over, reached or gnawed.
items.cn: 「bone of contention」、「to the bone」与「have a bone to pick」都出自 bone 被争夺、被抵及或被啃咬的用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and some idioms): the pre-Germanic root is a reconstruction, and the origin of bone up is unknown, with several unproven suggestions in circulation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与部分习语）：日耳曼语之前的词根属重构形式，「bone up」的来源不明，流传的几种说法均未获证实。

note.en: Group one separates bone from look-alike and derived words; group two lists the body materials and structures people confuse with bone.
note.cn: 第一组把 bone 与形近词及派生词分开；第二组列出人们常与骨混淆的身体材料与结构。

entries.definition: Boon is an unrelated word meaning a benefit or favour, with a different vowel history.
entries.definitionCN: boon 是无关的词，意为恩惠或福气，元音历史不同。

entries.definition: Bony is the adjective from bone and describes what is made of bone or very thin.
entries.definitionCN: bony 是 bone 的形容词，描述由骨构成或极瘦。

entries.definition: Backbone is a compound meaning the spine or the main support of an organization.
entries.definitionCN: backbone 是复合词，指脊柱或组织的主要支柱。

entries.definition: Debone adds de- 'remove' to bone, giving a formal verb for taking bones out.
entries.definitionCN: debone 给 bone 加 de-「去除」，构成正式的去骨动词。

entries.definition: Skeleton is the whole frame, while a bone is one part of it.
entries.definitionCN: skeleton 指整副支架，bone 是其中的一部分。

entries.definition: Cartilage is the flexible tissue at joints and in sharks; it is not mineralised like bone.
entries.definitionCN: cartilage 是关节处与鲨鱼体内的柔性组织，不像骨那样矿化。

entries.definition: Marrow is the soft tissue inside a bone cavity, often confused with the bone itself.
entries.definitionCN: marrow 是骨腔内的软组织，常与骨头本身混淆。

entries.definition: Ivory is the dentine of tusks, a different material often carved like bone.
entries.definitionCN: ivory 是象牙的齿质，是另一种常像骨一样雕刻的材料。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English bān gives bone, and the plural is simply bones.
normal.cn: 古英语 bān 给出 bone，复数直接加 -s。

normal.en: The family runs bone, bony, boneless, backbone, debone and bone-dry.
normal.cn: 词族包括 bone、bony、boneless、backbone、debone 与 bone-dry。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: bone marrow, bone of contention, to the bone, funny bone.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：骨髓、争端所在、彻骨、肘部麻筋。

normal.en: Latin os is 'bone' but is not related to bone; it appears in ossify and osteoporosis.
normal.cn: 拉丁 os 意为骨，却与 bone 无关；它出现在 ossify 与 osteoporosis 中。

normal.en: The verb bone means both to remove bones and, in slang, to study hard.
normal.cn: 动词 bone 既指去骨，也作俚语指刻苦攻读。

abstract.en: Picture a house whose beams are the only thing left standing.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子，只剩梁柱还立着。

abstract.en: Picture a dog with one bone and two owners pulling at it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只狗、一根骨头，两个主人都在拽。

abstract.en: Picture a cold that starts in the wind and ends inside the marrow.
abstract.cn: 想象一种寒冷从风里开始，最后进到骨髓里。

examples.en: The X-ray showed a clean fracture in the bone above the wrist.
examples.cn: 影像显示腕上方有一处干净的骨折。

examples.en: Bone density falls quickly after the age of fifty in some people.
examples.cn: 有些人在五十岁之后骨密度下降得很快。

examples.en: The museum displays tools carved from bone and antler.
examples.cn: 博物馆展出用骨与鹿角制成的工具。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「bone（帮）」——在身体里「帮」着撑住全身的硬物 → 骨头

root: 古英语 bān「骨」；与德语 Bein、荷兰语 been、古北欧语 bein 同出重构的日耳曼语 *bainam（重构形式）。更早印欧来源不确定。拉丁 os「骨」属另一词族，与 bone 非同源。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses follow one hard organ from a single bone and its tissue, through the whole frame, remains, carved material, several idioms, a misnamed nerve, the verb of removing bones and the slang for hard study.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项随一件硬器官展开：从单根骨与其组织，到整副骨架、遗骸、骨材、几条习语、被误称的神经、去骨动词，以及刻苦攻读的俚语义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifting a whole spine out of a split fish, the bone clean and continuous.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从剖开的鱼身里抽出整条脊骨，骨头干净而连续。

branches.en: THE ORGAN AND THE TISSUE: one bone, and the living material it is made of.
branches.cn: 器官与组织：一根骨，以及构成它的活组织。

branches.en: THE FRAME AND THE DEAD: all bones together, and bones as what a person leaves.
branches.cn: 骨架与死者：全部骨头合起来，以及人留下的骨。

branches.en: MATERIAL CULTURE: bone carved, fired and sold as bone china.
branches.cn: 物质文化：骨被雕刻、烧制，并作为骨瓷出售。

branches.en: IDIOMS OF DEPTH AND DISPUTE: what is fought over, what is reached to the core, and the complaint one carries.
branches.cn: 深度与争端的习语：被争夺的东西、被抵及的核心，以及随身带着的怨气。

branches.en: THE VERB: remove the bone, or apply oneself to the bone.
branches.cn: 动词：去掉骨头，或专心用功到骨子里。

intro.en: Bone is a Germanic root; English builds bony, boneless, backbone and debone on it, while the Latin os family supplies the technical vocabulary separately.
intro.cn: bone 是日耳曼词根；英语在其上构成 bony、boneless、backbone、debone，拉丁 os 词族则另行提供技术词汇。

latinIntro.en: Old English bān yields bone, bony and boneless; Latin os, ossis 'bone' yields ossify, ossuary and osteoporosis but is not cognate with bone.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 bān 衍生 bone、bony、boneless；拉丁 os, ossis「骨」衍生 ossify、ossuary、osteoporosis，但与 bone 并非同源。

items.example: One bone was broken.
items.exampleCN: 一根骨头断了。

items.example: The bones were laid out in order.
items.exampleCN: 骨头被按顺序摆好。

items.example: The fish is bony and hard to eat.
items.exampleCN: 这种鱼刺多，难以下口。

items.example: Boneless fillets cook faster.
items.exampleCN: 无骨鱼柳熟得更快。

items.example: The backbone carries the body's weight.
items.exampleCN: 脊柱承担身体的重量。

items.example: They debone the fish before freezing.
items.exampleCN: 他们在冷冻前把鱼去骨。

items.example: The soil is bone-dry in August.
items.exampleCN: 八月土壤干透了。

items.example: Bone china is thin and translucent.
items.exampleCN: 骨瓷薄而半透明。

items.example: Bone marrow produces blood cells.
items.exampleCN: 骨髓制造血细胞。

latinEntries.meaning: a place for bones, an ossuary
